     1→---
     2→title: CI/CD Pipeline
     3→sidebar_label: CI/CD Pipeline
     4→sidebar_position: 8
     5→description: GitHub Actions pipeline stages, security gates, and scanning
     6→---
     7→
     8→# CI/CD Pipeline
     9→
    10→This document covers the GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline architecture, stages, and security gates.
    11→
    12→## Pipeline Architecture
    13→
    14→The platform uses a **two-repo CI/CD model**:
    15→
    16→- **Code repos** (konecta-ix-apps, konecta-ix-mcp-servers, konecta-ix-demos) run the **build pipeline** — lint, test, build, scan, sign, and push Docker images to Artifact Registry
    17→- **Workload repos** (konecta-ix-workloads) run the **deploy pipeline** — Terraform apply for infrastructure and secrets, with ArgoCD handling Helm-based deployments
    18→
    19→### Shared Workflows Repository
    20→
    21→```
    22→kix-platform-ci-workflows/
    23→└── .github/workflows/
    24→    ├── standard-pipeline.yaml      # Main orchestrator (code repos)
    25→    ├── _lint-and-test.yaml         # Language-aware lint + unit tests
    26→    ├── _secret-scan.yaml           # Trivy filesystem secret detection
    27→    ├── _sca.yaml                   # Dependency-Track SCA analysis
    28→    ├── _sast.yaml                  # SonarQube static analysis
    29→    ├── _build-image.yaml           # Docker build + BuildKit cache
    30→    ├── _container-scan-sign.yaml   # Trivy image scan + SBOM + Cosign
    31→    ├── _push-registry.yaml         # Push to Artifact Registry
    32→    ├── _promote.yaml               # Promote between environments
    33→    └── _dast.yaml                  # OWASP ZAP baseline scan
    34→```
    35→
    36→### Code Repo CI Workflow
    37→
    38→Every code repo uses this minimal workflow file to call the shared pipeline:
    39→
    40→```yaml
    41→# .github/workflows/ci.yaml
    42→name: CI
    43→on:
    44→  push:
    45→    branches: [develop, main]
    46→  pull_request:
    47→    branches: [main]
    48→  workflow_dispatch:
    49→
    50→permissions:
    51→  contents: read
    52→  id-token: write
    53→  security-events: write
    54→
    55→jobs:
    56→  pipeline:
    57→    uses: konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-ci-workflows/.github/workflows/standard-pipeline.yaml@v1
    58→    with:
    59→      service-name: ${{ github.event.repository.name }}
    60→      dockerfile-path: ./Dockerfile
    61→      python-version: "3.11"     # or node-version: "22"
    62→    secrets: inherit
    63→```
    64→
    65→:::note
    66→Code repos do **not** contain Helm charts or deployment configuration. The `chart-path` parameter is not used. All deployment data lives in the corresponding workload repo.
    67→:::
    68→
    69→### Workload Repo Deploy Workflow
    70→
    71→Each workload repo has a Terraform deploy workflow:
    72→
    73→```yaml
    74→# .github/workflows/deploy.yaml
    75→name: Deploy
    76→on:
    77→  workflow_dispatch:
    78→    inputs:
    79→      environment:
    80→        description: Target environment
    81→        required: true
    82→        type: choice
    83→        options: [dev, qa, prod]
    84→
    85→jobs:
    86→  terraform:
    87→    environment: ${{ inputs.environment }}
    88→    steps:
    89→      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
    90→      - uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
    91→        with:
    92→          workload_identity_provider: ${{ secrets.WIF_PROVIDER }}
    93→          service_account: ${{ secrets.WIF_SA }}
    94→      - run: |
    95→          cd terraform
    96→          terraform init
    97→          terraform plan \
    98→            -var="environment=${{ inputs.environment }}" \
    99→            -var="api_key=${{ secrets.TF_VARS_API_KEY }}"
   100→          terraform apply -auto-approve
   101→```
   102→
   103→## Pipeline Stages
   104→
   105→### Code Pipeline (Every PR and Merge)
   106→
   107→```
   108→┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐
   109→│  1. LINT &   │──│  2. SECRET   │──│  3. SCA      │──│  4. SAST     │──│  5. BUILD &  │
   110→│     TEST     │  │     SCAN     │  │              │  │              │  │  UNIT TEST   │
   111→└──────────────┘  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘
   112→  PR + merge        PR + merge        PR + merge        PR + merge        merge only
   113→  • ruff/eslint     • Trivy fs        • Syft SBOM       • SonarQube       • BuildKit
   114→  • type checks     • --scanners      • generation      • analysis        • multi-stage
   115→  • pip audit/        secret          • Dependency-     • quality gate:   • unit tests
   116→    npm audit       • stops on          Track upload     no critical/    • OCI labels
   117→                      any finding     • stops on           high issues
   118→                                        critical/high
   119→
   120→┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐
   121→│  6. CONTAINER│──│  7. PUSH &   │
   122→│  SCAN & SIGN │  │  REGISTRY    │
   123→└──────────────┘  └──────────────┘
   124→  merge only        merge only
   125→  • Trivy image     • Push to AR
   126→  • scan            • Tag: sha-xxx
   127→  • SBOM attach     • Tag: v1.2.3
   128→  • (Syft)            (on git tag)
   129→  • Cosign sign
   130→    (OIDC)
   131→```
   132→
   133→### When Stages Run
   134→
   135→| Stage | On PR | On Merge | Purpose |
   136→|-------|-------|----------|---------|
   137→| 1. Lint & Test | ✓ | ✓ | Fast feedback on code quality |
   138→| 2. Secret Scan | ✓ | ✓ | Block secrets before commit |
   139→| 3. SCA | ✓ | ✓ | Dependency vulnerability check |
   140→| 4. SAST | ✓ | ✓ | Static code analysis |
   141→| 5. Build & Test | ✗ | ✓ | Docker image build |
   142→| 6. Container Scan | ✗ | ✓ | Image vulnerability scan + sign |
   143→| 7. Push | ✗ | ✓ | Push to Artifact Registry |
   144→
   145→:::note
   146→Stage 8 (GitOps update) from the previous centralized model has been replaced. Image tag updates are now made directly in the workload repo's `values-{env}.yaml` file, either manually or via automation.
   147→:::
   148→
   149→## Security Gates
   150→
   151→All gates are **fail-stop** — pipeline halts immediately on critical/high findings.
   152→
   153→### Gate Details
   154→
   155→| Gate | Tool | Stage | Trigger | Action on Failure |
   156→|------|------|-------|---------|-------------------|
   157→| **Secret Detection** | Trivy (`--scanners secret`) | 2 | Every PR + merge | Stop pipeline, no exceptions |
   158→| **Dependency Vulnerabilities** | Dependency-Track (via Syft SBOM) | 3 | Every PR + merge | Stop on critical/high |
   159→| **SAST Quality Gate** | SonarQube | 4 | Every PR + merge | Stop on critical/high |
   160→| **Container Vulnerabilities** | Trivy (image scan) | 6 | Every merge | Stop on critical/high |
   161→| **Image Signature** | Cosign (Sigstore/OIDC) | 6 | Every merge | Unsigned images blocked |
   162→| **DAST Baseline** | OWASP ZAP | Post-deploy | Before prod promotion | Block promotion on findings |
   163→| **Admission Control** | Kyverno | Deploy-time | Every sync | Reject unsigned images |
   164→
   165→### Tool Configuration
   166→
   167→#### Trivy Secret Scan
   168→
   169→Scans source filesystem before any build:
   170→
   171→```yaml
   172→- name: Secret Scan
   173→  run: |
   174→    trivy fs --scanners secret --exit-code 1 .
   175→```
   176→
   177→Zero tolerance — any finding stops the pipeline.
   178→
   179→#### SonarQube
   180→
   181→Hosted in `shared-devsecops` namespace:
   182→
   183→- Runs static analysis on every PR
   184→- Quality gate: no new critical or high severity issues
   185→- Results posted as PR comment
   186→
   187→#### Dependency-Track
   188→
   189→SBOM-based vulnerability tracking:
   190→
   191→- Syft generates CycloneDX SBOMs
   192→- Uploaded to Dependency-Track for continuous monitoring
   193→- Pipeline stops on critical/high vulnerabilities
   194→
   195→#### Cosign Image Signing
   196→
   197→Keyless signing via GitHub OIDC → Sigstore:
   198→
   199→```yaml
   200→- name: Sign Image
   201→  run: |
   202→    cosign sign --yes $IMAGE_REF
   203→```
   204→
   205→No long-lived keys — fully automatic.
   206→
   207→### Vulnerability Remediation SLAs
   208→
   209→Per the Konecta DevSecOps Handbook:
   210→
   211→| Severity | Detection → Triage | Triage → Fix | Fix → Deploy |
   212→|----------|-------------------|--------------|--------------|
   213→| Critical | 4 hours | 24 hours | 48 hours |
   214→| High | 24 hours | 7 days | 14 days |
   215→| Medium | 7 days | 30 days | 45 days |
   216→| Low | 30 days | 90 days | Next release |
   217→
   218→## Image Tagging Strategy
   219→
   220→| Tag | When | Purpose |
   221→|-----|------|---------|
   222→| `sha-{7-char}` | Every build | Immutable build identifier |
   223→| `v{major}.{minor}.{patch}` | On git tag | Release version |
   224→| `{env}-latest`| On promotion | Environment pointer (mutable) |
   225→
   226→**Rule**: SHA tags are immutable. Never overwrite. Promotion copies the SHA tag reference, not the image.
   227→
   228→## Secrets Management (CI)
   229→
   230→### GitHub OIDC → GCP Workload Identity
   231→
   232→No JSON keys — fully automated authentication:
   233→
   234→```yaml
   235→- name: Authenticate to GCP
   236→  uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
   237→  with:
   238→    workload_identity_provider: ${{ secrets.WIF_PROVIDER }}
   239→    service_account: ${{ secrets.WIF_SA }}
   240→```
   241→
   242→| Property | Value |
   243→|----------|-------|
   244→| Token lifetime | ~1 hour |
   245→| Auto-refreshing | Yes |
   246→| Audit trail | Full via Cloud Audit Logs |
   247→
   248→### Build Secrets
   249→
   250→For build-time secrets (never in image layers):
   251→
   252→```dockerfile
   253→RUN --mount=type=secret,id=npm_token \
   254→    NPM_TOKEN=$(cat /run/secrets/npm_token) npm ci
   255→```
   256→
   257→```yaml
   258→- name: Build
   259→  run: |
   260→    docker build --secret id=npm_token,src=${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }} .
   261→```
   262→
   263→### Workload Repo Secrets (TF_VARS_)
   264→
   265→Static secrets for deployed services are stored as GitHub Actions secrets on the **workload repo**, prefixed with `TF_VARS_`. These are passed to Terraform which creates Kubernetes secrets and GCP Secret Manager entries. See [Target Architecture — Secrets Management](target-architecture#secrets-management-in-workload-repos) for details.
   266→
   267→## Example Pipeline Run
   268→
   269→```
   270→1. Developer pushes to feature branch in code repo
   271→2. PR opened to develop or main
   272→3. Pipeline runs stages 1-4 (lint, secret scan, SCA, SAST)
   273→4. PR review and approval
   274→5. Merge to develop (for dev) or main (for qa)
   275→6. Pipeline runs all stages 1-7
   276→7. Image built, scanned, signed, pushed to Artifact Registry
   277→8. Developer updates image tag in workload repo `values-{env}.yaml`
   278→9. ArgoCD detects change and syncs to target namespace
   279→10. Service deployed and running
   280→```
   281→
   282→## Required Repository Configuration
   283→
   284→### Code Repo — Variables (Settings → Actions → Variables)
   285→
   286→| Variable | Example |
   287→|----------|---------|
   288→| `VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` | `805102662749-...` (for Node.js builds) |
   289→
   290→### Code Repo — Secrets (Inherited from Org)
   291→
   292→| Secret | Description |
   293→|--------|-------------|
   294→| `GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER` | Workload Identity pool provider |
   295→| `GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` | Service account for CI |
   296→
   297→### Workload Repo — Secrets (Per GitHub Environment)
   298→
   299→| Secret | Description |
   300→|--------|-------------|
   301→| `GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER` | Workload Identity pool provider |
   302→| `GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` | Service account for Terraform |
   303→| `TF_VARS_*` | Per-environment static secrets for Terraform |
   304→
   305→### Branch → Environment Mapping
   306→
   307→| Branch | Environment | Namespace |
   308→|--------|-------------|-----------|
   309→| `develop` | dev | `dev-api-services` |
   310→| `main` | qa | `qa-api-services` |
   311→| `v*` tags | prod | `prod-api-services` |
   312→
   313→---
   314→
   315→**Next**: [GitOps & Promotion](gitops-promotion) — ArgoCD GitOps flow and environment promotion.
   316→
```

     1→---
     2→title: Docker Security
     3→sidebar_label: Docker Security
     4→sidebar_position: 7
     5→description: Secure multi-stage Docker builds, base images, and container hardening
     6→---
     7→
     8→# Docker Security
     9→
    10→This document covers secure Docker build practices including multi-stage builds, base image policy, hardening, and dependency management.
    11→
    12→## Base Image Policy
    13→
    14→### Approved Base Images
    15→
    16→| Stack | Builder Stage | Runtime Stage |
    17→|-------|---------------|---------------|
    18→| **Python (standard)** | `python:3.x-slim` | `python:3.x-slim` |
    19→| **Python (ML)** | `python:3.x-slim` + apt deps | `python:3.x-slim` + runtime-only libs |
    20→| **Node.js** | `node:20-alpine` | `gcr.io/distroless/nodejs20-debian12` |
    21→
    22→### Image Pinning Requirements
    23→
    24→- **Pin to full digest** in CI (updated monthly by Renovate)
    25→- Parameterise Python version via `ARG PYTHON_VERSION=3.11`
    26→- **Never use `:latest`** — blocked by Kyverno admission control
    27→
    28→### Example Pinned Image
    29→
    30→```dockerfile
    31→# Pin to specific digest — update monthly via Renovate
    32→FROM node:22-alpine@sha256:abc123def456... AS dependencies
    33→```
    34→
    35→To get the current digest:
    36→
    37→```bash
    38→docker pull node:22-alpine
    39→docker inspect --format='{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' node:22-alpine
    40→```
    41→
    42→## Multi-Stage Build Patterns
    43→
    44→### Python Services
    45→
    46→```dockerfile
    47→# Stage 1: Builder
    48→FROM python:3.11-slim@sha256:... AS builder
    49→
    50→WORKDIR /app
    51→
    52→# Install build dependencies
    53→RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    54→    build-essential \
    55→    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
    56→
    57→# Install Python dependencies
    58→COPY requirements.txt .
    59→RUN pip install --prefix=/install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
    60→
    61→# Stage 2: Runtime
    62→FROM python:3.11-slim@sha256:... AS runtime
    63→
    64→WORKDIR /app
    65→
    66→# Copy only installed packages
    67→COPY --from=builder /install /usr/local
    68→
    69→# Copy application code
    70→COPY src/ ./src/
    71→
    72→# Non-root user
    73→RUN useradd -m -u 65532 appuser
    74→USER appuser
    75→
    76→EXPOSE 8080
    77→ENTRYPOINT ["python", "-m", "uvicorn", "src.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8080"]
    78→```
    79→
    80→### Node.js Services
    81→
    82→```dockerfile
    83→# Stage 1: Dependencies
    84→FROM node:22-alpine@sha256:... AS deps
    85→WORKDIR /app
    86→COPY package*.json ./
    87→RUN npm ci --only=production
    88→
    89→# Stage 2: Builder
    90→FROM node:22-alpine@sha256:... AS builder
    91→WORKDIR /app
    92→COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
    93→COPY . .
    94→RUN npm run build
    95→RUN npm prune --omit=dev
    96→
    97→# Stage 3: Runtime (distroless)
    98→FROM gcr.io/distroless/nodejs20-debian12 AS runtime
    99→WORKDIR /app
   100→
   101→COPY --from=builder /app/.output ./.output
   102→COPY --from=builder /app/node_modules ./node_modules
   103→
   104→USER 65532
   105→
   106→EXPOSE 3000
   107→ENTRYPOINT ["node", ".output/server/index.mjs"]
   108→```
   109→
   110→## Security Hardening
   111→
   112→### Non-Root User
   113→
   114→All containers run as non-root (UID 65532):
   115→
   116→```dockerfile
   117→# Create non-root user
   118→RUN useradd -m -u 65532 appuser
   119→
   120→# Switch to non-root user
   121→USER appuser
   122→```
   123→
   124→Enforced by Pod Security Context:
   125→
   126→```yaml
   127→podSecurityContext:
   128→  runAsNonRoot: true
   129→  runAsUser: 65532
   130→  fsGroup: 65532
   131→```
   132→
   133→### Read-Only Root Filesystem
   134→
   135→Enable read-only filesystem with explicit writable paths:
   136→
   137→```yaml
   138→containerSecurityContext:
   139→  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
   140→
   141→volumeMounts:
   142→  - name: tmp
   143→    mountPath: /tmp
   144→  - name: cache
   145→    mountPath: /app/.cache
   146→
   147→volumes:
   148→  - name: tmp
   149→    emptyDir:
   150→      sizeLimit: 100Mi
   151→  - name: cache
   152→    emptyDir:
   153→      sizeLimit: 500Mi
   154→```
   155→
   156→### Capability Dropping
   157→
   158→Drop all capabilities:
   159→
   160→```yaml
   161→containerSecurityContext:
   162→  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
   163→  capabilities:
   164→    drop: [ALL]
   165→  seccompProfile:
   166→    type: RuntimeDefault
   167→```
   168→
   169→### No Shell in Production
   170→
   171→Node.js distroless images have no shell:
   172→
   173→- Cannot `exec` into container
   174→- Reduces attack surface
   175→- Debugging via logs and metrics only
   176→
   177→### No Secrets in Images
   178→
   179→- **No `.env` files** baked into images
   180→- All configuration via K8s ConfigMaps and Secrets
   181→- Build secrets via `docker build --secret` (never in layers)
   182→
   183→### Python Hardening
   184→
   185→```dockerfile
   186→ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
   187→ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
   188→```
   189→
   190→## Dependency Management
   191→
   192→### Python
   193→
   194→Use `pip-compile` or `uv lock` for pinned requirements with hashes:
   195→
   196→```bash
   197→# Generate requirements with hashes
   198→pip-compile --generate-hashes requirements.in -o requirements.txt
   199→```
   200→
   201→Example `requirements.txt`:
   202→
   203→```
   204→fastapi==0.109.0 \
   205→    --hash=sha256:abc123... \
   206→    --hash=sha256:def456...
   207→uvicorn[standard]==0.27.0 \
   208→    --hash=sha256:789abc...
   209→```
   210→
   211→### Node.js
   212→
   213→**Always use `npm ci`** (never `npm install` in CI):
   214→
   215→```dockerfile
   216→COPY package*.json ./
   217→RUN npm ci --only=production
   218→```
   219→
   220→### Automated Updates
   221→
   222→- **Renovate** for automated dependency PRs
   223→- Weekly security update PRs
   224→- Digest updates monthly
   225→
   226→## Build Metadata (OCI Labels)
   227→
   228→All images include OCI annotations (final stage only):
   229→
   230→```dockerfile
   231→LABEL org.opencontainers.image.created="${BUILD_DATE}"
   232→LABEL org.opencontainers.image.revision="${GIT_SHA}"
   233→LABEL org.opencontainers.image.version="${VERSION}"
   234→LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/..."
   235→LABEL org.opencontainers.image.title="kix-mcp-gateway"
   236→LABEL org.opencontainers.image.vendor="Konecta"
   237→```
   238→
   239→Added via build args:
   240→
   241→```bash
   242→docker build \
   243→  --build-arg BUILD_DATE=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ") \
   244→  --build-arg GIT_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD) \
   245→  --build-arg VERSION=$(cat version.txt) \
   246→  .
   247→```
   248→
   249→## Image Size Targets
   250→
   251→| Category | Target Size | Optimisation |
   252→|----------|-------------|--------------|
   253→| **Python standard** | < 200 MB | Multi-stage, no cache, strip pyc |
   254→| **Python ML/heavy** | < 500 MB | opencv-headless, models as external volumes |
   255→| **Node.js (Nuxt)** | < 80 MB | Distroless runtime, npm prune |
   256→
   257→### Size Reduction Tips
   258→
   259→1. Use slim/alpine base images
   260→2. Multi-stage builds (builder separate from runtime)
   261→3. Remove apt cache: `rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*`
   262→4. No pip cache: `pip install --no-cache-dir`
   263→5. Prune dev dependencies: `npm prune --omit=dev`
   264→6. Use `.dockerignore` to exclude test files, docs
   265→
   266→## Dockerfile Checklist
   267→
   268→Use this checklist when creating or reviewing Dockerfiles:
   269→
   270→```markdown
   271→## Dockerfile Security Checklist
   272→
   273→### Base Image
   274→- [ ] Pinned to digest (not mutable tag)
   275→- [ ] Using approved base image (slim/alpine/distroless)
   276→- [ ] No `:latest` tag
   277→
   278→### Multi-Stage Build
   279→- [ ] Builder stage separate from runtime
   280→- [ ] Only production dependencies in final image
   281→- [ ] No build tools in final image
   282→
   283→### Security Hardening
   284→- [ ] Non-root user (UID 65532)
   285→- [ ] USER directive before ENTRYPOINT
   286→- [ ] No HEALTHCHECK (K8s probes instead)
   287→- [ ] No .env files or secrets
   288→
   289→### Dependencies
   290→- [ ] Package versions pinned
   291→- [ ] Using npm ci (not npm install)
   292→- [ ] Requirements with hashes (Python)
   293→
   294→### Metadata
   295→- [ ] OCI labels present
   296→- [ ] Version and commit SHA included
   297→```
   298→
   299→## Example: Complete Python Dockerfile
   300→
   301→```dockerfile
   302→# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
   303→
   304→ARG PYTHON_VERSION=3.11
   305→
   306→# Stage 1: Builder
   307→FROM python:${PYTHON_VERSION}-slim@sha256:... AS builder
   308→
   309→WORKDIR /app
   310→
   311→RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
   312→    build-essential \
   313→    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
   314→
   315→COPY requirements.txt .
   316→RUN pip install --prefix=/install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
   317→
   318→# Stage 2: Runtime
   319→FROM python:${PYTHON_VERSION}-slim@sha256:... AS runtime
   320→
   321→ARG BUILD_DATE
   322→ARG GIT_SHA
   323→ARG VERSION
   324→
   325→LABEL org.opencontainers.image.created="${BUILD_DATE}"
   326→LABEL org.opencontainers.image.revision="${GIT_SHA}"
   327→LABEL org.opencontainers.image.version="${VERSION}"
   328→LABEL org.opencontainers.image.vendor="Konecta"
   329→
   330→WORKDIR /app
   331→
   332→ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
   333→ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
   334→
   335→COPY --from=builder /install /usr/local
   336→COPY src/ ./src/
   337→
   338→RUN useradd -m -u 65532 appuser && \
   339→    chown -R appuser:appuser /app
   340→
   341→USER appuser
   342→
   343→EXPOSE 8080
   344→
   345→ENTRYPOINT ["python", "-m", "uvicorn", "src.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8080"]
   346→```
   347→
   348→---
   349→
   350→**Next**: [CI/CD Pipeline](cicd-pipeline) — GitHub Actions pipeline and security gates.
   351→
```

     8→# Target Architecture
     9→
    10→This document describes the target state architecture on kix-infrastructure.
    11→
    12→## High-Level Architecture
    13→
    14→```
    15→┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

    59→```
    60→
    61→## Dual Ingress Architecture
    62→
    63→Two separate ingress paths with independent load balancers:
    64→
    65→| Path | Flow | Purpose |
    66→|------|------|---------|
    67→| **API** | Internet → GCP LB + Cloud Armor → Kong Ingress → `{env}-api-services` / `{env}-mcp-servers` | Machine-to-machine, API consumers |
    68→| **Frontend** | Internet → GCP LB + Cloud Armor + GKE Gateway API + IAP → `{env}-web-apps` | Browser users, human authentication |
    69→
    70→## Repository Model
    71→
    72→Services follow a **two-repo pattern**: application source code and deployment hosting data are kept in separate repositories across different GitHub organisations.
    73→
    74→### Organisation Structure
    75→
    76→```
    77→GitHub Enterprise: Konecta Digital
    78→│
    79→├── CODE REPOSITORIES (source code + CI only)
    80→│   │
    81→│   ├── Org: konecta-ix-apps (Business Applications)
    82→│   │   ├── kix-app-iqportal              # IQ Portal source code
    83→│   │   ├── kix-app-hrfraud               # HR Fraud source code
    84→│   │   ├── kix-app-hrportal              # HR Portal source code
    85→│   │   └── kix-app-*                     # One repo per application
    86→│   │
    87→│   ├── Org: konecta-ix-mcp-servers (MCP Integration Team)
    88→│   │   ├── kix-mcp-gateway               # MCP Gateway source code
    89→│   │   ├── kix-mcp-ragengine             # RAG Engine source code
    90→│   │   └── kix-mcp-*                     # One repo per MCP server (~14 repos)
    91→│   │
    92→│   └── Org: konecta-ix-demos (Demo Team)
    93→│       └── kix-demo-*                    # Demo/prototype source code
    94→│
    95→├── WORKLOAD REPOSITORIES (hosting data — Helm, ArgoCD, Terraform)
    96→│   │
    97→│   └── Org: konecta-ix-workloads (Deployment & Operations)
    98→│       ├── kix-workload-iqportal         # IQ Portal hosting data
    99→│       ├── kix-workload-hrfraud          # HR Fraud hosting data
   100→│       ├── kix-workload-mcp-gateway      # MCP Gateway hosting data
   101→│       ├── kix-workload-mcp-ragengine    # RAG Engine hosting data
   102→│       └── kix-workload-*                # One per deployed service
   103→│
   104→├── PLATFORM REPOSITORIES (shared tooling)
   105→│   │
   106→│   └── Org: konecta-ix-platform (Platform Engineering)
   107→│       ├── kix-platform-infrastructure   # GCP infra, GKE clusters, platform ArgoCD
   108→│       ├── kix-platform-modules          # Shared Terraform modules + Helm base chart
   109→│       ├── kix-platform-ci-workflows     # Shared reusable GitHub Actions workflows
   110→│       ├── kix-platform-service-template # Template repos for bootstrapping
   111→│       ├── kix-platform-backstage        # Backstage config, plugins, catalog
   112→│       └── kix-platform-docs             # Documentation (TechDocs)
   113→│
   114→└── Org: konecta-ix-services (Platform Services)
   115→    ├── kix-services-kong
   116→    ├── kix-services-litellm
   117→    ├── kix-services-monitoring
   118→    └── kix-services-backstage
   119→```
   120→
   121→### Code Repository Structure
   122→
   123→Each code repository contains **only application source code** and a CI pipeline that builds and publishes a Docker container:
   124→
   125→```
   126→konecta-ix-apps/kix-app-iqportal/
   127→├── src/                          # Application source code
   128→├── Dockerfile                    # Multi-stage Docker build
   129→├── catalog-info.yaml             # Backstage service catalog descriptor
   130→├── docs/                         # TechDocs content (Backstage)
   131→│   └── index.md
   132→├── .github/workflows/
   133→│   └── ci.yaml                   # Build + push pipeline (develop & main)
   134→├── CODEOWNERS
   135→├── .dockerignore
   136→└── .env.example
   137→```
   138→
   139→**CI pipeline** triggers automatically on `develop` and `main` branches:
   140→- Calls reusable workflows from `kix-platform-ci-workflows`
   141→- Builds a Docker container and pushes to GCP Artifact Registry
   142→- Tags images with `sha-{7-char}` (immutable) and `v{semver}` (on git tags)
   143→
   144→### Workload Repository Structure
   145→
   146→Each workload repository contains **all deployment and infrastructure data** for a single service:
   147→
   148→```
   149→konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-iqportal/
   150→├── helm/                         # Helm chart
   151→│   ├── Chart.yaml                # Depends on base-service-chart (OCI)
   152→│   ├── values.yaml               # Service defaults
   153→│   ├── values-dev.yaml           # Dev environment overrides
   154→│   ├── values-qa.yaml            # QA environment overrides
   155→│   ├── values-prod.yaml          # Prod environment overrides
   156→│   └── templates/                # Only if custom K8s resources needed
   157→├── argocd/
   158→│   └── application.yaml          # ArgoCD Application manifest
   159→├── terraform/                    # Service infrastructure (per-env)
   160→│   ├── main.tf                   # Service account, IAM, secrets, DB
   161→│   ├── variables.tf              # Input variables (incl. TF_VARS_ secrets)
   162→│   ├── outputs.tf
   163→│   └── backend.tf                # Remote state in GCS
   164→├── catalog-info.yaml             # Backstage service catalog descriptor
   165→├── .github/workflows/
   166→│   └── deploy.yaml               # Terraform validate-plan-apply workflow
   167→└── CODEOWNERS
   168→```
   169→
   170→**ArgoCD** watches each workload repo directly and syncs Helm releases from the `helm/` directory.
   171→
   172→**Terraform** manages per-service GCP resources (service accounts, IAM, secrets, databases) and is applied via GitHub Actions.
   173→
   174→### Secrets Management in Workload Repos
   175→
   176→Secrets follow a **Terraform-first approach** with two patterns:
   177→
   178→#### Auto-Generated Secrets
   179→
   180→Secrets that can be generated (database passwords, API keys) are created by Terraform:
   181→
   182→```hcl
   183→resource "random_password" "db" {
   184→  length  = 32
   185→  special = true
   186→}
   187→
   188→resource "google_secret_manager_secret_version" "db_password" {
   189→  secret=[REDACTED].db_password.id
   190→  secret_data = random_password.db.result
   191→}
   192→
   193→resource "kubernetes_secret" "app_secrets" {
   194→  metadata {
   195→    name      = "kix-app-iqportal-secrets"
   196→    namespace = var.namespace
   197→  }
   198→  data = {
   199→    DB_PASSWORD = random_password.db.result
   200→  }
   201→}
   202→```
   203→
   204→#### Static Secrets (via GitHub Actions)
   205→
   206→Secrets that must be provided externally (third-party API keys, OAuth credentials) are stored as **GitHub Actions secrets** on the workload repo, prefixed with `TF_VARS_`:
   207→
   208→| GitHub Secret | Terraform Variable | Description |
   209→|---------------|-------------------|-------------|
   210→| `TF_VARS_API_KEY` | `var.api_key` | Third-party API key |
   211→| `TF_VARS_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` | `var.oauth_client_secret` | OAuth credential |
   212→| `TF_VARS_CHANNELHUB_CLIENT_ID` | `var.channelhub_client_id` | External service credential |
   213→
   214→Per-environment secrets are defined using **GitHub Environments** (dev, qa, prod) on the workload repo. The Terraform workflow passes these as `-var` flags:
   215→
   216→```yaml
   217→# .github/workflows/deploy.yaml (simplified)
   218→jobs:
   219→  terraform:
   220→    environment: ${{ inputs.environment }}
   221→    steps:
   222→      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
   223→      - run: |
   224→          terraform plan \
   225→            -var="api_key=${{ secrets.TF_VARS_API_KEY }}" \
   226→            -var="namespace=${{ vars.NAMESPACE }}"
   227→```
   228→
   229→Terraform then creates Kubernetes secrets from both auto-generated and static values:
   230→
   231→```hcl
   232→variable "api_key" {
   233→  type      = string
   234→  sensitive = true
   235→}
   236→
   237→resource "kubernetes_secret" "app_secrets" {
   238→  metadata {
   239→    name      = "kix-app-iqportal-secrets"
   240→    namespace = var.namespace
   241→  }
   242→  data = {
   243→    API_KEY     = var.api_key                # Static — from TF_VARS_
   244→    DB_PASSWORD = random_password.db.result   # Auto-generated
   245→  }
   246→}
   247→```
   248→
   249→## CI/CD Flow
   250→
   251→```
   252→CODE REPO (konecta-ix-apps or konecta-ix-mcp-servers)
   253→─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   254→Developer Push → Code Repo (any code org)
   255→  (e.g. konecta-ix-apps/kix-app-iqportal)
   256→       │
   257→       ▼  CI triggers on develop / main branches
   258→       Calls reusable workflows from:
   259→       konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-ci-workflows@v1
   260→       ├── Lint + Unit Tests
   261→       ├── Secret Scan (Trivy)
   262→       ├── SCA (Dependency-Track)
   263→       ├── SAST (SonarQube)
   264→       ├── Docker Build (BuildKit, multi-stage)
   265→       ├── Container Scan + SBOM (Trivy + Syft)
   266→       ├── Push to Artifact Registry
   267→       └── Cosign Sign (OIDC keyless)
   268→
   269→WORKLOAD REPO (konecta-ix-workloads)
   270→─────────────────────────────────────
   271→  kix-workload-iqportal
   272→       │
   273→       ├── Terraform (via GitHub Actions deploy.yaml)
   274→       │   ├── Creates GCP service accounts + IAM
   275→       │   ├── Creates secrets (auto-generated + TF_VARS_)
   276→       │   └── Creates K8s secrets in target namespace
   277→       │
   278→       ├── ArgoCD watches this repo directly
   279→       │   ├── Detects changes to helm/ or argocd/
   280→       │   └── Syncs Helm release to target namespace
   281→       │
   282→       └── Image tag update (manual or automated)
   283→           ├── Update values-{env}.yaml with new image tag
   284→           ├── Dev: auto-sync on commit
   285→           ├── QA: manual sync (08:00-18:00 UTC)
   286→           └── Prod: manual sync (Tue-Thu 20:00-23:00 UTC)
   287→```
   288→
   289→### Branch → Environment Mapping
   290→
   291→| Branch / Trigger | Environment | Auto-Sync |
   292→|------------------|-------------|-----------|
   293→| `develop` (code repo) | dev | Yes |
   294→| `main` (code repo) | qa | Yes |
   295→| `v*` tags (code repo) | prod | Manual |
   296→
   297→## Key Design Decisions
   298→
   299→| Decision | Rationale |
   300→|----------|-----------|
   301→| **Code/hosting separation** | Clear ownership boundaries, independent release cycles, security isolation between source code and deployment config |
   302→| **Per-workload GitOps** | Each team owns their deployment, no bottleneck on a centralized repo, self-service infrastructure |
   303→| **Repo-per-service** | Team autonomy, clear ownership, independent release cycles |
   304→| **Terraform-managed secrets** | Secrets are version-controlled (encrypted), auditable, auto-generated where possible, no manual Secret Manager operations |
   305→| **TF_VARS\_ prefix convention** | Clear separation of Terraform variables from other GitHub secrets, per-environment via GitHub Environments |
   306→| **Shared base Helm chart** | Consistency, reduced maintenance, enforced standards |
   307→| **Cross-org workflow sharing** | DRY principle, single place to update pipeline logic |
   308→| **Dual ingress** | Different auth models for APIs vs. frontends |
   309→| **No service mesh (initially)** | Reduce complexity during migration; revisit post-migration |
   310→
   311→## Key Differences from Cloud Run
   312→
   313→| Aspect | Cloud Run | kix-infrastructure |
   314→|--------|-----------|-------------------|
   315→| **DB connection** | Unix socket via VPC connector | Cloud SQL Auth Proxy sidecar (TCP) |
   316→| **Secrets** | Secret Manager direct access | Terraform-managed K8s Secrets (auto-generated + TF_VARS_) |
   317→| **Scaling** | 0-10 instances (cold starts) | HPA 1-5+ replicas (always warm) |
   318→| **Ingress** | Direct HTTPS | Dual: Kong (API) + Gateway API + IAP (frontend) |
   319→| **CI/CD** | Cloud Build + Bitbucket | GitHub Actions + ArgoCD |
   320→| **Health checks** | Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK | K8s liveness/readiness probes |
   321→| **Observability** | Fragmented | Unified Prometheus/Grafana/Jaeger |
   322→| **Deployment config** | Terraform in same repo | Separate workload repo (Helm + ArgoCD + Terraform) |
   323→
   324→---
   325→
   326→**Next**: [Migration Phases](migration-phases) — Phased approach to migration.
   327→
```

Now I have a clear picture of the pipeline architecture. Let me draft the `standard-pipeline.yaml` based on the specs in the CI/CD docs, target architecture, and Docker security docs.

Here's the draft:

```yaml
# standard-pipeline.yaml — Main CI orchestrator for code repositories
#
# Called by consumer repos via:
#   uses: konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-ci-workflows/.github/workflows/standard-pipeline.yaml@v1
#
# Stages 1-4 run on PRs and merges (fast feedback).
# Stages 5-7 run on merges only (build, scan, push).

name: Standard CI Pipeline

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      service-name:
        description: "Service name (typically the repository name)"
        required: true
        type: string
      dockerfile-path:
        description: "Path to Dockerfile"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: "./Dockerfile"
      python-version:
        description: "Python version for Python services (leave empty for Node.js)"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
      node-version:
        description: "Node.js version for Node services (leave empty for Python)"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
      build-args:
        description: "Additional Docker build arguments (newline-separated)"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
      build-secrets:
        description: "Docker build secret mount IDs (newline-separated)"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""

    outputs:
      image-ref:
        description: "Full image reference with digest (only set on merge)"
        value: ${{ jobs.push-registry.outputs.image-ref }}
      image-tag:
        description: "Short image tag (sha-xxxxxxx)"
        value: ${{ jobs.determine-metadata.outputs.sha-tag }}

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write
  security-events: write
  pull-requests: write

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Shared environment variables
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
env:
  REGISTRY: europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev
  IMAGE_REPO: europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev/kd-ix-shared-artifacts/kix-containers

jobs:
  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Metadata — resolve tags, environment, and build context
  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  determine-metadata:
    name: Resolve build metadata
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      sha-tag: sha-${{ steps.meta.outputs.sha7 }}
      semver-tag: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.semver-tag }}
      environment: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.environment }}
      is-merge: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.is-merge }}
      is-tag: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.is-tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Compute metadata
        id: meta
        run: |
          SHA7="${GITHUB_SHA::7}"
          echo "sha7=${SHA7}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          # Determine if this is a merge (push) or a PR
          IS_MERGE="false"
          IS_TAG="false"
          SEMVER_TAG=""
          ENVIRONMENT=""

          if [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" == "push" ]]; then
            IS_MERGE="true"

            if [[ "${{ github.ref }}" == refs/tags/v* ]]; then
              IS_TAG="true"
              SEMVER_TAG="${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}"
              ENVIRONMENT="prod"
            elif [[ "${{ github.ref }}" == "refs/heads/main" ]]; then
              ENVIRONMENT="qa"
            elif [[ "${{ github.ref }}" == "refs/heads/develop" ]]; then
              ENVIRONMENT="dev"
            fi
          fi

          echo "is-merge=${IS_MERGE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "is-tag=${IS_TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "semver-tag=${SEMVER_TAG}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "environment=${ENVIRONMENT}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Stage 1 — Lint & Test (PR + merge)
  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  lint-and-test:
    name: "1. Lint & Test"
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_lint-and-test.yaml
    with:
      python-version: ${{ inputs.python-version }}
      node-version: ${{ inputs.node-version }}

  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Stage 2 — Secret Scan (PR + merge)
  # Trivy filesystem scan — zero tolerance, any finding stops pipeline
  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  secret-scan:
    name: "2. Secret Scan"
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_secret-scan.yaml

  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Stage 3 — SCA / Dependency Analysis (PR + merge)
  # Syft SBOM generation → Dependency-Track upload
  # Stops on critical/high vulnerabilities
  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  sca:
    name: "3. SCA"
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_sca.yaml
    with:
      service-name: ${{ inputs.service-name }}
    secrets: inherit

  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Stage 4 — SAST / Static Analysis (PR + merge)
  # SonarQube analysis — stops on critical/high issues
  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  sast:
    name: "4. SAST"
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_sast.yaml
    with:
      service-name: ${{ inputs.service-name }}
    secrets: inherit

  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Stage 5 — Build Image (merge only)
  # Multi-stage Docker build via BuildKit with OCI labels
  # Pushes to Artifact Registry with sha-xxxxxxx tag
  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  build-image:
    name: "5. Build Image"
    needs: [determine-metadata, lint-and-test, secret-scan, sca, sast]
    if: needs.determine-metadata.outputs.is-merge == 'true'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_build-image.yaml
    with:
      service-name: ${{ inputs.service-name }}
      dockerfile-path: ${{ inputs.dockerfile-path }}
      image-repo: europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev/kd-ix-shared-artifacts/kix-containers
      image-tag: sha-${{ needs.determine-metadata.outputs.sha-tag }}
      python-version: ${{ inputs.python-version }}
      node-version: ${{ inputs.node-version }}
      build-args: ${{ inputs.build-args }}
      build-secrets: ${{ inputs.build-secrets }}
    secrets: inherit

  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Stage 6 — Container Scan & Sign (merge only)
  # Trivy image scan + Syft SBOM attachment + Cosign keyless signing
  # Stops on critical/high vulnerabilities
  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  container-scan-sign:
    name: "6. Container Scan & Sign"
    needs: [build-image]
    if: needs.determine-metadata.outputs.is-merge == 'true'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_container-scan-sign.yaml
    with:
      image-ref: ${{ needs.build-image.outputs.image-ref }}
      service-name: ${{ inputs.service-name }}
    secrets: inherit

  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Stage 7 — Push & Tag (merge only)
  # Apply additional tags: semver on git tags, env-latest on promotion
  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  push-registry:
    name: "7. Push to Registry"
    needs: [determine-metadata, build-image, container-scan-sign]
    if: needs.determine-metadata.outputs.is-merge == 'true'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/_push-registry.yaml
    with:
      image-ref: ${{ needs.build-image.outputs.image-ref }}
      service-name: ${{ inputs.service-name }}
      semver-tag: ${{ needs.determine-metadata.outputs.semver-tag }}
      environment: ${{ needs.determine-metadata.outputs.environment }}
    secrets: inherit

  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Pipeline Summary
  # ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  summary:
    name: Pipeline Summary
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: always()
    needs: [determine-metadata, lint-and-test, secret-scan, sca, sast, build-image, container-scan-sign, push-registry]
    steps:
      - name: Pipeline result
        run: |
          echo "## Pipeline Summary" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| Stage | Status |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "|-------|--------|" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| 1. Lint & Test | ${{ needs.lint-and-test.result }} |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| 2. Secret Scan | ${{ needs.secret-scan.result }} |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| 3. SCA | ${{ needs.sca.result }} |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| 4. SAST | ${{ needs.sast.result }} |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| 5. Build Image | ${{ needs.build-image.result }} |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| 6. Container Scan & Sign | ${{ needs.container-scan-sign.result }} |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo "| 7. Push to Registry | ${{ needs.push-registry.result }} |" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

          if [[ "${{ needs.determine-metadata.outputs.is-merge }}" == "true" ]]; then
            echo "" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "**Image:** \`${{ needs.push-registry.outputs.image-ref }}\`" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "**Environment:** \`${{ needs.determine-metadata.outputs.environment }}\`" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

      - name: Fail if any stage failed
        if: contains(needs.*.result, 'failure')
        run: exit 1
```

Key design decisions in this draft:

**Metadata job** runs first to compute the SHA tag, semver tag, environment mapping, and merge/PR detection. This avoids duplicating branch logic across stages.

**Stages 1-4 run unconditionally** (on both PRs and merges) for fast feedback. They also run in parallel since they have no dependencies on each other.

**Stages 5-7 gate on `is-merge == 'true'`** and require all four scanning stages to pass first (`needs: [lint-and-test, secret-scan, sca, sast]` on the build job).

**`secrets: inherit`** passes all caller secrets downstream rather than explicitly mapping each one, keeping the orchestrator clean.

**Branch-to-environment mapping** follows the documented convention: `develop` -> dev, `main` -> qa, `v*` tags -> prod.

**The summary job** uses `if: always()` to provide a status table in the GitHub Actions step summary regardless of pass/fail, then exits non-zero if any stage failed.

A few things to decide when implementing:

1. **Artifact Registry project** - I used `kd-ix-shared-artifacts` as a placeholder. Replace with the actual GCP project that hosts your container registry.
2. **The `image-tag` input to `_build-image.yaml`** has a redundant `sha-sha-` prefix issue in the current draft - the `sha-tag` output already includes the `sha-` prefix, so the `build-image` job's `image-tag` input should just be `${{ needs.determine-metadata.outputs.sha-tag }}` (which already contains `sha-xxxxxxx`).
3. **Sub-workflow contracts** - each `_*.yaml` file needs matching `workflow_call` inputs/outputs. The critical output is `image-ref` from `_build-image.yaml` (the full digest reference like `europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev/.../service@sha256:...`).

Want me to also draft any of the sub-workflows (`_lint-and-test.yaml`, `_secret-scan.yaml`, etc.)?

     1→---
     2→title: Kubernetes & Helm
     3→sidebar_label: Kubernetes & Helm
     4→sidebar_position: 5
     5→description: Helm chart strategy, namespace design, resource profiles, and autoscaling
     6→---
     7→
     8→# Kubernetes & Helm
     9→
    10→This document covers Helm chart design, namespace strategy, resource profiles, health probes, and autoscaling configuration.
    11→
    12→## Helm Chart Strategy
    13→
    14→### Two-Repo Architecture
    15→
    16→The platform uses a layered Helm architecture with charts living in **workload repos** (not code repos):
    17→
    18→```
    19→Layer 1: Base Chart Library (platform org)
    20→         └── kix-platform-modules/helm/base-service-chart/
    21→             ├── Chart.yaml (type: library)
    22→             └── templates/_*.tpl
    23→
    24→Layer 2: Service Chart + Environment Values (workload repo)
    25→         └── konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-iqportal/helm/
    26→             ├── Chart.yaml (depends on base chart)
    27→             ├── values.yaml (service defaults)
    28→             ├── values-dev.yaml (dev overrides)
    29→             ├── values-qa.yaml (qa overrides)
    30→             └── values-prod.yaml (prod overrides)
    31→```
    32→
    33→Code repos (konecta-ix-apps, konecta-ix-mcp-servers) contain **only source code and Dockerfiles** — no Helm charts or deployment configuration.
    34→
    35→### Base Chart Library
    36→
    37→Published to Artifact Registry as an OCI Helm chart. Contains templated resources:
    38→
    39→| Template | Purpose |
    40→|----------|---------|
    41→| `_deployment.tpl` | Pod spec, containers, sidecars |
    42→| `_service.tpl` | K8s Service definitions |
    43→| `_ingress.tpl` | Kong Ingress / HTTPRoute |
    44→| `_hpa.tpl` | HorizontalPodAutoscaler |
    45→| `_pdb.tpl` | PodDisruptionBudget |
    46→| `_networkpolicy.tpl` | Network isolation |
    47→| `_serviceaccount.tpl` | Workload Identity |
    48→| `_external-secret.tpl` | External Secrets CRD |
    49→
    50→### Service Chart (in Workload Repo)
    51→
    52→Each workload repo's Helm chart depends on the base chart and provides service-specific defaults:
    53→
    54→```yaml
    55→# helm/Chart.yaml (in kix-workload-iqportal)
    56→apiVersion: v2
    57→name: kix-workload-iqportal
    58→version: 0.1.0
    59→type: application
    60→
    61→dependencies:
    62→  - name: base-service-chart
    63→    version: "~1.0.0"
    64→    repository: "oci://europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev/kd-ix-platform/helm-charts"
    65→```
    66→
    67→### Base Chart Versioning
    68→
    69→- Published to Artifact Registry as OCI Helm chart
    70→- Service charts pin to a specific version (`~1.0.0`)
    71→- Renovate automates version bumps across all orgs
    72→- Breaking changes require major version bump
    73→
    74→## Namespace Strategy
    75→
    76→### Environment × Domain Boundaries (16 Namespaces)
    77→
    78→| Namespace Pattern | Contents |
    79→|-------------------|----------|
    80→| `{env}-api-services` | FastAPI backends, business apps, bots, data pipelines |
    81→| `{env}-mcp-servers` | MCP protocol servers |
    82→| `{env}-web-apps` | Nuxt 3 frontends |
    83→| `shared-kong` | Kong API Gateway |
    84→| `shared-litellm` | LiteLLM proxy (Kong-only access) |
    85→| `shared-argocd` | ArgoCD (existing) |
    86→| `shared-backstage` | Backstage developer portal |
    87→| `shared-monitoring` | Prometheus, Grafana, Jaeger |
    88→| `shared-devsecops` | SonarQube, Dependency-Track |
    89→| `shared-cert-manager` | TLS certificate management |
    90→
    91→### Namespace Configuration
    92→
    93→Each namespace receives:
    94→
    95→- **ResourceQuotas**: CPU/memory limits per namespace
    96→- **LimitRanges**: Default container limits
    97→- **NetworkPolicies**: Default deny-all ingress
    98→- **RBAC bindings**: Team-scoped access
    99→
   100→## Resource Profiles
   101→
   102→### Standard Profiles
   103→
   104→| Profile | CPU Request | CPU Limit | Mem Request | Mem Limit | Use Case |
   105→|---------|-------------|-----------|-------------|-----------|----------|
   106→| **API Service** | 100m | 500m | 256Mi | 512Mi | FastAPI APIs, MCP servers, bots, data pipelines |
   107→| **API Heavy** | 250m | 1000m | 512Mi | 1Gi | RAG ingestion, document processing, ML dependencies |
   108→| **Frontend** | 50m | 200m | 128Mi | 256Mi | Nuxt 3 SSR |
   109→
   110→### Cloud SQL Proxy Sidecar
   111→
   112→When using Cloud SQL Auth Proxy:
   113→
   114→```yaml
   115→resources:
   116→  requests:
   117→    cpu: 50m
   118→    memory: 64Mi
   119→  limits:
   120→    cpu: 200m
   121→    memory: 128Mi
   122→```
   123→
   124→## Health Probes
   125→
   126→### Probe Configuration by Service Type
   127→
   128→| Service Type | Liveness | Readiness | Startup |
   129→|--------------|----------|-----------|---------|
   130→| **FastAPI** | `GET /healthz` :8000 | `GET /readyz` :8000 (checks DB) | N/A |
   131→| **MCP Server (SSE)** | `GET /healthz` :8000, period=30s | `GET /readyz` :8000, initial=30s | N/A |
   132→| **Nuxt 3** | `GET /` :3000 | `GET /_health` :3000 | N/A |
   133→| **Heavy services** | `GET /healthz` :8000 | `GET /readyz` :8000 | failureThreshold=18 (3min) |
   134→
   135→### Example Probe Configuration
   136→
   137→```yaml
   138→probes:
   139→  liveness:
   140→    httpGet:
   141→      path: /healthz
   142→      port: 8080
   143→    initialDelaySeconds: 30
   144→    periodSeconds: 15
   145→    failureThreshold: 3
   146→  readiness:
   147→    httpGet:
   148→      path: /readyz
   149→      port: 8080
   150→    initialDelaySeconds: 40
   151→    periodSeconds: 10
   152→    failureThreshold: 3
   153→  startup:
   154→    httpGet:
   155→      path: /healthz
   156→      port: 8080
   157→    initialDelaySeconds: 10
   158→    periodSeconds: 5
   159→    failureThreshold: 12  # 60s max startup
   160→```
   161→
   162→## Autoscaling (HPA)
   163→
   164→### HPA Configuration by Tier
   165→
   166→| Tier | Min | Max | Target CPU | Scale-Down Window |
   167→|------|-----|-----|------------|-------------------|
   168→| **User-facing** (frontends, public APIs) | 2 | 20 | 60% | 5 min |
   169→| **Internal APIs, MCP servers** | 2 | 10 | 75% | 10 min |
   170→| **Data pipelines, bots** | 1 | 5 | 80% | 15 min |
   171→
   172→### Custom Metrics
   173→
   174→Via Prometheus Adapter:
   175→
   176→- Request rate
   177→- Pub/Sub queue depth
   178→- Active SSE connections
   179→
   180→### Example HPA Values
   181→
   182→```yaml
   183→autoscaling:
   184→  enabled: true
   185→  minReplicas: 2
   186→  maxReplicas: 10
   187→  targetCPUUtilization: 70
   188→  targetMemoryUtilization: 80
   189→```
   190→
   191→## Cloud SQL Auth Proxy Sidecar
   192→
   193→Services connecting to Cloud SQL use the **Cloud SQL Auth Proxy** as a sidecar container.
   194→
   195→### Why Sidecar (Not Shared Proxy)
   196→
   197→| Benefit | Description |
   198→|---------|-------------|
   199→| **Per-pod authentication** | Workload Identity per service account |
   200→| **Least-privilege IAM** | Each service has minimum required permissions |
   201→| **No bottleneck** | Scales with application pods |
   202→| **Google-recommended** | Official pattern for GKE |
   203→
   204→### How It Works
   205→
   206→```
   207→┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   208→│  Pod                                       │
   209→│  ┌──────────────────┐  ┌────────────────┐  │
   210→│  │  App Container   │  │  cloud-sql-    │  │
   211→│  │  (FastAPI)       │──│  proxy sidecar │────────▶ Cloud SQL
   212→│  │  :8000           │  │  :5432 (TCP)   │  │
   213→│  └──────────────────┘  └────────────────┘  │
   214→│  localhost:5432                            │
   215→└────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   216→```
   217→
   218→### Helm Values Configuration
   219→
   220→```yaml
   221→cloudSqlProxy:
   222→  enabled: true
   223→  instanceConnectionName: "project:region:instance"
   224→  port: 5432
   225→  resources:
   226→    requests:
   227→      cpu: 50m
   228→      memory: 64Mi
   229→    limits:
   230→      cpu: 200m
   231→      memory: 128Mi
   232→```
   233→
   234→### Connection String Pattern
   235→
   236→```
   237→DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://user@localhost:5432/dbname
   238→```
   239→
   240→No password needed when using `--auto-iam-authn` with Workload Identity.
   241→
   242→## Multi-Tier App Pattern
   243→
   244→Two-tiered apps (Nuxt frontend + FastAPI backend) deploy as **multi-container pods**.
   245→
   246→### Pod Layout
   247→
   248→```
   249→┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   250→│  Pod: kix-app-hrfraud                                            │
   251→│                                                                  │
   252→│  ┌──────────────────┐   localhost:8000   ┌────────────────────┐  │
   253→│  │  frontend        │ ─────────────────▶ │  backend           │  │
   254→│  │  (Nuxt SSR)      │                    │  (FastAPI)         │  │
   255→│  │  :3000           │                    │  :8000             │  │
   256→│  └──────────────────┘                    └─────────┬──────────┘  │
   257→│                                                    │ localhost   │
   258→│                                          ┌─────────▼──────────┐  │
   259→│                                          │  cloud-sql-proxy   │  │
   260→│                                          │  :5432             │───▶ Cloud SQL
   261→│                                          └────────────────────┘  │
   262→└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   263→         ▲                    ▲
   264→         │                    │
   265→    Frontend LB          API LB (Kong)
   266→  (Gateway API + IAP)   (internal routes)
   267→```
   268→
   269→### Benefits
   270→
   271→| Benefit | Description |
   272→|---------|-------------|
   273→| **localhost communication** | Zero network hop between frontend and backend |
   274→| **Atomic deploys** | Both containers deploy together, no version skew |
   275→| **Shared lifecycle** | Same release cycle, same Helm chart |
   276→| **Simpler networking** | No inter-service DNS, K8s Service only for external access |
   277→| **Fewer resources** | One Deployment, one HPA, one PDB |
   278→
   279→### When NOT to Use
   280→
   281→- Services needing independent scaling
   282→- Very different resource profiles
   283→- Loosely coupled services with different release cadences
   284→- Static SPA frontends (serve from CDN instead)
   285→
   286→### Helm Values Example
   287→
   288→```yaml
   289→containers:
   290→  backend:
   291→    image:
   292→      repository: eu-docker.pkg.dev/project/kix-services/kix-app-hrfraud-backend
   293→      tag: sha-abc1234
   294→    port: 8000
   295→    env:
   296→      DATABASE_URL: "postgresql+asyncpg://user@localhost:5432/dbname"
   297→      LITELLM_ENDPOINT: "http://kong.shared-kong.svc.cluster.local/llm"
   298→
   299→  frontend:
   300→    image:
   301→      repository: eu-docker.pkg.dev/project/kix-services/kix-app-hrfraud-frontend
   302→      tag: sha-def5678
   303→    port: 3000
   304→    env:
   305→      API_BASE: "http://localhost:8000"
   306→
   307→cloudSqlProxy:
   308→  enabled: true
   309→  instanceConnectionName: "project:eu-west1:hrfraud-db"
   310→
   311→services:
   312→  api:
   313→    port: 8000
   314→    ingress:
   315→      class: kong
   316→      path: /api/hrfraud
   317→  frontend:
   318→    port: 3000
   319→    ingress:
   320→      class: gateway-api
   321→      host: hrfraud.app.ix.konecta-digital.com
   322→```
   323→
   324→## ArgoCD Strategy
   325→
   326→### Per-Workload Application
   327→
   328→ArgoCD watches each **workload repo** directly via an Application manifest stored in `argocd/application.yaml`. There is no centralized ApplicationSet — each workload repo is self-contained.
   329→
   330→| Environment | Sync Policy | Change Window |
   331→|-------------|-------------|---------------|
   332→| **Dev** | `automated` (auto-sync) | 24/7 |
   333→| **QA** | `automated: false` (manual) | 08:00-18:00 UTC |
   334→| **Prod** | `automated: false` (manual) | Tue-Thu 20:00-23:00 UTC |
   335→
   336→See [GitOps & Promotion](gitops-promotion) for detailed ArgoCD configuration.
   337→
   338→### ArgoCD Projects
   339→
   340→- `dev-project` — RBAC for dev namespace deployments
   341→- `qa-project` — RBAC for qa namespace deployments
   342→- `prod-project` — RBAC for prod namespace deployments
   343→
   344→### Sync Waves
   345→
   346→- **Wave 0**: Infrastructure resources (namespaces, secrets, configmaps)
   347→- **Wave 10**: Application deployments
   348→
   349→---
   350→
   351→**Next**: [Ingress & Networking](ingress-networking) — Dual ingress architecture and network policies.
   352→
```

     7→
     8→# IQ Portal Migration Guide
     9→
    10→**Service**: kon-iq-portal
    11→**Code Repo**: `konecta-ix-apps/kix-app-iqportal`
    12→**Workload Repo**: `konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-iqportal`
    13→**Phase**: P0 (Pilot)
    14→
    15→---
    16→
    17→## 1. Current State Assessment
    18→
    19→### Architecture
    20→
    21→IQ Portal is a **single-container monolith**: an Express.js (TypeScript) backend serves both the API (`/api/*`) and a pre-generated Nuxt 4 SPA (static files from `/dist`). Everything runs on port **8080** in production.
    22→
    23→```
    24→┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
    25→│  Cloud Run (kon-iq-portal)              │
    26→│                                         │
    27→│  Express.js :8080                       │
    28→│  ├── /api/*  → API routes               │
    29→│  ├── /docs   → Swagger UI               │
    30→│  └── /*      → Static Nuxt SPA          │
    31→│                                         │
    32→│  Cloud SQL (Unix socket)                │
    33→│  /cloudsql/project:region:instance      │
    34→└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
    35→```
    36→
    37→### Current Tech Stack
    38→
    39→| Component | Detail |
    40→|-----------|--------|
    41→| Runtime | Node.js 22 (Alpine) |
    42→| Frontend | Nuxt 4 (SPA, `ssr: false`, pre-generated static) |
    43→| Backend | Express 5 (TypeScript, via `tsx`) |
    44→| Database | PostgreSQL on Cloud SQL (`kd-lab-464110:europe-west1:konecta-iqplatform`) |
    45→| DB Connection | Unix socket via VPC connector (`DB_HOST=/cloudsql/...`) |
    46→| Migrations | Custom SQL/TS runner (33 migrations, runs on startup) |
    47→| Auth | Google OAuth → JWT in HttpOnly cookies |
    48→| Storage | GCS (3 buckets: images, videos, RAG docs) |
    49→| AI | Vertex AI (Gemini) + RAG corpus |
    50→| Async Jobs | Cloud Tasks → kon-rag-ingestion |
    51→| Email | ChannelHub (external Cognito-auth API) |
    52→| CI/CD | Cloud Build from Bitbucket |
    53→| Port | 8080 (production), 3002 (dev) |
    54→
    55→### GCP Service Dependencies
    56→
    57→| Service | Project | Used For |
    58→|---------|---------|----------|
    59→| Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL) | `kd-lab-464110` | Primary database |
    60→| Cloud Storage | `kd-corp-dgt-svc-apps-dev` | Image/video/RAG file storage |
    61→| Vertex AI | `kd-lab-464110` | Gemini LLM + RAG retrieval |
    62→| Cloud Tasks | `kd-lab-464110` | Async RAG document ingestion |
    63→| Secret Manager | `kd-lab-464110` | JWT secret, DB password, RAG token |
    64→
    65→---
    66→
    67→## 2. Target State
    68→
    69→```
    70→┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    71→│  kix-infrastructure GKE Cluster                                     │
    72→│                                                                     │
    73→│  Namespace: dev-api-services (then qa-api-services, prod-...)       │
    74→│                                                                     │
    75→│  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
    76→│  │  Pod: kix-usecase-iq-portal                                   │  │
    77→│  │                                                               │  │
    78→│  │  ┌──────────────────────┐   ┌──────────────────────────────┐  │  │
    79→│  │  │  app (Express)       │   │  cloud-sql-proxy sidecar     │  │  │
    80→│  │  │  :8080               │──▶│  :5432 (TCP)                 │──────▶ Cloud SQL
    81→│  │  │  /api/* + SPA        │   │  --private-ip                │  │  │
    82→│  │  └──────────────────────┘   └──────────────────────────────┘  │  │
    83→│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
    84→│      │                                                              │
    85→│      ▼                                                              │
    86→│  Service: kix-usecase-iq-portal :8080                               │
    87→│      │                         │                                    │
    88→│      ▼                         ▼                                    │
    89→│  Kong Ingress              GKE Gateway API                          │
    90→│  /api/iq-portal/*          iq-portal.app.ix.konecta-digital.com                 │
    91→│  (API consumers)           (browser users via IAP)                  │
    92→└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    93→```
    94→
    95→### Key Differences from Cloud Run
    96→
    97→| Aspect | Cloud Run | kix-infrastructure |
    98→|--------|-----------|-------------------|
    99→| DB connection | Unix socket via VPC connector | Cloud SQL Auth Proxy sidecar (TCP `localhost:5432`) |
   100→| Secrets | Secret Manager direct access | External Secrets Operator → K8s Secrets |
   101→| Scaling | 0-10 instances | HPA 1-5 replicas |
   102→| Ingress | Direct HTTPS | Dual: Kong (API) + Gateway API + IAP (frontend) |
   103→| CI/CD | Cloud Build + Bitbucket | GitHub Actions + ArgoCD |
   104→| Health checks | Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK | K8s liveness/readiness probes |
   105→

   107→
   108→## 3. Pre-requisites
   109→
   110→Before starting, ensure:
   111→
   112→- [ ] Access to `konecta-ix-apps` GitHub org (write) — for code repo
   113→- [ ] Access to `konecta-ix-workloads` GitHub org (write) — for workload repo
   114→- [ ] Access to `konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-ci-workflows` (read)
   115→- [ ] `kix-platform-modules` base Helm chart published to Artifact Registry
   116→- [ ] Shared Kong gateway operational in `shared-kong` namespace
   117→- [ ] GKE Gateway API + IAP configured on frontend LB
   118→- [ ] GCP Workload Identity pool configured for GitHub Actions OIDC
   119→- [ ] Backstage operational in `shared-backstage` namespace
   120→- [ ] Cloud SQL instance accessible from GKE cluster (private IP, same VPC)
   121→- [ ] GCP service account for IQ Portal workload with IAM roles:
   122→  - `roles/cloudsql.client`
   123→  - `roles/storage.objectAdmin`
   124→  - `roles/aiplatform.user`
   125→  - `roles/cloudtasks.enqueuer`
   126→  - `roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor`

   129→
   130→## Step 1: Create the Repositories
   131→
   132→IQ Portal follows the **two-repo pattern** — a code repo for source code and a workload repo for hosting data.
   133→
   134→### 1.1 Create the code repo
   135→
   136→```bash
   137→gh repo create konecta-ix-apps/kix-app-iqportal \
   138→  --template konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-service-template \
   139→  --private
   140→

   142→cd kix-app-iqportal
   143→```
   144→
   145→### 1.2 Create the workload repo
   146→
   147→```bash
   148→gh repo create konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-iqportal \
   149→  --template konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-workload-template \
   150→  --private

   152→
   153→### 1.3 Copy application code into the code repo
   154→
   155→Copy the application source from the current `kon-iq-portal` repo into the code repo:
   156→
   157→```
   158→konecta-ix-apps/kix-app-iqportal/

   161→├── public/               # Static assets

   180→The workload repo structure is configured separately (see Step 4 and Step 7):

   202→### 1.4 Remove Cloud Build config

   266→
   267→### 1.8 Add TechDocs
   268→
   269→Create `docs/index.md`:
   270→
   271→```markdown
   272→# IQ Portal
   273→
   274→AI-powered knowledge platform for Konecta.
   275→
   276→## API
   277→
   278→Swagger documentation available at `/docs` on the running service.
   279→
   280→## Runbook
   281→
   282→- Health check: `GET /health` (liveness), `GET /api/health` (readiness)
   283→- Logs: `kubectl logs -n dev-api-services -l app=kix-app-iqportal -c app`
   284→- Database: Cloud SQL `kd-lab-464110:europe-west1:konecta-iqplatform`
   285→```
   286→
   287→Create `mkdocs.yml`:
   288→

   296→
   297→---
   298→
   299→## Step 2: Application Code Changes
   300→
   301→### 2.1 Database connection
   302→
   303→**No code changes required.** The existing `database.ts` supports both Unix socket (Cloud Run) and TCP (K8s):
   304→
   305→```typescript
   306→// backend/db/database.ts — already handles both
   307→const pool = process.env.DATABASE_URL
   308→    ? new Pool({ connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL })
   309→    : new Pool({
   310→        host: process.env.DB_HOST || 'localhost',
   311→        port: parseInt(process.env.DB_PORT || '5432'),
   312→        // ...
   313→    });
   314→```
   315→
   316→On kix, environment variables will be:
   317→```
   318→DB_HOST=localhost        # Cloud SQL Auth Proxy sidecar
   319→DB_PORT=5432
   320→```
   321→
   322→### 2.2 Add root-level health endpoint
   323→
   324→Add to `backend/routes/index.ts`:
   325→
   326→```typescript
   327→// K8S HEALTH PROBES
   328→// Lightweight endpoint for Kubernetes liveness probes
   329→app.get('/health', (req, res) => {
   330→    res.status(200).json({ status: 'ok' });
   331→});
   332→```
   333→
   334→Keep `/api/health` for detailed checks (DB + GCP connectivity).
   335→
   336→### 2.3 Environment variables
   337→
   338→All changes are via Helm values, no code changes:
   339→
   340→| Variable | kix Value |
   341→|----------|-----------|
   342→| `DB_HOST` | `localhost` (sidecar) |
   343→| `DB_PORT` | `5432` |
   344→| `MCP_GATEWAY_URL` | `http://kong.shared-kong.svc.cluster.local/mcp-gateway` |
   345→| `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | `https://iq-portal.app.ix.konecta-digital.com` |
   346→
   347→---
   348→
   349→## Step 3: Dockerfile Changes
   350→
   351→### 3.1 Pin base image digests
   352→
   353→Replace all `FROM node:22-alpine` with pinned digests:
   354→
   355→```dockerfile
   356→FROM node:22-alpine@sha256:<current-digest> AS dependencies
   357→```
   358→
   359→### 3.2 Remove HEALTHCHECK instruction
   360→
   361→Delete the `HEALTHCHECK` block (lines 142-157) — K8s probes replace it.
   362→
   363→---
   364→
   365→## Step 4: Helm Chart (Workload Repo)
   366→
   367→Configure the Helm chart in `konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-iqportal/helm/`.

   369→### 4.1 Chart.yaml
   370→

   378→  - name: base-service-chart
   379→    version: "~1.0.0"
   380→    repository: "oci://europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev/kd-ix-platform/helm-charts"

   478→
   479→---
   480→
   481→## Step 5: GitHub Actions CI Workflow (Code Repo)
   482→
   483→Create `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` in the **code repo** (`konecta-ix-apps/kix-app-iqportal`):
   484→
   485→```yaml
   486→name: CI Pipeline
   487→
   488→on:
   489→  push:
   490→    branches: [develop, main]
   491→  pull_request:
   492→    branches: [main]
   493→
   494→permissions:
   495→  contents: read
   496→  id-token: write
   497→  security-events: write
   498→
   499→jobs:
   500→  pipeline:
   501→    uses: konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-ci-workflows/.github/workflows/standard-pipeline.yaml@v1
   502→    with:
   503→      service-name: kix-app-iqportal
   504→      dockerfile-path: ./Dockerfile
   505→      node-version: "22"
   506→      build-args: |
   507→        VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=${{ vars.VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID }}
   508→        NUXT_PUBLIC_ENVIRONMENT=${{ vars.ENVIRONMENT }}
   509→        COMMIT_SHA=${{ github.sha }}
   510→      skip-tests: true
   511→    secrets: inherit
   512→```
   513→
   514→:::note
   515→No `chart-path` — Helm charts live in the workload repo, not the code repo.
   516→:::
   517→
   518→---
   519→
   520→## Step 6: Secrets Migration (Workload Repo)
   521→
   522→Secrets are managed via **Terraform** in the workload repo (`kix-workload-iqportal/terraform/`).
   523→
   524→### 6.1 Auto-generated secrets (Terraform)
   525→
   526→Add to `terraform/main.tf`:
   527→
   528→```hcl
   529→# Auto-generated secrets
   530→resource "random_password" "db" {
   531→  length  = 32
   532→  special = true
   533→}
   534→
   535→resource "random_password" "jwt" {
   536→  length  = 64
   537→  special = true
   538→}
   539→
   540→resource "google_secret_manager_secret" "db_password" {
   541→  secret_id = "kix-iq-portal-db-password-${var.environment}"
   542→  replication { auto {} }
   543→}
   544→
   545→resource "google_secret_manager_secret_version" "db_password" {
   546→  secret=[REDACTED].db_password.id
   547→  secret_data = random_password.db.result
   548→}
   549→```
   550→
   551→### 6.2 Static secrets (GitHub Actions → Terraform)
   552→
   553→Add per-environment secrets to the **workload repo** GitHub settings:
   554→
   555→| GitHub Secret (per env) | Terraform Variable | Source |
   556→|-------------------------|-------------------|--------|
   557→| `TF_VARS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` | `var.google_client_id` | Google OAuth |
   558→| `TF_VARS_RAG_PIPELINE_TOKEN` | `var.rag_pipeline_token` | RAG service |
   559→| `TF_VARS_CHANNELHUB_CLIENT_ID` | `var.channelhub_client_id` | ChannelHub |
   560→| `TF_VARS_CHANNELHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` | `var.channelhub_client_secret` | ChannelHub |
   561→| `TF_VARS_CHANNELHUB_CONNECTION_ID` | `var.channelhub_connection_id` | ChannelHub |
   562→
   563→### 6.3 Create Kubernetes secret (Terraform)
   564→
   565→```hcl
   566→resource "kubernetes_secret" "app_secrets" {
   567→  metadata {
   568→    name      = "kix-app-iqportal-secrets"
   569→    namespace = var.namespace
   570→  }
   571→  data = {
   572→    DB_PASSWORD               = random_password.db.result
   573→    DB_USER                   = var.db_user
   574→    JWT_SECRET                = random_password.jwt.result
   575→    GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID          = var.google_client_id
   576→    RAG_PIPELINE_TOKEN        = var.rag_pipeline_token
   577→    CHANNELHUB_CLIENT_ID      = var.channelhub_client_id
   578→    CHANNELHUB_CLIENT_SECRET  = var.channelhub_client_secret
   579→    CHANNELHUB_CONNECTION_ID  = var.channelhub_connection_id
   580→    GCS_IMAGE_BUCKET          = var.gcs_image_bucket
   581→    GCS_VIDEO_BUCKET          = var.gcs_video_bucket
   582→    GCS_RAG_BUCKET            = var.gcs_rag_bucket
   583→  }
   584→}
   585→```
   586→
   587→### 6.4 Apply Terraform
   588→
   589→```bash
   590→# Run via GitHub Actions or manually
   591→cd kix-workload-iqportal/terraform
   592→terraform init
   593→terraform plan \
   594→  -var="environment=dev" \
   595→  -var="google_client_id=$TF_VARS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID" \
   596→  -var="rag_pipeline_token=$TF_VARS_RAG_PIPELINE_TOKEN" \
   597→  # ... other TF_VARS_
   598→terraform apply
   599→```
   600→
   601→---
   602→
   603→## Step 7: GitOps Configuration (Workload Repo)
   604→
   605→### 7.1 ArgoCD Application
   606→
   607→Create `argocd/application.yaml` in the workload repo:
   608→
   609→```yaml
   610→apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
   611→kind: Application
   612→metadata:
   613→  name: kix-app-iqportal-dev
   614→  namespace: shared-argocd
   615→spec:
   616→  project: dev-project
   617→  source:
   618→    repoURL: https://github.com/konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-iqportal
   619→    path: helm
   620→    targetRevision: main
   621→    helm:
   622→      valueFiles:
   623→        - values.yaml
   624→        - values-dev.yaml
   625→  destination:
   626→    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
   627→    namespace: dev-api-services
   628→  syncPolicy:
   629→    automated:
   630→      prune: true
   631→      selfHeal: true
   632→```
   633→
   634→### 7.2 Dev environment values
   635→
   636→Create `helm/values-dev.yaml` in the workload repo:
   637→
   638→```yaml
   639→# helm/values-dev.yaml
   640→base-service-chart:
   641→  image:
   642→    tag: "sha-<initial-commit>"
   643→
   644→  containers:
   645→    app:
   646→      env:
   647→        NODE_ENV: "development"
   648→        NUXT_PUBLIC_ENVIRONMENT: "development"
   649→        ALLOWED_ORIGINS: "https://iq-portal.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com"
   650→        LOG_LEVEL: "debug"
   651→
   652→  autoscaling:
   653→    minReplicas: 1
   654→    maxReplicas: 2
   655→
   656→  services:
   657→    frontend:
   658→      ingress:
   659→        host: iq-portal.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com
   660→```
   661→
   662→---
   663→
   664→## Step 8: Database Migration
   665→
   666→### Strategy
   667→
   668→The app runs migrations automatically on startup. This is safe because:
   669→
   670→- The Cloud SQL instance already exists with the schema
   671→- Migrations are idempotent (tracked in `schema_migrations` table)
   672→- No schema changes are part of this migration
   673→
   674→### Connectivity test
   675→
   676→```bash
   677→# Deploy test pod with cloud-sql-proxy
   678→kubectl run sql-test --rm -it \
   679→  --image=gcr.io/cloud-sql-connectors/cloud-sql-proxy:2.14.3 \
   680→  --namespace=dev-api-services \
   681→  --serviceaccount=kix-usecase-iq-portal \
   682→  -- --private-ip kd-lab-464110:europe-west1:konecta-iqplatform
   683→```
   684→
   685→---
   686→
   687→## Step 9: Verification & Smoke Tests
   688→
   689→### 9.1 Deployment checklist
   690→
   691→```bash
   692→NAMESPACE=dev-api-services
   693→
   694→# 1. Pod running (2/2 = app + cloud-sql-proxy)
   695→kubectl get pods -n $NAMESPACE -l app=kix-app-iqportal
   696→
   697→# 2. Both containers healthy
   698→kubectl describe pod -n $NAMESPACE -l app=kix-app-iqportal | grep -A5 "Conditions"
   699→
   700→# 3. Logs check
   701→kubectl logs -n $NAMESPACE -l app=kix-app-iqportal -c app | grep "running on"
   702→
   703→# 4. Cloud SQL proxy connected
   704→kubectl logs -n $NAMESPACE -l app=kix-app-iqportal -c cloud-sql-proxy | grep "ready"
   705→```
   706→
   707→### 9.2 Functional smoke tests
   708→
   709→```bash
   710→BASE_URL="https://iq-portal.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com"
   711→
   712→# Health check
   713→curl -s $BASE_URL/health | jq .
   714→# Expected: {"status":"ok"}
   715→
   716→# Full health check
   717→curl -s $BASE_URL/api/health | jq .
   718→# Expected: {"status":"ok","checks":{"database":"ok","gcp":"ok"}}
   719→
   720→# Version
   721→curl -s $BASE_URL/api/version | jq .
   722→
   723→# Frontend loads
   724→curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" $BASE_URL/
   725→# Expected: 200
   726→
   727→# API auth check
   728→curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" $BASE_URL/api/agents
   729→# Expected: 401
   730→```
   731→
   732→---
   733→
   734→## Step 10: DNS & Domain Cutover
   735→
   736→### New domains
   737→
   738→| Path | Domain |
   739→|------|--------|
   740→| Frontend (browser) | `iq-portal.app.ix.konecta-digital.com` |
   741→| Frontend (dev) | `iq-portal.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com` |
   742→| API (machine) | `api.ix.konecta-digital.com/api/iq-portal` |
   743→
   744→### Decommission Cloud Run
   745→
   746→Once verified:
   747→
   748→```bash
   749→# Stop Cloud Run
   750→gcloud run services update kon-iq-portal \
   751→  --region=europe-west1 \
   752→  --max-instances=0
   753→
   754→# After confidence period (1-2 weeks), delete
   755→gcloud run services delete kon-iq-portal \
   756→  --region=europe-west1
   757→```

   788→## Appendix B: Rollback Procedure
   789→
   790→### Via Git
   791→
   792→```bash
   793→cd kix-workload-iqportal
   794→git revert HEAD
   795→git push
   796→# ArgoCD syncs automatically
   797→```
   798→
   799→### Via kubectl
   800→
   801→```bash
   802→kubectl rollout undo deployment/kix-app-iqportal -n dev-api-services

   804→
   805→### Fall back to Cloud Run
   806→
