     1→---
     2→title: GitOps & Promotion
     3→sidebar_label: GitOps & Promotion
     4→sidebar_position: 9
     5→description: ArgoCD GitOps flow, environment promotion, and rollback procedures
     6→---
     7→
     8→# GitOps & Promotion
     9→
    10→This document covers the ArgoCD GitOps flow, environment promotion strategy, and rollback procedures.
    11→
    12→## GitOps Flow
    13→
    14→### Per-Workload Repository Model
    15→
    16→Each service has its own **workload repo** in `konecta-ix-workloads` that ArgoCD watches directly. There is no centralized GitOps repository for application deployments.
    17→
    18→```
    19→CODE REPO                              WORKLOAD REPO
    20→konecta-ix-apps/                       konecta-ix-workloads/
    21→kix-app-iqportal                       kix-workload-iqportal
    22→────────────────                       ─────────────────────
    23→1. PR merged to develop
    24→2. Pipeline builds sha-abc1234
    25→3. Image pushed to Artifact Registry
    26→4. Developer or automation updates ──▶ 5. values-dev.yaml
    27→   image tag in workload repo              image.tag: sha-abc1234
    28→                                        6. ArgoCD detects change → syncs dev
    29→```
    30→
    31→### Workload Repository Structure
    32→
    33→```
    34→kix-workload-iqportal/
    35→├── helm/
    36→│   ├── Chart.yaml              # Depends on base-service-chart
    37→│   ├── values.yaml             # Service defaults (all envs)
    38→│   ├── values-dev.yaml         # Dev overrides (image tag, replicas, env vars)
    39→│   ├── values-qa.yaml          # QA overrides
    40→│   └── values-prod.yaml        # Prod overrides
    41→├── argocd/
    42→│   └── application.yaml        # ArgoCD Application manifest
    43→├── terraform/
    44→│   ├── main.tf                 # Service accounts, IAM, secrets
    45→│   ├── variables.tf
    46→│   └── backend.tf
    47→└── .github/workflows/
    48→    └── deploy.yaml             # Terraform validate-plan-apply
    49→```
    50→
    51→### Environment Values File
    52→
    53→Each environment has a values override file in the workload repo:
    54→
    55→```yaml
    56→# helm/values-dev.yaml
    57→base-service-chart:
    58→  image:
    59→    tag: "sha-abc1234"  # Updated on each deployment
    60→
    61→  containers:
    62→    app:
    63→      env:
    64→        NODE_ENV: "development"
    65→        LOG_LEVEL: "debug"
    66→
    67→  autoscaling:
    68→    minReplicas: 1
    69→    maxReplicas: 2
    70→```
    71→
    72→## ArgoCD Configuration
    73→
    74→### Per-Workload ArgoCD Application
    75→
    76→Each workload repo contains its own ArgoCD Application manifest. ArgoCD watches the repo directly:
    77→
    78→```yaml
    79→# argocd/application.yaml
    80→apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
    81→kind: Application
    82→metadata:
    83→  name: kix-app-iqportal-dev
    84→  namespace: shared-argocd
    85→spec:
    86→  project: dev-project
    87→  source:
    88→    repoURL: https://github.com/konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-iqportal
    89→    path: helm
    90→    targetRevision: main
    91→    helm:
    92→      valueFiles:
    93→        - values.yaml
    94→        - values-dev.yaml
    95→  destination:
    96→    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    97→    namespace: dev-api-services
    98→  syncPolicy:
    99→    automated:
   100→      prune: true
   101→      selfHeal: true
   102→    syncOptions:
   103→      - CreateNamespace=false
   104→```
   105→
   106→:::note
   107→Multiple ArgoCD Application manifests can exist in the same workload repo (one per environment), or environments can be managed via separate branches/tags. The example above shows the single-manifest approach with environment-specific value files.
   108→:::
   109→
   110→### Sync Policies by Environment
   111→
   112→| Environment | Sync Mode | When |
   113→|-------------|-----------|------|
   114→| **Dev** | `automated` (auto-sync) | 24/7 |
   115→| **QA** | `automated: false` (manual) | 08:00-18:00 UTC |
   116→| **Prod** | `automated: false` (manual) | Tue-Thu 20:00-23:00 UTC |
   117→
   118→### ArgoCD Projects
   119→
   120→RBAC isolation per environment:
   121→
   122→```yaml
   123→apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
   124→kind: AppProject
   125→metadata:
   126→  name: dev-project
   127→  namespace: shared-argocd
   128→spec:
   129→  description: Development environment
   130→  sourceRepos:
   131→    - 'https://github.com/konecta-ix-workloads/*'
   132→    - 'https://github.com/konecta-ix-services/*'
   133→  destinations:
   134→    - namespace: 'dev-*'
   135→      server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
   136→  clusterResourceWhitelist:
   137→    - group: ''
   138→      kind: Namespace
   139→```
   140→
   141→## Environment Promotion
   142→
   143→### Promotion Workflow
   144→
   145→Promotion updates the image tag in the target environment's values file within the workload repo:
   146→
   147→```
   148→Dev (values-dev.yaml)  →  QA (values-qa.yaml)  →  Prod (values-prod.yaml)
   149→  sha-abc1234                sha-abc1234               sha-abc1234
   150→```
   151→
   152→### Dev → QA Promotion
   153→
   154→1. Verify service is healthy in dev
   155→2. Update `helm/values-qa.yaml` with the image tag from dev:
   156→   ```bash
   157→   # In kix-workload-iqportal
   158→   # Update image.tag in values-qa.yaml to match values-dev.yaml
   159→   ```
   160→3. Create PR, review, merge
   161→4. ArgoCD syncs to QA (manual sync during change window)
   162→
   163→### QA → Prod Promotion (with DAST)
   164→
   165→1. Verify service is healthy in QA
   166→2. Run **OWASP ZAP baseline scan** against QA endpoint
   167→3. If ZAP finds vulnerabilities → promotion blocked, findings reported
   168→4. If ZAP passes → update `helm/values-prod.yaml` with the image tag
   169→5. Create PR with approval requirement
   170→6. After merge, ArgoCD syncs to prod (manual sync during change window)
   171→
   172→### Change Windows
   173→
   174→| Environment | Window | Notes |
   175→|-------------|--------|-------|
   176→| **Dev** | 24/7 | Auto-approve allowed |
   177→| **QA** | 08:00-18:00 UTC (Mon-Fri) | Manual approval required |
   178→| **Prod** | Tue-Thu 20:00-23:00 UTC | Manual approval + change ticket |
   179→
   180→## Rollback Procedures
   181→
   182→### Manual Rollback via Git (Recommended)
   183→
   184→Fastest rollback method — revert the image tag change in the workload repo:
   185→
   186→```bash
   187→cd kix-workload-iqportal
   188→
   189→# Revert the last commit (image tag update)
   190→git revert HEAD
   191→git push
   192→
   193→# ArgoCD auto-syncs (dev) or manual sync (qa/prod)
   194→```
   195→
   196→### Manual Rollback via kubectl
   197→
   198→For emergency when git is unavailable:
   199→
   200→```bash
   201→# Roll back to previous ReplicaSet
   202→kubectl rollout undo deployment/kix-app-iqportal -n dev-api-services
   203→
   204→# Verify
   205→kubectl rollout status deployment/kix-app-iqportal -n dev-api-services
   206→```
   207→
   208→:::warning
   209→kubectl rollback doesn't update Git — reconcile Git state in the workload repo after emergency.
   210→:::
   211→
   212→### ArgoCD Rollback
   213→
   214→Via ArgoCD UI or CLI:
   215→
   216→```bash
   217→# List recent syncs
   218→argocd app history kix-app-iqportal-dev
   219→
   220→# Rollback to specific revision
   221→argocd app rollback kix-app-iqportal-dev <revision>
   222→```
   223→
   224→## Sync Waves
   225→
   226→Resources deploy in order via sync waves:
   227→
   228→| Wave | Resources |
   229→|------|-----------|
   230→| 0 | Namespaces, RBAC, SecretStores |
   231→| 5 | ConfigMaps, Secrets |
   232→| 10 | Deployments, Services, HPA |
   233→| 15 | Ingress, NetworkPolicies |
   234→
   235→Example annotation:
   236→
   237→```yaml
   238→metadata:
   239→  annotations:
   240→    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "10"
   241→```
   242→
   243→## Health Checks
   244→
   245→ArgoCD monitors resource health:
   246→
   247→| Resource | Health Check |
   248→|----------|--------------|
   249→| Deployment | All replicas ready |
   250→| Service | Endpoints exist |
   251→| Ingress | Address assigned |
   252→| HPA | Current replicas within bounds |
   253→
   254→## Notifications
   255→
   256→ArgoCD notifications on sync events:
   257→
   258→| Event | Channel | Recipients |
   259→|-------|---------|------------|
   260→| Sync success | Slack #deployments | Team channel |
   261→| Sync failure | Slack #deployments + PagerDuty | Team + On-call |
   262→| Health degraded | Slack #alerts | Team channel |
   263→| Prod deployment | Slack #prod-changes | Wider audience |
   264→
   265→### Example Notification Template
   266→
   267→```yaml
   268→apiVersion: v1
   269→kind: ConfigMap
   270→metadata:
   271→  name: argocd-notifications-cm
   272→data:
   273→  template.app-sync-succeeded: |
   274→    message: |
   275→      Application {{.app.metadata.name}} sync succeeded.
   276→      Revision: {{.app.status.sync.revision}}
   277→      Environment: {{.app.spec.destination.namespace}}
   278→```
   279→
   280→## Disaster Recovery
   281→
   282→### Multi-Region Failover
   283→
   284→1. Secondary GKE cluster in eu-west4 (pre-provisioned)
   285→2. DNS-based failover to secondary cluster
   286→3. ArgoCD can deploy to secondary from same workload repo Git state
   287→
   288→### Recovery Steps
   289→
   290→1. Detect primary failure (health check timeout)
   291→2. Update DNS to point to secondary LB
   292→3. ArgoCD in secondary syncs from workload repos
   293→4. Services running on secondary within 15 minutes
   294→
   295→### State Recovery
   296→
   297→Application state in managed services (Cloud SQL, GCS) — replicated separately.
   298→
   299→---
   300→
   301→**Next**: [Backstage & Onboarding](backstage-onboarding) — Developer portal and service onboarding.
   302→
```

     1→---
     2→title: Migration Phases
     3→sidebar_label: Migration Phases
     4→sidebar_position: 4
     5→description: Phased migration strategy with priorities and timeline
     6→---
     7→
     8→# Migration Phases
     9→
    10→This document describes the phased approach to migrating services from Cloud Run to kix-infrastructure.
    11→
    12→## Migration Context
    13→
    14→**No services are currently in production.** Services will migrate directly to new domains on kix-infrastructure — no dual-stack, no DNS cutover, no downtime concerns.
    15→
    16→All application services are **stateless** — state lives in Cloud SQL, Firestore, and GCS. Container images contain no data; configuration is provided via ConfigMaps and Secrets.
    17→
    18→## Migration Priority
    19→
    20→| Priority | Services | Rationale |
    21→|----------|----------|-----------|
    22→| **P0 — Pilot** | kix-usecase-iq-portal (backend + frontend) | Validates entire platform: both ingress paths, Cloud SQL sidecar, standard pipeline, cross-org dispatch |
    23→| **P1 — Platform Core** | Kong, LiteLLM (behind Kong), MCP Gateway | Must be running before other services can function |
    24→| **P2 — MCP Servers** | Remaining 13 MCP servers | Foundation for AI/business workflows |
    25→| **P3 — Business Apps** | kix-app-hrfraud, kix-app-hrportal, kix-usecase-testiq | Remaining user-facing applications |
    26→| **P4 — Data & Demos** | RAG pipelines, bot, prototypes | Lower priority, migrate last |
    27→
    28→## Phase 1: Platform Foundation + Pilot
    29→
    30→**Focus**: Establish platform infrastructure and validate with the pilot service.
    31→
    32→### Platform Infrastructure Tasks
    33→
    34→| Task | Repository | Description |
    35→|------|------------|-------------|
    36→| Create CI workflows repo | `kix-platform-ci-workflows` | Standard pipeline with reusable workflows |
    37→| Add base Helm chart | `kix-platform-modules` | Publish to Artifact Registry as OCI chart |
    38→| Configure ArgoCD | `kix-platform-infrastructure` | ApplicationSets with git directory generator |
    39→| Create service template | `kix-platform-service-template` | Template repo for bootstrapping |
    40→| Install GitHub App | Cross-org | Enable cross-org dispatch for GitOps updates |
    41→| Configure OIDC | Per org | GitHub OIDC → GCP Workload Identity Pool |
    42→| Deploy Kong + LiteLLM | `shared-kong`, `shared-litellm` | API gateway and LLM proxy |
    43→| Deploy Backstage | `shared-backstage` | Developer portal with GitHub org discovery |
    44→
    45→### Pilot: IQ Portal
    46→
    47→Deploy `kix-usecase-iq-portal` as the first service through the full pipeline:
    48→
    49→| Validation Point | Description |
    50→|------------------|-------------|
    51→| **Backend deployment** | Kong API ingress, Cloud SQL Auth Proxy sidecar, External Secrets |
    52→| **Frontend deployment** | GKE Gateway API + IAP ingress path, separate LB |
    53→| **Helm chart profiles** | Both API Service and Frontend profiles |
    54→| **Cross-org dispatch** | konecta-ix-workloads → konecta-ix-platform GitOps |
    55→| **Full CI pipeline** | Build, scan, sign, push, deploy |
    56→
    57→**Outcome**: Fix any issues in base chart, CI workflows, or ArgoCD config before scaling out.
    58→
    59→**Detailed guide**: [IQ Portal Migration Guide](service-guides/iq-portal)
    60→
    61→## Phase 2: MCP Servers
    62→
    63→**Focus**: Migrate all MCP servers using the validated platform.
    64→
    65→### Migration Order
    66→
    67→| Order | Service | Priority | Dependencies |
    68→|-------|---------|----------|--------------|
    69→| 1 | kix-mcp-gateway | P1 | None — gateway for other MCP servers |
    70→| 2 | kix-mcp-ragengine | P2 | Vertex AI RAG corpus |
    71→| 3 | kix-mcp-channelhub | P2 | Channel Hub external API |
    72→| 4 | kix-mcp-google-search | P2 | Google Search API |
    73→| 5-14 | Remaining MCP servers | P2-P3 | Various GCP APIs |
    74→
    75→### Per-Service Migration Steps
    76→
    77→For each MCP server:
    78→
    79→1. Create repo from template in `konecta-ix-mcp-servers`
    80→2. Copy application code and update configuration
    81→3. Add `catalog-info.yaml` for Backstage
    82→4. Push to trigger CI pipeline
    83→5. Verify deployment in dev
    84→6. Promote to qa, then prod
    85→7. Decommission corresponding Cloud Run service
    86→
    87→### Expected Outcomes
    88→
    89→- All 14 MCP servers running on kix-infrastructure
    90→- Unified observability via Prometheus/Grafana
    91→- Service catalog populated in Backstage
    92→- Cloud Run MCP services decommissioned
    93→
    94→## Phase 3: Business Applications
    95→
    96→**Focus**: Migrate remaining user-facing applications.
    97→
    98→### Migration Order
    99→
   100→| Order | Service | Type | Notes |
   101→|-------|---------|------|-------|
   102→| 1 | kix-app-hrfraud | Multi-tier (Nuxt + FastAPI + Cloud SQL) | Similar pattern to IQ Portal |
   103→| 2 | kix-app-hrportal | Frontend only | Nuxt 3 SPA |
   104→| 3 | kix-usecase-testiq | Frontend only | Nuxt 3 SPA |
   105→
   106→### Multi-Tier App Pattern
   107→
   108→Apps like `kix-app-hrfraud` deploy as **multi-container pods** (see [Kubernetes & Helm](kubernetes-helm#multi-tier-app-pattern)):
   109→
   110→- Nuxt frontend (port 3000) + FastAPI backend (port 8000) + cloud-sql-proxy sidecar (port 5432)
   111→- Frontend calls backend via `localhost:8000`
   112→- Both containers deploy atomically
   113→
   114→### Expected Outcomes
   115→
   116→- All business apps running on kix-infrastructure
   117→- Frontend apps behind GKE Gateway API + IAP
   118→- Cloud Run business app services decommissioned
   119→
   120→## Phase 4: Data Pipelines & Cleanup
   121→
   122→**Focus**: Migrate remaining services and decommission Cloud Run.
   123→
   124→### Migration Tasks
   125→
   126→| Service | Type | Notes |
   127→|---------|------|-------|
   128→| kix-usecase-rag-ingestion | Data pipeline | Cloud Tasks integration |
   129→| kix-usecase-rag-googledrive | Data pipeline | Google Drive API |
   130→| kix-demo-porfolioguru | Bot | Convert from Cloud Functions |
   131→| kix-demo-prototypes | Various | Low priority |
   132→
   133→### Cleanup Tasks
   134→
   135→| Task | Description |
   136→|------|-------------|
   137→| Decommission Cloud Run | Delete all migrated Cloud Run services |
   138→| Remove Cloud Build configs | Delete `cloudbuild.yaml` from old repos |
   139→| Archive old repos | Mark Bitbucket repos as read-only |
   140→| Update DNS records | Point to kix-infrastructure LB IPs |
   141→
   142→## Post-Migration Activities
   143→
   144→### Validation
   145→
   146→- [ ] All services deployed and healthy
   147→- [ ] Prometheus metrics flowing
   148→- [ ] Backstage catalog complete
   149→- [ ] CI pipelines green for all services
   150→- [ ] ArgoCD sync status healthy
   151→
   152→### Documentation
   153→
   154→- [ ] Update runbooks with new procedures
   155→- [ ] Archive Cloud Run documentation
   156→- [ ] Train teams on new deployment process
   157→
   158→### Optimisation

   161→- [ ] Optimise resource requests/limits
   162→- [ ] Review network policies
   163→- [ ] Implement KEDA for scale-to-zero (if needed)
   164→
   165→## Migration Checklist Template
   166→
   167→Use this checklist for each service migration:
   168→
   169→```markdown

   171→
   172→### Pre-Migration
   173→- [ ] Review current Cloud Run configuration

   177→
   178→### Migration

   181→- [ ] Configure Helm values
   182→- [ ] Add catalog-info.yaml
   183→- [ ] Create ExternalSecret for secrets
   184→- [ ] Push and trigger CI pipeline
   185→
   186→### Validation
   187→- [ ] Pod running (container + sidecars healthy)
   188→- [ ] Health probes passing
   189→- [ ] Ingress routing correctly

     7→
     8→# Backstage & Onboarding
     9→
    10→This document covers Backstage integration and the process for onboarding new services to the platform.
    11→
    12→## Backstage Overview
    13→
    14→**Backstage** (`shared-backstage` namespace) serves as the internal developer portal, providing a single pane of glass across all 24+ services spread across 6 GitHub organisations.
    15→
    16→### Core Capabilities
    17→
    18→| Capability | Backstage Feature | Integration |
    19→|------------|------------------|-------------|
    20→| **Service catalog** | Software Catalog | Auto-discovers `catalog-info.yaml` from all GitHub orgs |
    21→| **New service creation** | Software Templates | Pre-built templates for Python/Node.js/MCP services |
    22→| **Documentation** | TechDocs | Renders `docs/` markdown into unified portal |
    23→| **CI/CD visibility** | GitHub Actions plugin | Pipeline status, build history per service |
    24→| **Deployment status** | ArgoCD plugin | Sync status, deployed image tag, health per environment |
    25→| **Live K8s status** | Kubernetes plugin | Pod count, status, resource usage, logs |
    26→| **Security posture** | SonarQube + Dependency-Track plugins | Code quality, vulnerability counts |
    27→| **API documentation** | API docs plugin | Renders OpenAPI/Swagger specs |
    28→| **Ownership** | Catalog model | Maps services → teams → GitHub orgs |
    29→
    30→## Service Onboarding
    31→
    32→### Option A: Via Backstage Software Template (Recommended)
    33→
    34→The fastest way to create a new service. Backstage scaffolds **two repositories** — one for code, one for hosting:
    35→
    36→1. **Open Backstage** at `https://backstage.app.ix.konecta-digital.com`
    37→2. **Create Component** → Select template:
    38→   - Python API
    39→   - Node.js API
    40→   - Nuxt Frontend
    41→   - MCP Server
    42→3. **Fill in the form**:
    43→   - Service name
    44→   - Owning team
    45→   - Code GitHub org (konecta-ix-apps, konecta-ix-mcp-servers, etc.)
    46→   - Cloud SQL requirement (yes/no)
    47→   - Ingress type (Kong/Gateway API/both)
    48→4. **Backstage scaffolds the code repo** (e.g. `konecta-ix-apps/kix-app-newservice`) with:
    49→   - Standard `Dockerfile`
    50→   - Standard `.github/workflows/ci.yaml`
    51→   - Pre-filled `catalog-info.yaml`
    52→   - `docs/index.md` stub for TechDocs
    53→5. **Backstage scaffolds the workload repo** (e.g. `konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-newservice`) with:
    54→   - `helm/` directory (`Chart.yaml`, `values.yaml`, `values-{env}.yaml`)
    55→   - `argocd/application.yaml` (ArgoCD Application manifest)
    56→   - `terraform/` directory (service account, IAM, secrets)
    57→   - `.github/workflows/deploy.yaml` (Terraform workflow)
    58→6. **ArgoCD watches the workload repo** and syncs the Helm release
    59→7. **First push to code repo** triggers standard CI pipeline
    60→8. **Service appears in Backstage catalog**
    61→
    62→### Option B: Manual Onboarding
    63→
    64→For cases where template doesn't fit:
    65→
    66→1. **Create code repo** from template:
    67→   ```bash
    68→   gh repo create konecta-ix-mcp-servers/kix-mcp-newservice \
    69→     --template konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-service-template \
    70→     --private
    71→   ```
    72→
    73→2. **Create workload repo** from template:
    74→   ```bash
    75→   gh repo create konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-mcp-newservice \
    76→     --template konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-workload-template \
    77→     --private
    78→   ```
    79→
    80→3. **Configure code repo**:
    81→   - Copy application source code
    82→   - Update `Dockerfile`
    83→   - Create `catalog-info.yaml`
    84→   - Configure `.github/workflows/ci.yaml`
    85→
    86→4. **Configure workload repo**:
    87→   - Update `helm/values.yaml` with service defaults
    88→   - Create `helm/values-dev.yaml`, `helm/values-qa.yaml`, `helm/values-prod.yaml` with env overrides
    89→   - Update `argocd/application.yaml` with correct repo URL and namespace
    90→   - Update `terraform/` with service account, IAM, and secrets
    91→   - Add `TF_VARS_*` secrets to GitHub repo settings per environment
    92→
    93→5. **ArgoCD picks up** the workload repo Application manifest
    94→
    95→6. **Backstage auto-discovers** `catalog-info.yaml` from code repo within 30 minutes
    96→
    97→## catalog-info.yaml
    98→
    99→Every service repo must include a `catalog-info.yaml` for Backstage discovery:
   100→
   101→```yaml
   102→apiVersion: backstage.io/v1alpha1
   103→kind: Component
   104→metadata:
   105→  name: kix-mcp-gateway
   106→  description: MCP Gateway — routes MCP protocol requests to backend servers
   107→  annotations:
   108→    # GitHub
   109→    github.com/project-slug: konecta-ix-mcp-servers/kix-mcp-gateway
   110→    # ArgoCD
   111→    argocd/app-name: kix-mcp-gateway
   112→    # Kubernetes
   113→    backstage.io/kubernetes-id: kix-mcp-gateway
   114→    backstage.io/kubernetes-namespace: dev-mcp-servers,qa-mcp-servers,prod-mcp-servers
   115→    # TechDocs
   116→    backstage.io/techdocs-ref: dir:.
   117→    # SonarQube
   118→    sonarqube.org/project-key: kix-mcp-gateway
   119→  tags:
   120→    - python
   121→    - mcp
   122→    - fastmcp
   123→  links:
   124→    - url: https://api.ix.konecta-digital.com/api/mcp-gateway/health
   125→      title: Health Check
   126→      icon: dashboard
   127→spec:
   128→  type: service
   129→  lifecycle: production
   130→  owner: group:mcp-integration-team
   131→  system: kix-platform
   132→  providesApis:
   133→    - mcp-gateway-api
   134→  dependsOn:
   135→    - component:kix-services-kong
   136→    - component:kix-services-litellm
   137→```
   138→
   139→### Key Annotations
   140→
   141→| Annotation | Purpose |
   142→|------------|---------|
   143→| `github.com/project-slug` | Links to GitHub repo |
   144→| `argocd/app-name` | Shows deployment status |
   145→| `backstage.io/kubernetes-id` | Shows pod status |
   146→| `backstage.io/kubernetes-namespace` | Which namespaces to query |
   147→| `backstage.io/techdocs-ref` | TechDocs source location |
   148→| `sonarqube.org/project-key` | Links to code quality |
   149→
   150→## Software Templates
   151→
   152→Backstage hosts 4 Software Templates in `kix-platform-backstage/templates/`:
   153→
   154→| Template | Creates | Includes |
   155→|----------|---------|----------|
   156→| `python-api` | Python FastAPI service | Dockerfile, chart/, ci.yaml, catalog-info.yaml, docs/ |
   157→| `nodejs-api` | Node.js Express service | Dockerfile, chart/, ci.yaml, catalog-info.yaml, docs/ |
   158→| `mcp-server` | Python FastMCP server | Dockerfile, chart/, ci.yaml, catalog-info.yaml, docs/ |
   159→| `nuxt-frontend` | Nuxt 3 frontend | Dockerfile, chart/, ci.yaml, catalog-info.yaml, docs/ |
   160→
   161→### Template Parameters
   162→
   163→Each template prompts for:
   164→
   165→| Parameter | Description |
   166→|-----------|-------------|
   167→| `name` | Service name (e.g., `kix-mcp-newservice`) |
   168→| `description` | Brief description |
   169→| `owner` | Owning team (Backstage group) |
   170→| `githubOrg` | Target GitHub organisation |
   171→| `cloudSql` | Needs Cloud SQL? (adds sidecar) |
   172→| `ingressType` | Kong, Gateway API, or both |
   173→
   174→## Catalog Discovery
   175→
   176→Backstage discovers services via GitHub organisation-wide discovery:
   177→
   178→```yaml
   179→# Backstage app-config.yaml
   180→catalog:
   181→  providers:
   182→    github:
   183→      konecta-ix-platform:
   184→        organization: konecta-ix-platform
   185→        catalogPath: /catalog-info.yaml
   186→        schedule:
   187→          frequency: { minutes: 30 }
   188→          timeout: { minutes: 3 }
   189→      konecta-ix-mcp-servers:
   190→        organization: konecta-ix-mcp-servers
   191→        catalogPath: /catalog-info.yaml
   192→        schedule:
   193→          frequency: { minutes: 30 }
   194→          timeout: { minutes: 3 }
   195→      # ... other orgs
   196→```
   197→
   198→### Discovery Frequency
   199→
   200→- Automatic refresh: every 30 minutes
   201→- Manual refresh: via Backstage UI (Catalog → Refresh)
   202→
   203→## TechDocs
   204→
   205→### Setup
   206→
   207→Every service should include a `docs/` directory and `mkdocs.yml`:
   208→
   209→```
   210→service-repo/
   211→├── docs/
   212→│   └── index.md
   213→└── mkdocs.yml
   214→```
   215→
   216→### mkdocs.yml
   217→
   218→```yaml
   219→site_name: MCP Gateway
   220→nav:
   221→  - Home: index.md
   222→  - API: api.md
   223→  - Runbook: runbook.md
   224→plugins:
   225→  - techdocs-core
   226→```
   227→
   228→### Building TechDocs
   229→
   230→TechDocs are built automatically by Backstage or can be pre-built in CI:
   231→
   232→```yaml
   233→- name: Build TechDocs
   234→  run: |
   235→    npx @techdocs/cli generate --source-dir . --output-dir ./site
   236→    npx @techdocs/cli publish --publisher-type googleGcs \
   237→      --storage-name $TECHDOCS_BUCKET \
   238→      --entity default/component/kix-mcp-gateway
   239→```
   240→
   241→## Backstage Plugins
   242→
   243→### Installed Plugins
   244→
   245→| Plugin | Purpose |
   246→|--------|---------|
   247→| `@backstage/plugin-github-actions` | CI pipeline status |
   248→| `@roadiehq/backstage-plugin-argo-cd` | Deployment status |
   249→| `@backstage/plugin-kubernetes` | Pod status, logs |
   250→| `@backstage/plugin-sonarqube` | Code quality metrics |
   251→| `@backstage/plugin-techdocs` | Documentation rendering |
   252→| `@backstage/plugin-api-docs` | OpenAPI documentation |
   253→| `@backstage/plugin-catalog-import` | Entity import |
   254→
   255→### Plugin Configuration
   256→
   257→Example ArgoCD plugin config:
   258→

   264→    - type: 'config'
   265→      instances:
   266→        - name: main
   267→          url: https://argocd.ix.konecta-digital.com
   268→```
   269→
   270→## Onboarding Checklist
   271→

  "old_string": "### Two-Repo Architecture\n\nThe platform uses a layered Helm architecture with charts living in **workload repos** (not code repos):\n\n```\nLayer 1: Base Chart Library (platform org)\n         └── kix-platform-modules/helm/base-service-chart/\n             ├── Chart.yaml (type: library)\n             └── templates/_*.tpl\n\nLayer 2: Service Chart + Environment Values (workload repo)\n         └── konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-iqportal/helm/\n             ├── Chart.yaml (depends on base chart)\n             ├── values.yaml (service defaults)\n             ├── values-dev.yaml (dev overrides)\n             ├── values-qa.yaml (qa overrides)\n             └── values-prod.yaml (prod overrides)\n```\n\nCode repos (konecta-ix-apps, konecta-ix-mcp-servers) contain **only source code and Dockerfiles** — no Helm charts or deployment configuration.\n\n### Base Chart Library\n\nPublished to Artifact Registry as an OCI Helm chart. Contains templated resources:\n\n| Template | Purpose |\n|----------|---------|\n| `_deployment.tpl` | Pod spec, containers, sidecars |\n| `_service.tpl` | K8s Service definitions |\n| `_ingress.tpl` | Kong Ingress / HTTPRoute |\n| `_hpa.tpl` | HorizontalPodAutoscaler |\n| `_pdb.tpl` | PodDisruptionBudget |\n| `_networkpolicy.tpl` | Network isolation |\n| `_serviceaccount.tpl` | Workload Identity |\n| `_external-secret.tpl` | External Secrets CRD |\n\n### Service Chart (in Workload Repo)\n\nEach workload repo's Helm chart depends on the base chart and provides service-specific defaults:\n\n```yaml\n# helm/Chart.yaml (in kix-workload-iqportal)\napiVersion: v2\nname: kix-workload-iqportal\nversion: 0.1.0\ntype: application\n\ndependencies:\n  - name: base-service-chart\n    version: \"~1.0.0\"\n    repository: \"oci://europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev/kd-ix-platform/helm-charts\"\n```\n\n### Base Chart Versioning\n\n- Published to Artifact Registry as OCI Helm chart\n- Service charts pin to a specific version (`~1.0.0`)\n- Renovate automates version bumps across all orgs\n- Breaking changes require major version bump",
  "new_string": "### Two-Repo Architecture\n\nThe platform uses a layered Helm architecture. The **base chart** lives in the platform modules Git repo and is composed with **per-service values** from workload repos via ArgoCD multi-source:\n\n```\nBase Chart (platform org — Git source of truth)\n         └── kix-platform-modules/helm/base-service-chart/\n             ├── Chart.yaml (type: application)\n             └── templates/\n                 ├── deployment.yaml\n                 ├── service.yaml\n                 ├── ingress.yaml\n                 └── ...\n\nPer-Service Values (workload repo)\n         └── konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-iqportal/helm/\n             ├── values.yaml (service defaults)\n             ├── values-dev.yaml (dev overrides)\n             ├── values-qa.yaml (qa overrides)\n             └── values-prod.yaml (prod overrides)\n```\n\nArgoCD multi-source combines the chart from Git with values from the workload repo — no OCI registry needed for Helm charts.\n\nCode repos (konecta-ix-apps, konecta-ix-mcp-servers) contain **only source code and Dockerfiles** — no Helm charts or deployment configuration.\n\n### Base Chart\n\nThe base chart is an **application chart** (`type: application`) in `kix-platform-modules/helm/base-service-chart/`. It is pulled directly from Git over HTTPS by ArgoCD — no OCI publish step required.\n\nContains standard Kubernetes resource templates driven by values:\n\n| Template | Purpose |\n|----------|---------|\n| `deployment.yaml` | Pod spec, containers, sidecars |\n| `service.yaml` | K8s Service definitions |\n| `ingress.yaml` | Kong Ingress / HTTPRoute |\n| `hpa.yaml` | HorizontalPodAutoscaler |\n| `pdb.yaml` | PodDisruptionBudget |\n| `networkpolicy.yaml` | Network isolation |\n| `serviceaccount.yaml` | Workload Identity |\n| `external-secret.yaml` | External Secrets CRD |\n\n### Per-Service Values (in Workload Repo)\n\nWorkload repos provide **values files only** — no `Chart.yaml` dependency block is needed. ArgoCD multi-source composes the base chart with service-specific values at sync time:\n\n```yaml\n# ArgoCD Application (argocd/application.yaml) — multi-source\nspec:\n  sources:\n    - repoURL: https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-modules\n      path: helm/base-service-chart\n      targetRevision: v1.0.0          # Pin to base chart version tag\n      helm:\n        valueFiles:\n          - $values/helm/values.yaml\n          - $values/helm/values-dev.yaml\n    - repoURL: https://github.com/konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-iqportal\n      targetRevision: main\n      ref: values\n```\n\n### Base Chart Versioning\n\n- Source of truth is the `kix-platform-modules` Git repo\n- Version pinning via Git tags (e.g. `v1.0.0`, `v1.1.0`)\n- ArgoCD `targetRevision` points to the desired tag\n- Renovate automates version bumps across all workload repos\n- Breaking changes require major version bump"
}

     8→# Application Migration
     9→
    10→This section provides a comprehensive guide for migrating services from **GCP Cloud Run** to the **kix-infrastructure** Kubernetes platform. The migration adopts modern cloud-native patterns including Helm charts, GitOps-driven deployments, and a unified CI/CD pipeline.
    11→
    12→## Executive Summary
    13→
    14→The platform is migrating approximately **24 microservices** from Cloud Run to a Kubernetes-native architecture. This migration delivers:
    15→
    16→- **Standardised packaging** with Helm charts for declarative Kubernetes deployment
    17→- **Secure container builds** with multi-stage Docker, vulnerability scanning, and image signing
    18→- **Unified CI/CD** via GitHub Actions for build/scan/push and ArgoCD for GitOps deployments
    19→- **Developer portal** via Backstage for service catalog, scaffolding, and documentation
    20→- **Dual ingress architecture** with Kong for APIs and GKE Gateway API + IAP for frontends
    21→
    22→**Key principles**: Simple, secure, auditable, repeatable.
    23→
    24→## Migration Scope
    25→
    26→### In Scope (24 Services)
    27→
    28→| Category | Count | Stack |
    29→|----------|-------|-------|
    30→| MCP Servers | 14 | Python (FastMCP) |
    31→| Business Apps | 4 | Python (FastAPI) + Node.js (Nuxt 3) |
    32→| Data Pipelines | 3 | Python |
    33→| Bots | 1 | Python |
    34→| Prototypes | 2 | Python |
    35→
    36→### Out of Scope
    37→
    38→- **CrewAI Flows & Tools** (12) — remain on current platform
    39→- **Infrastructure Repos** (4) — handled separately
    40→- **Config/Proxies** (2) — remain as-is

## Approved Plan:
# Plan: Remove Base Chart + OCI, Standalone Workload Charts, Org Rename

## Context

Three interrelated changes across the app-migration docs:

1. **Remove base-service-chart entirely** — no shared library chart, no OCI, no external dependency. Each workload repo contains a **standalone Helm chart** with its own templates and values. ArgoCD syncs from the workload repo over Git HTTPS.

2. **Org rename**: `konecta-ix-apps` → `konecta-ix-applications` across all docs.

3. **Fix two previously broken files** (kubernetes-helm.md, gitops-promotion.md) that were incorrectly edited toward a multi-source ArgoCD pattern.

## Target Architecture

```
konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-<service>/
├── helm/
│   ├── Chart.yaml                # Standalone chart (no dependencies)
│   ├── templates/                # K8s resource templates
│   │   ├── deployment.yaml
│   │   ├── service.yaml
│   │   ├── hpa.yaml
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── values.yaml               # Service defaults
│   ├── values-dev.yaml
│   ├── values-qa.yaml
│   └── values-prod.yaml
├── argocd/
│   └── application.yaml          # Single-source ArgoCD Application
├── terraform/
│   └── ...
└── .github/workflows/
    └── deploy.yaml
```

Key points:
- **No base-service-chart** — each chart is self-contained
- **No `base-service-chart:` values prefix** — values are at the top level
- **No Chart.yaml `dependencies:` block**
- **ArgoCD single source** over Git HTTPS: `repoURL: https://github.com/konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-<service>`

## Changes by File

### 1. `docs/app-migration/kubernetes-helm.md` — Major rewrite (lines 14–83)

Currently broken (has multi-source ArgoCD from previous edit). Rewrite the Helm strategy section:
- Remove "Two-Repo Architecture" / base chart layer diagram → replace with workload repo standalone chart structure
- Remove "Base Chart" section → replace with standalone chart description showing templates
- Remove "Per-Service Values" multi-source section → show Chart.yaml without dependencies
- Remove "Base Chart Versioning" section
- Remove `base-service-chart:` prefix concept
- Fix org reference: `konecta-ix-apps` → `konecta-ix-applications` (line 38)

### 2. `docs/app-migration/gitops-promotion.md` — Fix structure + values

- Lines 34-52: Add `Chart.yaml` + `templates/` to workload repo structure, remove multi-source note
- Line 41: Change `(multi-source)` comment back to just "ArgoCD Application manifest"
- Lines 50-52: Remove the `:::note` about multi-source
- Line 60: Remove `base-service-chart:` prefix from values example, bring values to top level
- Line 20: `konecta-ix-apps` → `konecta-ix-applications`

### 3. `docs/app-migration/service-guides/iq-portal.md`

- Line 115: Remove prerequisite about base chart published to AR
- Lines 370-381: Rewrite Chart.yaml — remove `dependencies:` block, keep as standalone
- Line 386: Remove `base-service-chart:` prefix from values.yaml, bring all values to top level
- Line 640: Remove `base-service-chart:` prefix from values-dev.yaml, bring to top level

### 4. `docs/app-migration/target-architecture.md`

- Line 81: `konecta-ix-apps` → `konecta-ix-applications` (+ 3 other occurrences)
- Line 108: `Shared Terraform modules + Helm base chart` → `Shared Terraform modules`
- Lines 148-168: Update workload repo structure — add `templates/`, remove `Chart.yaml # Depends on base-service-chart (OCI)` → just `Chart.yaml`
- Line 306: Remove or rephrase "Shared base Helm chart" design decision row

### 5. `docs/app-migration/migration-phases.md`

- Line 37: Remove "Add base Helm chart / Publish to Artifact Registry as OCI chart" row, or change to "Create workload repo Helm chart template"
- Line 57: Rephrase "Fix any issues in base chart" → "Fix any issues in Helm charts"

### 6. `docs/app-migration/backstage-onboarding.md`

- Line 45: `konecta-ix-apps` → `konecta-ix-applications`
- Line 48: `konecta-ix-apps` → `konecta-ix-applications`
- Line 286: `helm/Chart.yaml depends on base-service-chart` → `helm/Chart.yaml and templates/ configured`

### 7. `docs/app-migration/appendix-reference.md`

- Lines 128-134: `konecta-ix-apps` → `konecta-ix-applications` (6 occurrences)
- Line 101: `Shared Terraform modules + Helm base chart` → `Shared Terraform modules`

### 8. `docs/app-migration/cicd-pipeline.md`

- Line 16: `konecta-ix-apps` → `konecta-ix-applications`

### 9. `docs/app-migration/current-state.md`

- Lines 60-61: `konecta-ix-apps` → `konecta-ix-applications`

### 10. `docs/app-migration/index.md`

- Line 83: `konecta-ix-apps` → `konecta-ix-applications` (both text and URL)

### 11. `docs/app-migration/operations-risks.md`

- Line 58: Rephrase "Base chart library reduces per-service overhead" → remove or update rationale

## Files NOT Changed

- `docs/crewai/*` — CrewAI's external OCI registry, unrelated
- `docs/app-migration/security.md` — "OCI annotation" = container image SBOMs
- `docs/developer-guide/*` — Docker image registry refs, not Helm
- `docs/infrastructure-ops/*` — Docker image mirrors
- `docs/reference/module-catalog.md` — references kix-platform-modules for Terraform/Helm modules generally
- `CLAUDE.md` — no `konecta-ix-apps` or base-service-chart references

## Verification

1. `npm run build` — Docusaurus validates links
2. `grep -r "base-service-chart" docs/app-migration/` → 0 results
3. `grep -r "oci://europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev/kd-ix-platform/helm-charts" docs/` → 0 results
4. `grep -r "konecta-ix-apps" docs/` → 0 results
5. `grep -r "multi-source" docs/app-migration/` → 0 results
6. `grep -r "type: library" docs/app-migration/` → 0 results

     6→---
     7→
     8→# Kubernetes & Helm
     9→
    10→This document covers Helm chart design, namespace strategy, resource profiles, health probes, and autoscaling configuration.
    11→
    12→## Helm Chart Strategy
    13→
    14→### Two-Repo Architecture
    15→
    16→The platform uses a layered Helm architecture. The **base chart** lives in the platform modules Git repo and is composed with **per-service values** from workload repos via ArgoCD multi-source:
    17→
    18→```
    19→Base Chart (platform org — Git source of truth)
    20→         └── kix-platform-modules/helm/base-service-chart/
    21→             ├── Chart.yaml (type: application)
    22→             └── templates/
    23→                 ├── deployment.yaml
    24→                 ├── service.yaml
    25→                 ├── ingress.yaml
    26→                 └── ...
    27→
    28→Per-Service Values (workload repo)
    29→         └── konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-iqportal/helm/
    30→             ├── values.yaml (service defaults)
    31→             ├── values-dev.yaml (dev overrides)
    32→             ├── values-qa.yaml (qa overrides)
    33→             └── values-prod.yaml (prod overrides)
    34→```
    35→
    36→ArgoCD multi-source combines the chart from Git with values from the workload repo — no OCI registry needed for Helm charts.
    37→
    38→Code repos (konecta-ix-apps, konecta-ix-mcp-servers) contain **only source code and Dockerfiles** — no Helm charts or deployment configuration.
    39→
    40→### Base Chart
    41→
    42→The base chart is an **application chart** (`type: application`) in `kix-platform-modules/helm/base-service-chart/`. It is pulled directly from Git over HTTPS by ArgoCD — no OCI publish step required.
    43→
    44→Contains standard Kubernetes resource templates driven by values:
    45→
    46→| Template | Purpose |
    47→|----------|---------|
    48→| `deployment.yaml` | Pod spec, containers, sidecars |
    49→| `service.yaml` | K8s Service definitions |
    50→| `ingress.yaml` | Kong Ingress / HTTPRoute |
    51→| `hpa.yaml` | HorizontalPodAutoscaler |
    52→| `pdb.yaml` | PodDisruptionBudget |
    53→| `networkpolicy.yaml` | Network isolation |
    54→| `serviceaccount.yaml` | Workload Identity |
    55→| `external-secret.yaml` | External Secrets CRD |
    56→
    57→### Per-Service Values (in Workload Repo)
    58→
    59→Workload repos provide **values files only** — no `Chart.yaml` dependency block is needed. ArgoCD multi-source composes the base chart with service-specific values at sync time:
    60→
    61→```yaml
    62→# ArgoCD Application (argocd/application.yaml) — multi-source
    63→spec:
    64→  sources:
    65→    - repoURL: https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-modules
    66→      path: helm/base-service-chart
    67→      targetRevision: v1.0.0          # Pin to base chart version tag
    68→      helm:
    69→        valueFiles:
    70→          - $values/helm/values.yaml
    71→          - $values/helm/values-dev.yaml
    72→    - repoURL: https://github.com/konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-iqportal
    73→      targetRevision: main
    74→      ref: values
    75→```
    76→
    77→### Base Chart Versioning
    78→
    79→- Source of truth is the `kix-platform-modules` Git repo
    80→- Version pinning via Git tags (e.g. `v1.0.0`, `v1.1.0`)
    81→- ArgoCD `targetRevision` points to the desired tag
    82→- Renovate automates version bumps across all workload repos
    83→- Breaking changes require major version bump
    84→
    85→## Namespace Strategy
```

It is pulled directly from Git over HTTPS by ArgoCD — no OCI publish step required.\n\nContains standard Kubernetes resource templates driven by values:\n\n| Template | Purpose |\n|----------|---------|\n| `deployment.yaml` | Pod spec, containers, sidecars |\n| `service.yaml` | K8s Service definitions |\n| `ingress.yaml` | Kong Ingress / HTTPRoute |\n| `hpa.yaml` | HorizontalPodAutoscaler |\n| `pdb.yaml` | PodDisruptionBudget |\n| `networkpolicy.yaml` | Network isolation |\n| `serviceaccount.yaml` | Workload Identity |\n| `external-secret.yaml` | External Secrets CRD |\n\n### Per-Service Values (in Workload Repo)\n\nWorkload repos provide **values files only** — no `Chart.yaml` dependency block is needed. ArgoCD multi-source composes the base chart with service-specific values at sync time:\n\n```yaml\n# ArgoCD Application (argocd/application.yaml) — multi-source\nspec:\n  sources:\n    - repoURL: https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-modules\n      path: helm/base-service-chart\n      targetRevision: v1.0.0          # Pin to base chart version tag\n      helm:\n        valueFiles:\n          - $values/helm/values.yaml\n          - $values/helm/values-dev.yaml\n    - repoURL: https://github.com/konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-iqportal\n      targetRevision: main\n      ref: values\n```\n\n### Base Chart Versioning\n\n- Source of truth is the `kix-platform-modules` Git repo\n- Version pinning via Git tags (e.g. `v1.0.0`, `v1.1.0`)\n- ArgoCD `targetRevision` points to the desired tag\n- Renovate automates version bumps across all workload repos\n- Breaking changes require major version bump",
  "new_string": "### Two-Repo Architecture\n\nThe platform uses a **two-repo model**: code repos hold application source code, workload repos hold everything needed to deploy — Helm chart, ArgoCD Application, Terraform, and environment-specific values.\n\n```\nCode Repo (source code + CI only)\n         └── konecta-ix-applications/kix-app-iqportal/\n             ├── src/\n             ├── Dockerfile\n             └── .github/workflows/ci.yaml\n\nWorkload Repo (deployment — single source of truth)\n         └── konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-iqportal/\n             ├── helm/\n             │   ├── Chart.yaml           # Standalone chart (no dependencies)\n             │   ├── templates/           # K8s resource templates\n             │   ├── values.yaml          # Service defaults\n             │   ├── values-dev.yaml      # Dev overrides\n             │   ├── values-qa.yaml       # QA overrides\n             │   └── values-prod.yaml     # Prod overrides\n             ├── argocd/application.yaml  # ArgoCD Application\n             └── terraform/              # Service infrastructure\n```\n\nArgoCD syncs the workload repo directly over **Git HTTPS** — each chart is self-contained with no external dependencies.\n\nCode repos (konecta-ix-applications, konecta-ix-mcp-servers) contain **only source code and Dockerfiles** — no Helm charts or deployment configuration.\n\n### Workload Repo Helm Chart\n\nEach workload repo contains a **standalone Helm chart** in the `helm/` directory. The chart includes all Kubernetes resource templates directly — no shared base chart dependency.\n\nStandard templates included per chart:\n\n| Template | Purpose |\n|----------|---------|\n| `deployment.yaml` | Pod spec, containers, sidecars |\n| `service.yaml` | K8s Service definitions |\n| `ingress.yaml` | Kong Ingress / HTTPRoute |\n| `hpa.yaml` | HorizontalPodAutoscaler |\n| `pdb.yaml` | PodDisruptionBudget |\n| `networkpolicy.yaml` | Network isolation |\n| `serviceaccount.yaml` | Workload Identity |\n| `external-secret.yaml` | External Secrets CRD |\n\n### Chart.yaml\n\nEach workload chart is a standalone application chart with no external dependencies:\n\n```yaml\n# helm/Chart.yaml (in kix-workload-iqportal)\napiVersion: v2\nname: kix-workload-iqportal\nversion: 0.1.0\ntype: application\n```\n\n### Chart Scaffolding\n\nNew workload repos are scaffolded from the `kix-platform-workload-template` repo (or via Backstage Software Templates), which includes a standard set of Helm templates. Teams can customise templates as needed for their service."

     6→---
     7→
     8→# GitOps & Promotion
     9→
    10→This document covers the ArgoCD GitOps flow, environment promotion strategy, and rollback procedures.
    11→
    12→## GitOps Flow
    13→
    14→### Per-Workload Repository Model
    15→
    16→Each service has its own **workload repo** in `konecta-ix-workloads` that ArgoCD watches directly. There is no centralized GitOps repository for application deployments.
    17→
    18→```
    19→CODE REPO                              WORKLOAD REPO
    20→konecta-ix-apps/                       konecta-ix-workloads/
    21→kix-app-iqportal                       kix-workload-iqportal
    22→────────────────                       ─────────────────────
    23→1. PR merged to develop
    24→2. Pipeline builds sha-abc1234
    25→3. Image pushed to Artifact Registry
    26→4. Developer or automation updates ──▶ 5. values-dev.yaml
    27→   image tag in workload repo              image.tag: sha-abc1234
    28→                                        6. ArgoCD detects change → syncs dev
    29→```
    30→
    31→### Workload Repository Structure
    32→
    33→```
    34→kix-workload-iqportal/
    35→├── helm/
    36→│   ├── values.yaml             # Service defaults (all envs)
    37→│   ├── values-dev.yaml         # Dev overrides (image tag, replicas, env vars)
    38→│   ├── values-qa.yaml          # QA overrides
    39→│   └── values-prod.yaml        # Prod overrides
    40→├── argocd/
    41→│   └── application.yaml        # ArgoCD Application manifest (multi-source)
    42→├── terraform/
    43→│   ├── main.tf                 # Service accounts, IAM, secrets
    44→│   ├── variables.tf
    45→│   └── backend.tf
    46→└── .github/workflows/
    47→    └── deploy.yaml             # Terraform validate-plan-apply
    48→```
    49→
    50→:::note
    51→Workload repos contain **values files only** — no `Chart.yaml` dependency block. The base chart is pulled directly from the `kix-platform-modules` Git repo via ArgoCD multi-source.
    52→:::
    53→
    54→### Environment Values File
    55→
    56→Each environment has a values override file in the workload repo:
    57→
    58→```yaml
    59→# helm/values-dev.yaml
    60→base-service-chart:
    61→  image:
    62→    tag: "sha-abc1234"  # Updated on each deployment
    63→
    64→  containers:
    65→    app:
    66→      env:
    67→        NODE_ENV: "development"
    68→        LOG_LEVEL: "debug"
    69→
    70→  autoscaling:
    71→    minReplicas: 1
    72→    maxReplicas: 2
    73→```
    74→
    75→## ArgoCD Configuration
```

   108→## 3. Pre-requisites
   109→
   110→Before starting, ensure:
   111→
   112→- [ ] Access to `konecta-ix-applications` GitHub org (write) — for code repo
   113→- [ ] Access to `konecta-ix-workloads` GitHub org (write) — for workload repo
   114→- [ ] Access to `konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-ci-workflows` (read)
   115→- [ ] `kix-platform-modules` base Helm chart published to Artifact Registry
   116→- [ ] Shared Kong gateway operational in `shared-kong` namespace
   117→- [ ] GKE Gateway API + IAP configured on frontend LB
   118→- [ ] GCP Workload Identity pool configured for GitHub Actions OIDC
   119→- [ ] Backstage operational in `shared-backstage` namespace

     1→---
     2→title: CI/CD Pipeline
     3→sidebar_label: CI/CD Pipeline
     4→sidebar_position: 8
     5→description: GitHub Actions pipeline stages, security gates, and scanning
     6→---
     7→
     8→# CI/CD Pipeline
     9→
    10→This document covers the GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline architecture, stages, and security gates.
    11→
    12→## Pipeline Architecture
    13→
    14→The platform uses a **two-repo CI/CD model**:
    15→
    16→- **Code repos** (konecta-ix-applications, konecta-ix-mcp-servers, konecta-ix-demos) run the **build pipeline** — lint, test, build, scan, sign, and push Docker images to Artifact Registry
    17→- **Workload repos** (konecta-ix-workloads) run the **deploy pipeline** — Terraform apply for infrastructure and secrets, with ArgoCD handling Helm-based deployments
    18→
    19→### Shared Workflows Repository
    20→
    21→```
    22→kix-platform-ci-workflows/
    23→└── .github/workflows/
    24→    ├── standard-pipeline.yaml      # Main orchestrator (code repos)
    25→    ├── _lint-and-test.yaml         # Language-aware lint + unit tests
    26→    ├── _secret-scan.yaml           # Trivy filesystem secret detection
    27→    ├── _sca.yaml                   # Dependency-Track SCA analysis
    28→    ├── _sast.yaml                  # SonarQube static analysis
    29→    ├── _build-image.yaml           # Docker build + BuildKit cache
    30→    ├── _container-scan-sign.yaml   # Trivy image scan + SBOM + Cosign
    31→    ├── _push-registry.yaml         # Push to Artifact Registry
    32→    ├── _promote.yaml               # Promote between environments
    33→    └── _dast.yaml                  # OWASP ZAP baseline scan
    34→```
    35→
    36→### Code Repo CI Workflow
    37→
    38→Every code repo uses this minimal workflow file to call the shared pipeline:
    39→
    40→```yaml
    41→# .github/workflows/ci.yaml
    42→name: CI
    43→on:
    44→  push:
    45→    branches: [develop, main]
    46→  pull_request:
    47→    branches: [main]
    48→  workflow_dispatch:
    49→
    50→permissions:
    51→  contents: read
    52→  id-token: write
    53→  security-events: write
    54→
    55→jobs:
    56→  pipeline:
    57→    uses: konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-ci-workflows/.github/workflows/standard-pipeline.yaml@v1
    58→    with:
    59→      service-name: ${{ github.event.repository.name }}
    60→      dockerfile-path: ./Dockerfile
    61→      python-version: "3.11"     # or node-version: "22"
    62→    secrets: inherit
    63→```
    64→
    65→:::note
    66→Code repos do **not** contain Helm charts or deployment configuration. The `chart-path` parameter is not used. All deployment data lives in the corresponding workload repo.
    67→:::
    68→
    69→### Workload Repo Deploy Workflow
    70→
    71→Each workload repo has a Terraform deploy workflow:
    72→
    73→```yaml
    74→# .github/workflows/deploy.yaml
    75→name: Deploy
    76→on:
    77→  workflow_dispatch:
    78→    inputs:
    79→      environment:
    80→        description: Target environment
    81→        required: true
    82→        type: choice
    83→        options: [dev, qa, prod]
    84→
    85→jobs:
    86→  terraform:
    87→    environment: ${{ inputs.environment }}
    88→    steps:
    89→      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
    90→      - uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
    91→        with:
    92→          workload_identity_provider: ${{ secrets.WIF_PROVIDER }}
    93→          service_account: ${{ secrets.WIF_SA }}
    94→      - run: |
    95→          cd terraform
    96→          terraform init
    97→          terraform plan \
    98→            -var="environment=${{ inputs.environment }}" \
    99→            -var="api_key=${{ secrets.TF_VARS_API_KEY }}"
   100→          terraform apply -auto-approve
   101→```
   102→
   103→## Pipeline Stages
   104→
   105→### Code Pipeline (Every PR and Merge)
   106→
   107→```
   108→┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐
   109→│  1. LINT &   │──│  2. SECRET   │──│  3. SCA      │──│  4. SAST     │──│  5. BUILD &  │
   110→│     TEST     │  │     SCAN     │  │              │  │              │  │  UNIT TEST   │
   111→└──────────────┘  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘
   112→  PR + merge        PR + merge        PR + merge        PR + merge        merge only
   113→  • ruff/eslint     • Trivy fs        • Syft SBOM       • SonarQube       • BuildKit
   114→  • type checks     • --scanners      • generation      • analysis        • multi-stage
   115→  • pip audit/        secret          • Dependency-     • quality gate:   • unit tests
   116→    npm audit       • stops on          Track upload     no critical/    • OCI labels
   117→                      any finding     • stops on           high issues
   118→                                        critical/high
   119→
   120→┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐
   121→│  6. CONTAINER│──│  7. PUSH &   │
   122→│  SCAN & SIGN │  │  REGISTRY    │
   123→└──────────────┘  └──────────────┘
   124→  merge only        merge only
   125→  • Trivy image     • Push to AR
   126→  • scan            • Tag: sha-xxx
   127→  • SBOM attach     • Tag: v1.2.3
   128→  • (Syft)            (on git tag)
   129→  • Cosign sign
   130→    (OIDC)
   131→```
   132→
   133→### When Stages Run
   134→
   135→| Stage | On PR | On Merge | Purpose |
   136→|-------|-------|----------|---------|
   137→| 1. Lint & Test | ✓ | ✓ | Fast feedback on code quality |
   138→| 2. Secret Scan | ✓ | ✓ | Block secrets before commit |
   139→| 3. SCA | ✓ | ✓ | Dependency vulnerability check |
   140→| 4. SAST | ✓ | ✓ | Static code analysis |
   141→| 5. Build & Test | ✗ | ✓ | Docker image build |
   142→| 6. Container Scan | ✗ | ✓ | Image vulnerability scan + sign |
   143→| 7. Push | ✗ | ✓ | Push to Artifact Registry |
   144→
   145→:::note
   146→Stage 8 (GitOps update) from the previous centralized model has been replaced. Image tag updates are now made directly in the workload repo's `values-{env}.yaml` file, either manually or via automation.
   147→:::
   148→
   149→## Security Gates
   150→
   151→All gates are **fail-stop** — pipeline halts immediately on critical/high findings.
   152→
   153→### Gate Details
   154→
   155→| Gate | Tool | Stage | Trigger | Action on Failure |
   156→|------|------|-------|---------|-------------------|
   157→| **Secret Detection** | Trivy (`--scanners secret`) | 2 | Every PR + merge | Stop pipeline, no exceptions |
   158→| **Dependency Vulnerabilities** | Dependency-Track (via Syft SBOM) | 3 | Every PR + merge | Stop on critical/high |
   159→| **SAST Quality Gate** | SonarQube | 4 | Every PR + merge | Stop on critical/high |
   160→| **Container Vulnerabilities** | Trivy (image scan) | 6 | Every merge | Stop on critical/high |
   161→| **Image Signature** | Cosign (Sigstore/OIDC) | 6 | Every merge | Unsigned images blocked |
   162→| **DAST Baseline** | OWASP ZAP | Post-deploy | Before prod promotion | Block promotion on findings |
   163→| **Admission Control** | Kyverno | Deploy-time | Every sync | Reject unsigned images |
   164→
   165→### Tool Configuration
   166→
   167→#### Trivy Secret Scan
   168→
   169→Scans source filesystem before any build:
   170→
   171→```yaml
   172→- name: Secret Scan
   173→  run: |
   174→    trivy fs --scanners secret --exit-code 1 .
   175→```
   176→
   177→Zero tolerance — any finding stops the pipeline.
   178→
   179→#### SonarQube
   180→
   181→Hosted in `shared-devsecops` namespace:
   182→
   183→- Runs static analysis on every PR
   184→- Quality gate: no new critical or high severity issues
   185→- Results posted as PR comment
   186→
   187→#### Dependency-Track
   188→
   189→SBOM-based vulnerability tracking:
   190→
   191→- Syft generates CycloneDX SBOMs
   192→- Uploaded to Dependency-Track for continuous monitoring
   193→- Pipeline stops on critical/high vulnerabilities
   194→
   195→#### Cosign Image Signing
   196→
   197→Keyless signing via GitHub OIDC → Sigstore:
   198→
   199→```yaml
   200→- name: Sign Image
   201→  run: |
   202→    cosign sign --yes $IMAGE_REF
   203→```
   204→
   205→No long-lived keys — fully automatic.
   206→
   207→### Vulnerability Remediation SLAs
   208→
   209→Per the Konecta DevSecOps Handbook:
   210→
   211→| Severity | Detection → Triage | Triage → Fix | Fix → Deploy |
   212→|----------|-------------------|--------------|--------------|
   213→| Critical | 4 hours | 24 hours | 48 hours |
   214→| High | 24 hours | 7 days | 14 days |
   215→| Medium | 7 days | 30 days | 45 days |
   216→| Low | 30 days | 90 days | Next release |
   217→
   218→## Image Tagging Strategy
   219→
   220→| Tag | When | Purpose |
   221→|-----|------|---------|
   222→| `sha-{7-char}` | Every build | Immutable build identifier |
   223→| `v{major}.{minor}.{patch}` | On git tag | Release version |
   224→| `{env}-latest`| On promotion | Environment pointer (mutable) |
   225→
   226→**Rule**: SHA tags are immutable. Never overwrite. Promotion copies the SHA tag reference, not the image.
   227→
   228→## Secrets Management (CI)
   229→
   230→### GitHub OIDC → GCP Workload Identity
   231→
   232→No JSON keys — fully automated authentication:
   233→
   234→```yaml
   235→- name: Authenticate to GCP
   236→  uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
   237→  with:
   238→    workload_identity_provider: ${{ secrets.WIF_PROVIDER }}
   239→    service_account: ${{ secrets.WIF_SA }}
   240→```
   241→
   242→| Property | Value |
   243→|----------|-------|
   244→| Token lifetime | ~1 hour |
   245→| Auto-refreshing | Yes |
   246→| Audit trail | Full via Cloud Audit Logs |
   247→
   248→### Build Secrets
   249→
   250→For build-time secrets (never in image layers):
   251→
   252→```dockerfile
   253→RUN --mount=type=secret,id=npm_token \
   254→    NPM_TOKEN=$(cat /run/secrets/npm_token) npm ci
   255→```
   256→
   257→```yaml
   258→- name: Build
   259→  run: |
   260→    docker build --secret id=npm_token,src=${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }} .
   261→```
   262→
   263→### Workload Repo Secrets (TF_VARS_)
   264→
   265→Static secrets for deployed services are stored as GitHub Actions secrets on the **workload repo**, prefixed with `TF_VARS_`. These are passed to Terraform which creates Kubernetes secrets and GCP Secret Manager entries. See [Target Architecture — Secrets Management](target-architecture#secrets-management-in-workload-repos) for details.
   266→
   267→## Example Pipeline Run
   268→
   269→```
   270→1. Developer pushes to feature branch in code repo
   271→2. PR opened to develop or main
   272→3. Pipeline runs stages 1-4 (lint, secret scan, SCA, SAST)
   273→4. PR review and approval
   274→5. Merge to develop (for dev) or main (for qa)
   275→6. Pipeline runs all stages 1-7
   276→7. Image built, scanned, signed, pushed to Artifact Registry
   277→8. Developer updates image tag in workload repo `values-{env}.yaml`
   278→9. ArgoCD detects change and syncs to target namespace
   279→10. Service deployed and running
   280→```
   281→
   282→## Required Repository Configuration
   283→
   284→### Code Repo — Variables (Settings → Actions → Variables)
   285→
   286→| Variable | Example |
   287→|----------|---------|
   288→| `VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` | `805102662749-...` (for Node.js builds) |
   289→
   290→### Code Repo — Secrets (Inherited from Org)
   291→
   292→| Secret | Description |
   293→|--------|-------------|
   294→| `GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER` | Workload Identity pool provider |
   295→| `GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` | Service account for CI |
   296→
   297→### Workload Repo — Secrets (Per GitHub Environment)
   298→
   299→| Secret | Description |
   300→|--------|-------------|
   301→| `GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER` | Workload Identity pool provider |
   302→| `GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` | Service account for Terraform |
   303→| `TF_VARS_*` | Per-environment static secrets for Terraform |
   304→
   305→### Branch → Environment Mapping
   306→
   307→| Branch | Environment | Namespace |
   308→|--------|-------------|-----------|
   309→| `develop` | dev | `dev-api-services` |
   310→| `main` | qa | `qa-api-services` |
   311→| `v*` tags | prod | `prod-api-services` |
   312→
   313→---
   314→
   315→**Next**: [GitOps & Promotion](gitops-promotion) — ArgoCD GitOps flow and environment promotion.
   316→
```

     1→---
     2→title: GitOps & Promotion
     3→sidebar_label: GitOps & Promotion
     4→sidebar_position: 9
     5→description: ArgoCD GitOps flow, environment promotion, and rollback procedures
     6→---
     7→
     8→# GitOps & Promotion
     9→
    10→This document covers the ArgoCD GitOps flow, environment promotion strategy, and rollback procedures.
    11→
    12→## GitOps Flow
    13→
    14→### Per-Workload Repository Model
    15→
    16→Each service has its own **workload repo** in `konecta-ix-workloads` that ArgoCD watches directly. There is no centralized GitOps repository for application deployments.
    17→
    18→```
    19→CODE REPO                              WORKLOAD REPO
    20→konecta-ix-applications/                konecta-ix-workloads/
    21→kix-app-iqportal                       kix-workload-iqportal
    22→────────────────                       ─────────────────────
    23→1. PR merged to develop
    24→2. Pipeline builds sha-abc1234
    25→3. Image pushed to Artifact Registry
    26→4. Developer or automation updates ──▶ 5. values-dev.yaml
    27→   image tag in workload repo              image.tag: sha-abc1234
    28→                                        6. ArgoCD detects change → syncs dev
    29→```
    30→
    31→### Workload Repository Structure
    32→
    33→```
    34→kix-workload-iqportal/
    35→├── helm/
    36→│   ├── Chart.yaml              # Standalone chart (no external dependencies)
    37→│   ├── templates/              # K8s resource templates
    38→│   ├── values.yaml             # Service defaults (all envs)
    39→│   ├── values-dev.yaml         # Dev overrides (image tag, replicas, env vars)
    40→│   ├── values-qa.yaml          # QA overrides
    41→│   └── values-prod.yaml        # Prod overrides
    42→├── argocd/
    43→│   └── application.yaml        # ArgoCD Application manifest
    44→├── terraform/
    45→│   ├── main.tf                 # Service accounts, IAM, secrets
    46→│   ├── variables.tf
    47→│   └── backend.tf
    48→└── .github/workflows/
    49→    └── deploy.yaml             # Terraform validate-plan-apply
    50→```
    51→
    52→### Environment Values File
    53→
    54→Each environment has a values override file in the workload repo:
    55→
    56→```yaml
    57→# helm/values-dev.yaml
    58→image:
    59→  tag: "sha-abc1234"  # Updated on each deployment
    60→
    61→containers:
    62→  app:
    63→    env:
    64→      NODE_ENV: "development"
    65→      LOG_LEVEL: "debug"
    66→
    67→autoscaling:
    68→  minReplicas: 1
    69→  maxReplicas: 2
    70→```
    71→
    72→## ArgoCD Configuration
    73→
    74→### Per-Workload ArgoCD Application
    75→
    76→Each workload repo contains its own ArgoCD Application manifest. ArgoCD watches the repo directly:
    77→
    78→```yaml
    79→# argocd/application.yaml
    80→apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
    81→kind: Application
    82→metadata:
    83→  name: kix-app-iqportal-dev
    84→  namespace: shared-argocd
    85→spec:
    86→  project: dev-project
    87→  source:
    88→    repoURL: https://github.com/konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-iqportal
    89→    path: helm
    90→    targetRevision: main
    91→    helm:
    92→      valueFiles:
    93→        - values.yaml
    94→        - values-dev.yaml
    95→  destination:
    96→    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    97→    namespace: dev-api-services
    98→  syncPolicy:
    99→    automated:
   100→      prune: true
   101→      selfHeal: true
   102→    syncOptions:
   103→      - CreateNamespace=false
   104→```
   105→
   106→:::note
   107→Multiple ArgoCD Application manifests can exist in the same workload repo (one per environment), or environments can be managed via separate branches/tags. The example above shows the single-manifest approach with environment-specific value files.
   108→:::
   109→
   110→### Sync Policies by Environment
   111→
   112→| Environment | Sync Mode | When |
   113→|-------------|-----------|------|
   114→| **Dev** | `automated` (auto-sync) | 24/7 |
   115→| **QA** | `automated: false` (manual) | 08:00-18:00 UTC |
   116→| **Prod** | `automated: false` (manual) | Tue-Thu 20:00-23:00 UTC |
   117→
   118→### ArgoCD Projects
   119→
   120→RBAC isolation per environment:
   121→
   122→```yaml
   123→apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
   124→kind: AppProject
   125→metadata:
   126→  name: dev-project
   127→  namespace: shared-argocd
   128→spec:
   129→  description: Development environment
   130→  sourceRepos:
   131→    - 'https://github.com/konecta-ix-workloads/*'
   132→    - 'https://github.com/konecta-ix-services/*'
   133→  destinations:
   134→    - namespace: 'dev-*'
   135→      server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
   136→  clusterResourceWhitelist:
   137→    - group: ''
   138→      kind: Namespace
   139→```
   140→
   141→## Environment Promotion
   142→
   143→### Promotion Workflow
   144→
   145→Promotion updates the image tag in the target environment's values file within the workload repo:
   146→
   147→```
   148→Dev (values-dev.yaml)  →  QA (values-qa.yaml)  →  Prod (values-prod.yaml)
   149→  sha-abc1234                sha-abc1234               sha-abc1234
   150→```
   151→
   152→### Dev → QA Promotion
   153→
   154→1. Verify service is healthy in dev
   155→2. Update `helm/values-qa.yaml` with the image tag from dev:
   156→   ```bash
   157→   # In kix-workload-iqportal
   158→   # Update image.tag in values-qa.yaml to match values-dev.yaml
   159→   ```
   160→3. Create PR, review, merge
   161→4. ArgoCD syncs to QA (manual sync during change window)
   162→
   163→### QA → Prod Promotion (with DAST)
   164→
   165→1. Verify service is healthy in QA
   166→2. Run **OWASP ZAP baseline scan** against QA endpoint
   167→3. If ZAP finds vulnerabilities → promotion blocked, findings reported
   168→4. If ZAP passes → update `helm/values-prod.yaml` with the image tag
   169→5. Create PR with approval requirement
   170→6. After merge, ArgoCD syncs to prod (manual sync during change window)
   171→
   172→### Change Windows
   173→
   174→| Environment | Window | Notes |
   175→|-------------|--------|-------|
   176→| **Dev** | 24/7 | Auto-approve allowed |
   177→| **QA** | 08:00-18:00 UTC (Mon-Fri) | Manual approval required |
   178→| **Prod** | Tue-Thu 20:00-23:00 UTC | Manual approval + change ticket |
   179→
   180→## Rollback Procedures
   181→
   182→### Manual Rollback via Git (Recommended)
   183→
   184→Fastest rollback method — revert the image tag change in the workload repo:
   185→
   186→```bash
   187→cd kix-workload-iqportal
   188→
   189→# Revert the last commit (image tag update)
   190→git revert HEAD
   191→git push
   192→
   193→# ArgoCD auto-syncs (dev) or manual sync (qa/prod)
   194→```
   195→
   196→### Manual Rollback via kubectl
   197→
   198→For emergency when git is unavailable:
   199→
   200→```bash
   201→# Roll back to previous ReplicaSet
   202→kubectl rollout undo deployment/kix-app-iqportal -n dev-api-services
   203→
   204→# Verify
   205→kubectl rollout status deployment/kix-app-iqportal -n dev-api-services
   206→```
   207→
   208→:::warning
   209→kubectl rollback doesn't update Git — reconcile Git state in the workload repo after emergency.
   210→:::
   211→
   212→### ArgoCD Rollback
   213→
   214→Via ArgoCD UI or CLI:
   215→
   216→```bash
   217→# List recent syncs
   218→argocd app history kix-app-iqportal-dev
   219→
   220→# Rollback to specific revision
   221→argocd app rollback kix-app-iqportal-dev <revision>
   222→```
   223→
   224→## Sync Waves
   225→
   226→Resources deploy in order via sync waves:
   227→
   228→| Wave | Resources |
   229→|------|-----------|
   230→| 0 | Namespaces, RBAC, SecretStores |
   231→| 5 | ConfigMaps, Secrets |
   232→| 10 | Deployments, Services, HPA |
   233→| 15 | Ingress, NetworkPolicies |
   234→
   235→Example annotation:
   236→
   237→```yaml
   238→metadata:
   239→  annotations:
   240→    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "10"
   241→```
   242→
   243→## Health Checks
   244→
   245→ArgoCD monitors resource health:
   246→
   247→| Resource | Health Check |
   248→|----------|--------------|
   249→| Deployment | All replicas ready |
   250→| Service | Endpoints exist |
   251→| Ingress | Address assigned |
   252→| HPA | Current replicas within bounds |
   253→
   254→## Notifications
   255→
   256→ArgoCD notifications on sync events:
   257→
   258→| Event | Channel | Recipients |
   259→|-------|---------|------------|
   260→| Sync success | Slack #deployments | Team channel |
   261→| Sync failure | Slack #deployments + PagerDuty | Team + On-call |
   262→| Health degraded | Slack #alerts | Team channel |
   263→| Prod deployment | Slack #prod-changes | Wider audience |
   264→
   265→### Example Notification Template
   266→
   267→```yaml
   268→apiVersion: v1
   269→kind: ConfigMap
   270→metadata:
   271→  name: argocd-notifications-cm
   272→data:
   273→  template.app-sync-succeeded: |
   274→    message: |
   275→      Application {{.app.metadata.name}} sync succeeded.
   276→      Revision: {{.app.status.sync.revision}}
   277→      Environment: {{.app.spec.destination.namespace}}
   278→```
   279→
   280→## Disaster Recovery
   281→
   282→### Multi-Region Failover
   283→
   284→1. Secondary GKE cluster in eu-west4 (pre-provisioned)
   285→2. DNS-based failover to secondary cluster
   286→3. ArgoCD can deploy to secondary from same workload repo Git state
   287→
   288→### Recovery Steps
   289→
   290→1. Detect primary failure (health check timeout)
   291→2. Update DNS to point to secondary LB
   292→3. ArgoCD in secondary syncs from workload repos
   293→4. Services running on secondary within 15 minutes
   294→
   295→### State Recovery
   296→
   297→Application state in managed services (Cloud SQL, GCS) — replicated separately.
   298→
   299→---
   300→
   301→**Next**: [Backstage & Onboarding](backstage-onboarding) — Developer portal and service onboarding.
   302→
