     1→---
     2→title: Kubernetes & Helm
     3→sidebar_label: Kubernetes & Helm
     4→sidebar_position: 5
     5→description: Helm chart strategy, namespace design, resource profiles, and autoscaling
     6→---
     7→
     8→# Kubernetes & Helm
     9→
    10→This document covers Helm chart design, namespace strategy, resource profiles, health probes, and autoscaling configuration.
    11→
    12→## Helm Chart Strategy
    13→
    14→### Two-Repo Architecture
    15→
    16→The platform uses a **two-repo model**: code repos hold application source code, workload repos hold everything needed to deploy — Helm chart, ArgoCD Application, Terraform, and environment-specific values.
    17→
    18→```
    19→Code Repo (source code + CI only)
    20→         └── konecta-ix-applications/kix-app-iqportal/
    21→             ├── src/
    22→             ├── Dockerfile
    23→             └── .github/workflows/ci.yaml
    24→
    25→Workload Repo (deployment — single source of truth)
    26→         └── konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-iqportal/
    27→             ├── helm/
    28→             │   ├── Chart.yaml           # Standalone chart (no dependencies)
    29→             │   ├── templates/           # K8s resource templates
    30→             │   ├── values.yaml          # Service defaults
    31→             │   ├── values-dev.yaml      # Dev overrides
    32→             │   ├── values-qa.yaml       # QA overrides
    33→             │   └── values-prod.yaml     # Prod overrides
    34→             ├── argocd/application.yaml  # ArgoCD Application
    35→             └── terraform/              # Service infrastructure
    36→```
    37→
    38→ArgoCD syncs the workload repo directly over **Git HTTPS** — each chart is self-contained with no external dependencies.
    39→
    40→Code repos (konecta-ix-applications, konecta-ix-mcp-servers) contain **only source code and Dockerfiles** — no Helm charts or deployment configuration.
    41→
    42→### Workload Repo Helm Chart
    43→
    44→Each workload repo contains a **standalone Helm chart** in the `helm/` directory. The chart includes all Kubernetes resource templates directly — no shared base chart dependency.
    45→
    46→Standard templates included per chart:
    47→
    48→| Template | Purpose |
    49→|----------|---------|
    50→| `deployment.yaml` | Pod spec, containers, sidecars |
    51→| `service.yaml` | K8s Service definitions |
    52→| `ingress.yaml` | Kong Ingress / HTTPRoute |
    53→| `hpa.yaml` | HorizontalPodAutoscaler |
    54→| `pdb.yaml` | PodDisruptionBudget |
    55→| `networkpolicy.yaml` | Network isolation |
    56→| `serviceaccount.yaml` | Workload Identity |
    57→| `external-secret.yaml` | External Secrets CRD |
    58→
    59→### Chart.yaml
    60→
    61→Each workload chart is a standalone application chart with no external dependencies:
    62→
    63→```yaml
    64→# helm/Chart.yaml (in kix-workload-iqportal)
    65→apiVersion: v2
    66→name: kix-workload-iqportal
    67→version: 0.1.0
    68→type: application
    69→```
    70→
    71→### Chart Scaffolding
    72→
    73→New workload repos are scaffolded from the `kix-platform-workload-template` repo (or via Backstage Software Templates), which includes a standard set of Helm templates. Teams can customise templates as needed for their service.
    74→
    75→## Namespace Strategy
    76→
    77→### Environment × Domain Boundaries (16 Namespaces)
    78→
    79→| Namespace Pattern | Contents |
    80→|-------------------|----------|
    81→| `{env}-api-services` | FastAPI backends, business apps, bots, data pipelines |
    82→| `{env}-mcp-servers` | MCP protocol servers |
    83→| `{env}-web-apps` | Nuxt 3 frontends |
    84→| `shared-kong` | Kong API Gateway |
    85→| `shared-litellm` | LiteLLM proxy (Kong-only access) |
    86→| `shared-argocd` | ArgoCD (existing) |
    87→| `shared-backstage` | Backstage developer portal |
    88→| `shared-monitoring` | Prometheus, Grafana, Jaeger |
    89→| `shared-devsecops` | SonarQube, Dependency-Track |
    90→| `shared-cert-manager` | TLS certificate management |
    91→
    92→### Namespace Configuration
    93→
    94→Each namespace receives:
    95→
    96→- **ResourceQuotas**: CPU/memory limits per namespace
    97→- **LimitRanges**: Default container limits
    98→- **NetworkPolicies**: Default deny-all ingress
    99→- **RBAC bindings**: Team-scoped access
   100→
   101→## Resource Profiles
   102→
   103→### Standard Profiles
   104→
   105→| Profile | CPU Request | CPU Limit | Mem Request | Mem Limit | Use Case |
   106→|---------|-------------|-----------|-------------|-----------|----------|
   107→| **API Service** | 100m | 500m | 256Mi | 512Mi | FastAPI APIs, MCP servers, bots, data pipelines |
   108→| **API Heavy** | 250m | 1000m | 512Mi | 1Gi | RAG ingestion, document processing, ML dependencies |
   109→| **Frontend** | 50m | 200m | 128Mi | 256Mi | Nuxt 3 SSR |
   110→
   111→### Cloud SQL Proxy Sidecar
   112→
   113→When using Cloud SQL Auth Proxy:
   114→
   115→```yaml
   116→resources:
   117→  requests:
   118→    cpu: 50m
   119→    memory: 64Mi
   120→  limits:
   121→    cpu: 200m
   122→    memory: 128Mi
   123→```
   124→
   125→## Health Probes
   126→
   127→### Probe Configuration by Service Type
   128→
   129→| Service Type | Liveness | Readiness | Startup |
   130→|--------------|----------|-----------|---------|
   131→| **FastAPI** | `GET /healthz` :8000 | `GET /readyz` :8000 (checks DB) | N/A |
   132→| **MCP Server (SSE)** | `GET /healthz` :8000, period=30s | `GET /readyz` :8000, initial=30s | N/A |
   133→| **Nuxt 3** | `GET /` :3000 | `GET /_health` :3000 | N/A |
   134→| **Heavy services** | `GET /healthz` :8000 | `GET /readyz` :8000 | failureThreshold=18 (3min) |
   135→
   136→### Example Probe Configuration
   137→
   138→```yaml
   139→probes:
   140→  liveness:
   141→    httpGet:
   142→      path: /healthz
   143→      port: 8080
   144→    initialDelaySeconds: 30
   145→    periodSeconds: 15
   146→    failureThreshold: 3
   147→  readiness:
   148→    httpGet:
   149→      path: /readyz
   150→      port: 8080
   151→    initialDelaySeconds: 40
   152→    periodSeconds: 10
   153→    failureThreshold: 3
   154→  startup:
   155→    httpGet:
   156→      path: /healthz
   157→      port: 8080
   158→    initialDelaySeconds: 10
   159→    periodSeconds: 5
   160→    failureThreshold: 12  # 60s max startup
   161→```
   162→
   163→## Autoscaling (HPA)
   164→
   165→### HPA Configuration by Tier
   166→
   167→| Tier | Min | Max | Target CPU | Scale-Down Window |
   168→|------|-----|-----|------------|-------------------|
   169→| **User-facing** (frontends, public APIs) | 2 | 20 | 60% | 5 min |
   170→| **Internal APIs, MCP servers** | 2 | 10 | 75% | 10 min |
   171→| **Data pipelines, bots** | 1 | 5 | 80% | 15 min |
   172→
   173→### Custom Metrics
   174→
   175→Via Prometheus Adapter:
   176→
   177→- Request rate
   178→- Pub/Sub queue depth
   179→- Active SSE connections
   180→
   181→### Example HPA Values
   182→
   183→```yaml
   184→autoscaling:
   185→  enabled: true
   186→  minReplicas: 2
   187→  maxReplicas: 10
   188→  targetCPUUtilization: 70
   189→  targetMemoryUtilization: 80
   190→```
   191→
   192→## Cloud SQL Auth Proxy Sidecar
   193→
   194→Services connecting to Cloud SQL use the **Cloud SQL Auth Proxy** as a sidecar container.
   195→
   196→### Why Sidecar (Not Shared Proxy)
   197→
   198→| Benefit | Description |
   199→|---------|-------------|
   200→| **Per-pod authentication** | Workload Identity per service account |
   201→| **Least-privilege IAM** | Each service has minimum required permissions |
   202→| **No bottleneck** | Scales with application pods |
   203→| **Google-recommended** | Official pattern for GKE |
   204→
   205→### How It Works
   206→
   207→```
   208→┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   209→│  Pod                                       │
   210→│  ┌──────────────────┐  ┌────────────────┐  │
   211→│  │  App Container   │  │  cloud-sql-    │  │
   212→│  │  (FastAPI)       │──│  proxy sidecar │────────▶ Cloud SQL
   213→│  │  :8000           │  │  :5432 (TCP)   │  │
   214→│  └──────────────────┘  └────────────────┘  │
   215→│  localhost:5432                            │
   216→└────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   217→```
   218→
   219→### Helm Values Configuration
   220→
   221→```yaml
   222→cloudSqlProxy:
   223→  enabled: true
   224→  instanceConnectionName: "project:region:instance"
   225→  port: 5432
   226→  resources:
   227→    requests:
   228→      cpu: 50m
   229→      memory: 64Mi
   230→    limits:
   231→      cpu: 200m
   232→      memory: 128Mi
   233→```
   234→
   235→### Connection String Pattern
   236→
   237→```
   238→DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://user@localhost:5432/dbname
   239→```
   240→
   241→No password needed when using `--auto-iam-authn` with Workload Identity.
   242→
   243→## Multi-Tier App Pattern
   244→
   245→Two-tiered apps (Nuxt frontend + FastAPI backend) deploy as **multi-container pods**.
   246→
   247→### Pod Layout
   248→
   249→```
   250→┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   251→│  Pod: kix-app-hrfraud                                            │
   252→│                                                                  │
   253→│  ┌──────────────────┐   localhost:8000   ┌────────────────────┐  │
   254→│  │  frontend        │ ─────────────────▶ │  backend           │  │
   255→│  │  (Nuxt SSR)      │                    │  (FastAPI)         │  │
   256→│  │  :3000           │                    │  :8000             │  │
   257→│  └──────────────────┘                    └─────────┬──────────┘  │
   258→│                                                    │ localhost   │
   259→│                                          ┌─────────▼──────────┐  │
   260→│                                          │  cloud-sql-proxy   │  │
   261→│                                          │  :5432             │───▶ Cloud SQL
   262→│                                          └────────────────────┘  │
   263→└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
   264→         ▲                    ▲
   265→         │                    │
   266→    Frontend LB          API LB (Kong)
   267→  (Gateway API + IAP)   (internal routes)
   268→```
   269→
   270→### Benefits
   271→
   272→| Benefit | Description |
   273→|---------|-------------|
   274→| **localhost communication** | Zero network hop between frontend and backend |
   275→| **Atomic deploys** | Both containers deploy together, no version skew |
   276→| **Shared lifecycle** | Same release cycle, same Helm chart |
   277→| **Simpler networking** | No inter-service DNS, K8s Service only for external access |
   278→| **Fewer resources** | One Deployment, one HPA, one PDB |
   279→
   280→### When NOT to Use
   281→
   282→- Services needing independent scaling
   283→- Very different resource profiles
   284→- Loosely coupled services with different release cadences
   285→- Static SPA frontends (serve from CDN instead)
   286→
   287→### Helm Values Example
   288→
   289→```yaml
   290→containers:
   291→  backend:
   292→    image:
   293→      repository: eu-docker.pkg.dev/project/kix-services/kix-app-hrfraud-backend
   294→      tag: sha-abc1234
   295→    port: 8000
   296→    env:
   297→      DATABASE_URL: "postgresql+asyncpg://user@localhost:5432/dbname"
   298→      LITELLM_ENDPOINT: "http://kong.shared-kong.svc.cluster.local/llm"
   299→
   300→  frontend:
   301→    image:
   302→      repository: eu-docker.pkg.dev/project/kix-services/kix-app-hrfraud-frontend
   303→      tag: sha-def5678
   304→    port: 3000
   305→    env:
   306→      API_BASE: "http://localhost:8000"
   307→
   308→cloudSqlProxy:
   309→  enabled: true
   310→  instanceConnectionName: "project:eu-west1:hrfraud-db"
   311→
   312→services:
   313→  api:
   314→    port: 8000
   315→    ingress:
   316→      class: kong
   317→      path: /api/hrfraud
   318→  frontend:
   319→    port: 3000
   320→    ingress:
   321→      class: gateway-api
   322→      host: hrfraud.app.ix.konecta-digital.com
   323→```
   324→
   325→## ArgoCD Strategy
   326→
   327→### Per-Workload Application
   328→
   329→ArgoCD watches each **workload repo** directly via an Application manifest stored in `argocd/application.yaml`. There is no centralized ApplicationSet — each workload repo is self-contained.
   330→
   331→| Environment | Sync Policy | Change Window |
   332→|-------------|-------------|---------------|
   333→| **Dev** | `automated` (auto-sync) | 24/7 |
   334→| **QA** | `automated: false` (manual) | 08:00-18:00 UTC |
   335→| **Prod** | `automated: false` (manual) | Tue-Thu 20:00-23:00 UTC |
   336→
   337→See [GitOps & Promotion](gitops-promotion) for detailed ArgoCD configuration.
   338→
   339→### ArgoCD Projects
   340→
   341→- `dev-project` — RBAC for dev namespace deployments
   342→- `qa-project` — RBAC for qa namespace deployments
   343→- `prod-project` — RBAC for prod namespace deployments
   344→
   345→### Sync Waves
   346→
   347→- **Wave 0**: Infrastructure resources (namespaces, secrets, configmaps)
   348→- **Wave 10**: Application deployments
   349→
   350→---
   351→
   352→**Next**: [Ingress & Networking](ingress-networking) — Dual ingress architecture and network policies.
   353→
```

     1→---
     2→title: Security Architecture
     3→sidebar_label: Security
     4→sidebar_position: 11
     5→description: Runtime security, secrets management, and admission control for migrated services
     6→---
     7→
     8→# Security Architecture
     9→
    10→This document covers runtime security, secrets management, and admission control for migrated services.
    11→
    12→## Container Security
    13→
    14→### Image Security
    15→
    16→| Control | Implementation |
    17→|---------|----------------|
    18→| **Multi-stage builds** | Builder dependencies never ship in runtime |
    19→| **Base image policy** | Pinned digests, updated monthly, slim/distroless only |
    20→| **Vulnerability scanning** | Trivy pre-push, CRITICAL/HIGH block deployment |
    21→| **Image signing** | Cosign keyless (OIDC) — every image cryptographically signed |
    22→| **SBOM** | Generated for every build, stored as OCI annotation |
    23→| **Registry** | Artifact Registry with vulnerability scanning, IAM-restricted |
    24→
    25→### Supply Chain Security
    26→
    27→| Control | Implementation |
    28→|---------|----------------|
    29→| **Dependency pinning** | Hash-verified `requirements.txt`, `package-lock.json` |
    30→| **Dependency scanning** | `pip audit` / `npm audit` in CI |
    31→| **Automated updates** | Renovate for dependency PRs |
    32→| **GitHub Actions hardening** | Pin actions by SHA, minimal GITHUB_TOKEN permissions |
    33→| **No third-party actions** | Without security review |
    34→| **OIDC authentication** | No stored credentials for GCP interactions |
    35→
    36→## Runtime Security
    37→
    38→### Pod Security Standards
    39→
    40→All pods run with `restricted` profile:
    41→
    42→```yaml
    43→podSecurityContext:
    44→  runAsNonRoot: true
    45→  runAsUser: 65532
    46→  fsGroup: 65532
    47→  seccompProfile:
    48→    type: RuntimeDefault
    49→
    50→containerSecurityContext:
    51→  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
    52→  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
    53→  capabilities:
    54→    drop: [ALL]
    55→```
    56→
    57→### Restrictions
    58→
    59→| Setting | Value | Rationale |
    60→|---------|-------|-----------|
    61→| `runAsNonRoot` | `true` | No root processes |
    62→| `readOnlyRootFilesystem` | `true` | Prevent filesystem modifications |
    63→| `allowPrivilegeEscalation` | `false` | No privilege escalation |
    64→| `capabilities.drop` | `[ALL]` | No Linux capabilities |
    65→| `hostNetwork` | `false` | No host network access |
    66→| `hostPID` | `false` | No host PID namespace |
    67→| `hostIPC` | `false` | No host IPC namespace |
    68→| `privileged` | `false` | No privileged containers |
    69→
    70→### Writable Paths
    71→
    72→Only explicit `emptyDir` mounts are writable:
    73→
    74→```yaml
    75→volumeMounts:
    76→  - name: tmp
    77→    mountPath: /tmp
    78→  - name: cache
    79→    mountPath: /app/.cache
    80→
    81→volumes:
    82→  - name: tmp
    83→    emptyDir:
    84→      sizeLimit: 100Mi
    85→  - name: cache
    86→    emptyDir:
    87→      sizeLimit: 500Mi
    88→```
    89→
    90→## Secrets Management
    91→
    92→### Terraform-Managed Secrets
    93→
    94→Secrets are managed via **Terraform** in each workload repo (`konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-*/terraform/`). Terraform creates both GCP Secret Manager entries and Kubernetes secrets:
    95→
    96→```
    97→Terraform → GCP Secret Manager (audit trail) → K8s Secret → Pod
    98→```
    99→
   100→### Auto-Generated Secrets
   101→
   102→Secrets that can be generated (database passwords, HMAC keys) are created by Terraform:
   103→
   104→```hcl
   105→resource "random_password" "db" {
   106→  length  = 32
   107→  special = true
   108→}
   109→
   110→resource "google_secret_manager_secret_version" "db_password" {
   111→  secret=[REDACTED].db_password.id
   112→  secret_data = random_password.db.result
   113→}
   114→
   115→resource "kubernetes_secret" "app_secrets" {
   116→  metadata {
   117→    name      = "kix-mcp-gateway-secrets"
   118→    namespace = var.namespace
   119→  }
   120→  data = {
   121→    DB_PASSWORD = random_password.db.result
   122→  }
   123→}
   124→```
   125→
   126→### Static Secrets (TF_VARS\_ Pattern)
   127→
   128→Secrets that must be provided externally (third-party API keys, OAuth credentials) are stored as **GitHub Actions secrets** on the workload repo, prefixed with `TF_VARS_`:
   129→
   130→```hcl
   131→variable "api_key" {
   132→  type      = string
   133→  sensitive = true
   134→}
   135→
   136→resource "kubernetes_secret" "app_secrets" {
   137→  metadata {
   138→    name      = "kix-mcp-gateway-secrets"
   139→    namespace = var.namespace
   140→  }
   141→  data = {
   142→    API_KEY     = var.api_key                # Static — from TF_VARS_API_KEY
   143→    DB_PASSWORD = random_password.db.result   # Auto-generated
   144→  }
   145→}
   146→```
   147→
   148→Per-environment secrets are defined using **GitHub Environments** (dev, qa, prod) on the workload repo. See [Target Architecture — Secrets Management](target-architecture#secrets-management-in-workload-repos) for details.
   149→
   150→### Secret Rotation
   151→
   152→- Re-run Terraform to rotate auto-generated secrets
   153→- Update GitHub Actions secret and re-run Terraform for static secrets
   154→- Rolling restart pods to pick up updated K8s secrets: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/{app} -n {namespace}`
   155→
   156→### What NOT to Store in Secrets
   157→
   158→| Data | Where to Store |
   159→|------|----------------|
   160→| Configuration (non-sensitive) | ConfigMaps |
   161→| Feature flags | ConfigMaps or external service |
   162→| Large files | GCS with signed URLs |
   163→| Certificates | cert-manager (auto-managed) |
   164→
   165→## Workload Identity
   166→
   167→### No Service Account Keys
   168→
   169→Every service uses Workload Identity for GCP API access:
   170→
   171→```yaml
   172→serviceAccount:
   173→  annotations:
   174→    iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account: kix-mcp-gateway@kd-ix-platform.iam.gserviceaccount.com
   175→```
   176→
   177→### IAM Binding
   178→
   179→```hcl
   180→resource "google_service_account_iam_binding" "workload_identity" {
   181→  service_account_id = google_service_account.sa.name
   182→  role               = "roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser"
   183→  members = [
   184→    "serviceAccount:${var.project_id}.svc.id.goog[${var.namespace}/${var.k8s_sa}]"
   185→  ]
   186→}
   187→```
   188→
   189→### Least Privilege Roles
   190→
   191→| Service Type | Required Roles |
   192→|--------------|----------------|
   193→| **API with Cloud SQL** | `roles/cloudsql.client` |
   194→| **With GCS access** | `roles/storage.objectViewer` or `objectAdmin` |
   195→| **With Vertex AI** | `roles/aiplatform.user` |
   196→| **With Pub/Sub** | `roles/pubsub.publisher` or `subscriber` |
   197→| **With Secret Manager** | `roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor` |
   198→
   199→## Network Security
   200→
   201→### Default Deny
   202→
   203→All application namespaces have default deny ingress:
   204→
   205→```yaml
   206→apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
   207→kind: NetworkPolicy
   208→metadata:
   209→  name: default-deny-ingress
   210→spec:
   211→  podSelector: {}
   212→  policyTypes:
   213→    - Ingress
   214→```
   215→
   216→### Explicit Allow Rules
   217→
   218→Services explicitly allow traffic from:
   219→
   220→- GCP health check IPs (35.191.0.0/16, 130.211.0.0/22)
   221→- Kong namespace (for API services)
   222→- Gateway namespace (for frontend services)
   223→- Specific internal services as needed
   224→
   225→### Private Cluster
   226→
   227→| Setting | Value |
   228→|---------|-------|
   229→| Public node IPs | Disabled |
   230→| Master authorised networks | VPN/bastion only |
   231→| Private Google Access | Enabled |
   232→| Egress | Via Cloud NAT |
   233→
   234→## Admission Control
   235→
   236→### Kyverno Policies
   237→
   238→Kyverno enforces security policies at admission time:
   239→
   240→| Policy | Effect |
   241→|--------|--------|
   242→| `require-image-signature` | Reject unsigned images (prod) |
   243→| `disallow-latest-tag` | Block `:latest` tag |
   244→| `require-resource-limits` | Enforce CPU/memory limits |
   245→| `require-konecta-registry` | Only allow Artifact Registry images |
   246→| `restrict-capabilities` | Enforce capability drop |
   247→| `require-labels` | Enforce standard labels |
   248→
   249→### Example Policy: Require Image Signature
   250→
   251→```yaml
   252→apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
   253→kind: ClusterPolicy
   254→metadata:
   255→  name: require-image-signature
   256→spec:
   257→  validationFailureAction: enforce
   258→  rules:
   259→    - name: verify-signature
   260→      match:
   261→        resources:
   262→          kinds:
   263→            - Pod
   264→          namespaces:
   265→            - "prod-*"
   266→      verifyImages:
   267→        - imageReferences:
   268→            - "europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev/kd-ix-platform/*"
   269→          attestors:
   270→            - entries:
   271→                - keyless:
   272→                    subject: "https://github.com/konecta-ix-*"
   273→                    issuer: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
   274→```
   275→
   276→### Example Policy: Block Latest Tag
   277→
   278→```yaml
   279→apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
   280→kind: ClusterPolicy
   281→metadata:
   282→  name: disallow-latest-tag
   283→spec:
   284→  validationFailureAction: enforce
   285→  rules:
   286→    - name: validate-image-tag
   287→      match:
   288→        resources:
   289→          kinds:
   290→            - Pod
   291→      validate:
   292→        message: "Using ':latest' tag is not allowed."
   293→        pattern:
   294→          spec:
   295→            containers:
   296→              - image: "!*:latest"
   297→```
   298→
   299→## RBAC
   300→
   301→### Namespace Isolation
   302→
   303→Each namespace has dedicated:
   304→
   305→- ServiceAccount per application
   306→- Role with minimal permissions
   307→- RoleBinding to ServiceAccount
   308→
   309→### ArgoCD Project RBAC
   310→
   311→```yaml
   312→apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
   313→kind: AppProject
   314→metadata:
   315→  name: prod-project
   316→spec:
   317→  destinations:
   318→    - namespace: 'prod-*'
   319→      server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
   320→  sourceRepos:
   321→    - 'https://github.com/konecta-ix-*'
   322→  roles:
   323→    - name: deployer
   324→      policies:
   325→        - p, proj:prod-project:deployer, applications, sync, prod-project/*, allow
   326→      groups:
   327→        - platform-team
   328→```
   329→
   330→## Audit Logging
   331→
   332→### GCP Audit Logs
   333→
   334→All GCP API calls logged:
   335→
   336→- Admin Activity (always on)
   337→- Data Access (enabled for sensitive services)
   338→- System Events
   339→
   340→### Kubernetes Audit Logs
   341→
   342→Cluster audit logs sent to Cloud Logging:
   343→
   344→- RequestReceived
   345→- ResponseStarted
   346→- ResponseComplete
   347→
   348→### Log Retention
   349→
   350→| Log Type | Hot Storage | Archive |
   351→|----------|-------------|---------|
   352→| Application logs | 30 days | 7 years |
   353→| Audit logs | 400 days | 7 years |
   354→| Security events | 1 year | 7 years |
   355→
   356→## Compliance
   357→
   358→### EU Data Residency
   359→
   360→All data and processing in EU regions only:
   361→
   362→```hcl
   363→variable "region" {
   364→  validation {
   365→    condition     = can(regex("^europe-", var.region))
   366→    error_message = "Region must be in Europe"
   367→  }
   368→}
   369→```
   370→
   371→### Allowed Regions
   372→
   373→- `europe-west1` (Belgium)
   374→- `europe-west4` (Netherlands)
   375→
   376→### Organisation Policy Constraints
   377→
   378→Enforced at org level:
   379→
   380→| Constraint | Effect |
   381→|------------|--------|
   382→| No public IPs on VMs | Enforced |
   383→| Domain-restricted IAM | `konecta-group.com` only |
   384→| No service account key downloads | Enforced |
   385→| Audit logging mandatory | Enforced |
   386→| EU regions only | Enforced |
   387→

   391→
```

     1→---
     2→title: Observability
     3→sidebar_label: Observability
     4→sidebar_position: 12
     5→description: Monitoring, logging, tracing, and alerting for migrated services
     6→---
     7→
     8→# Observability
     9→
    10→This document covers the monitoring, logging, tracing, and alerting stack for migrated services.
    11→
    12→## Observability Stack
    13→
    14→| Component | Tool | Purpose |
    15→|-----------|------|---------|
    16→| **Metrics** | Prometheus | Scrape K8s + application metrics |
    17→| **Dashboards** | Grafana | Visualisation, alerting |
    18→| **Tracing** | Jaeger | Distributed traces (OpenTelemetry) |
    19→| **Logging** | GCP Cloud Logging | Centralised log aggregation |
    20→| **Instrumentation** | OpenTelemetry SDK | App-level traces, metrics, logs |
    21→| **Collection** | OTel Collector (DaemonSet) | Receive, process, export telemetry |
    22→
    23→## Metrics
    24→
    25→### Prometheus Configuration
    26→
    27→Prometheus deployed in `shared-monitoring` namespace scrapes metrics from:
    28→
    29→- Kubernetes system components
    30→- Application pods via ServiceMonitor/PodMonitor
    31→- Kong gateway metrics
    32→- LiteLLM proxy metrics
    33→
    34→### Application Metrics
    35→
    36→All services expose Prometheus metrics on `/metrics`:
    37→
    38→```python
    39→# FastAPI example
    40→from prometheus_client import Counter, Histogram, generate_latest
    41→from fastapi import FastAPI, Response
    42→
    43→REQUEST_COUNT = Counter('http_requests_total', 'Total HTTP requests', ['method', 'endpoint', 'status'])
    44→REQUEST_LATENCY = Histogram('http_request_duration_seconds', 'HTTP request latency', ['method', 'endpoint'])
    45→
    46→app = FastAPI()
    47→
    48→@app.get("/metrics")
    49→async def metrics():
    50→    return Response(generate_latest(), media_type="text/plain")
    51→```
    52→
    53→### ServiceMonitor
    54→
    55→```yaml
    56→apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
    57→kind: ServiceMonitor
    58→metadata:
    59→  name: kix-mcp-gateway
    60→  namespace: dev-mcp-servers
    61→spec:
    62→  selector:
    63→    matchLabels:
    64→      app: kix-mcp-gateway
    65→  endpoints:
    66→    - port: http
    67→      path: /metrics
    68→      interval: 30s
    69→```
    70→
    71→### Standard Metrics
    72→
    73→| Metric | Type | Description |
    74→|--------|------|-------------|
    75→| `http_requests_total` | Counter | Total HTTP requests by method, endpoint, status |
    76→| `http_request_duration_seconds` | Histogram | Request latency distribution |
    77→| `http_requests_in_flight` | Gauge | Current in-flight requests |
    78→| `db_connections_active` | Gauge | Active database connections |
    79→| `db_query_duration_seconds` | Histogram | Database query latency |
    80→
    81→## Distributed Tracing
    82→
    83→### OpenTelemetry Integration
    84→
    85→All services emit OpenTelemetry traces:
    86→
    87→```python
    88→# FastAPI with OpenTelemetry
    89→from opentelemetry import trace
    90→from opentelemetry.instrumentation.fastapi import FastAPIInstrumentor
    91→from opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.grpc.trace_exporter import OTLPSpanExporter
    92→from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
    93→from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor
    94→
    95→# Configure OTLP exporter
    96→trace.set_tracer_provider(TracerProvider())
    97→otlp_exporter = OTLPSpanExporter(endpoint="otel-collector.shared-monitoring:4317")
    98→trace.get_tracer_provider().add_span_processor(BatchSpanProcessor(otlp_exporter))
    99→
   100→# Instrument FastAPI
   101→FastAPIInstrumentor.instrument_app(app)
   102→```
   103→
   104→### OTel Collector DaemonSet
   105→
   106→Deployed as DaemonSet in `shared-monitoring`:
   107→
   108→```yaml
   109→apiVersion: apps/v1
   110→kind: DaemonSet
   111→metadata:
   112→  name: otel-collector
   113→  namespace: shared-monitoring
   114→spec:
   115→  template:
   116→    spec:
   117→      containers:
   118→        - name: otel-collector
   119→          image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:latest
   120→          args:
   121→            - --config=/conf/otel-collector-config.yaml
   122→```
   123→
   124→### Collector Pipeline
   125→
   126→```yaml
   127→# otel-collector-config.yaml
   128→receivers:
   129→  otlp:
   130→    protocols:
   131→      grpc:
   132→        endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4317
   133→      http:
   134→        endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318
   135→
   136→processors:
   137→  batch:
   138→    timeout: 5s
   139→    send_batch_size: 1000
   140→
   141→exporters:
   142→  jaeger:
   143→    endpoint: jaeger.shared-monitoring:14250
   144→  prometheus:
   145→    endpoint: 0.0.0.0:8889
   146→
   147→service:
   148→  pipelines:
   149→    traces:
   150→      receivers: [otlp]
   151→      processors: [batch]
   152→      exporters: [jaeger]
   153→    metrics:
   154→      receivers: [otlp]
   155→      processors: [batch]
   156→      exporters: [prometheus]
   157→```
   158→
   159→## Logging
   160→
   161→### Structured Logging
   162→
   163→All services use structured JSON logging:
   164→
   165→```python
   166→import structlog
   167→
   168→logger = structlog.get_logger()
   169→
   170→logger.info(
   171→    "request_processed",
   172→    request_id=request_id,
   173→    duration_ms=duration,
   174→    status_code=200,
   175→    user_id=user_id
   176→)
   177→```
   178→
   179→Output:
   180→
   181→```json
   182→{
   183→  "timestamp": "2026-02-10T12:00:00Z",
   184→  "level": "info",
   185→  "event": "request_processed",
   186→  "request_id": "abc-123",
   187→  "duration_ms": 45,
   188→  "status_code": 200,
   189→  "user_id": "user-456"
   190→}
   191→```
   192→
   193→### Log Aggregation
   194→
   195→GKE nodes forward container logs to Cloud Logging:
   196→
   197→```
   198→Container stdout/stderr → Fluentbit (GKE addon) → Cloud Logging
   199→```
   200→
   201→### Log Queries
   202→
   203→Example Cloud Logging queries:
   204→
   205→```
   206→# All logs from a service in dev
   207→resource.type="k8s_container"
   208→resource.labels.namespace_name="dev-api-services"
   209→resource.labels.container_name="kix-mcp-gateway"
   210→
   211→# Error logs only
   212→severity>=ERROR
   213→
   214→# Specific request ID
   215→jsonPayload.request_id="abc-123"
   216→```
   217→
   218→### Log-Based Metrics
   219→
   220→Create metrics from log patterns:
   221→
   222→```yaml
   223→# Cloud Logging metric
   224→name: error_rate
   225→filter: |
   226→  resource.type="k8s_container"
   227→  severity>=ERROR
   228→metricDescriptor:
   229→  metricKind: DELTA
   230→  valueType: INT64
   231→```
   232→
   233→## Dashboards
   234→
   235→### Grafana Configuration
   236→
   237→Grafana deployed in `shared-monitoring` with:
   238→
   239→- Prometheus datasource
   240→- Jaeger datasource
   241→- Cloud Logging datasource (via BigQuery export)
   242→
   243→### Standard Dashboards
   244→
   245→| Dashboard | Purpose |
   246→|-----------|---------|
   247→| **Platform Overview** | Cluster health, node status, resource usage |
   248→| **Service Health** | Per-service request rate, latency, errors |
   249→| **Kong Gateway** | API traffic, rate limiting, auth failures |
   250→| **LiteLLM Proxy** | LLM request rate, token usage, model distribution |
   251→| **Database Connections** | Cloud SQL connection pool, query latency |
   252→
   253→### Service Dashboard Template
   254→
   255→Every service gets a dashboard with:
   256→
   257→- Request rate (requests/sec)
   258→- Error rate (% 5xx)
   259→- P50/P95/P99 latency
   260→- Pod count and status
   261→- Resource usage (CPU/memory)
   262→
   263→## Alerting
   264→
   265→### Alert Configuration
   266→
   267→Alerts defined in Prometheus AlertManager:
   268→
   269→```yaml
   270→apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
   271→kind: PrometheusRule
   272→metadata:
   273→  name: kix-service-alerts
   274→  namespace: shared-monitoring
   275→spec:
   276→  groups:
   277→    - name: service-health
   278→      rules:
   279→        - alert: HighErrorRate
   280→          expr: |
   281→            sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m]))
   282→            /
   283→            sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m])) > 0.05
   284→          for: 3m
   285→          labels:
   286→            severity: critical
   287→          annotations:
   288→            summary: "High error rate detected"
   289→            description: "Error rate is {{ $value | humanizePercentage }}"
   290→```
   291→
   292→### Key Alerts
   293→
   294→| Alert | Condition | Severity | Action |
   295→|-------|-----------|----------|--------|
   296→| **Pod CrashLoopBackOff** | > 2 restarts in 5m | Critical | Investigate logs |
   297→| **High Error Rate** | > 5% for 3m | Critical | Triggers auto-rollback |
   298→| **High Latency** | P95 > 2x baseline for 5m | Warning | Investigate traces |
   299→| **HPA at Max** | Max replicas for > 10m | Warning | Consider scaling limits |
   300→| **Certificate Expiry** | < 14 days | Warning | Check cert-manager |
   301→| **ArgoCD Sync Failure** | Sync failed | Critical | Check ArgoCD logs |
   302→| **PVC Nearly Full** | > 85% usage | Warning | Expand or cleanup |
   303→
   304→### Alert Routing
   305→
   306→```yaml
   307→# AlertManager config
   308→route:
   309→  receiver: default
   310→  routes:
   311→    - match:
   312→        severity: critical
   313→      receiver: pagerduty-critical
   314→    - match:
   315→        severity: warning
   316→      receiver: slack-warnings
   317→
   318→receivers:
   319→  - name: default
   320→    slack_configs:
   321→      - channel: '#alerts'
   322→  - name: pagerduty-critical
   323→    pagerduty_configs:
   324→      - service_key: xxx
   325→  - name: slack-warnings
   326→    slack_configs:
   327→      - channel: '#alerts-warnings'
   328→```
   329→
   330→## SLOs and SLIs
   331→
   332→### Service Level Indicators
   333→
   334→| SLI | Target | Measurement |
   335→|-----|--------|-------------|
   336→| **Availability** | 99.9% | Successful requests / total requests |
   337→| **Latency** | P95 < 500ms | Request duration histogram |
   338→| **Error Rate** | < 0.1% | 5xx responses / total responses |
   339→| **Saturation** | CPU < 80% | Container CPU utilisation |
   340→
   341→### SLO Dashboards
   342→
   343→Grafana SLO dashboards show:
   344→
   345→- Error budget remaining
   346→- Burn rate
   347→- Time to exhaustion
   348→- SLI trends over time

     1→---
     2→title: Ingress & Networking
     3→sidebar_label: Ingress & Networking
     4→sidebar_position: 6
     5→description: Dual ingress architecture, network policies, and load balancing
     6→---
     7→
     8→# Ingress & Networking
     9→
    10→This document covers the dual ingress architecture, network policies, and load balancing configuration.
    11→
    12→## Dual Load Balancer Architecture
    13→
    14→Two separate ingress paths with independent load balancers provide isolation between API and frontend traffic.
    15→
    16→### Path 1: API / Backend Ingress (Kong)
    17→
    18→```
    19→Internet → GCP External LB + Cloud Armor (WAF)
    20→         → Kong Ingress Controller (shared-kong)
    21→         → {env}-api-services, {env}-mcp-servers
    22→```
    23→
    24→| Component | Purpose |
    25→|-----------|---------|
    26→| **GCP LB** | External load balancer with static IP |
    27→| **Cloud Armor** | WAF with OWASP top-10 rules, DDoS protection |
    28→| **Kong** | API routing, rate limiting, authentication plugins, CORS |
    29→
    30→#### Kong Configuration
    31→
    32→- Routes configured via `konghq.com/plugins` annotations per Ingress resource
    33→- Rate limiting per consumer/route
    34→- JWT validation for API auth
    35→- CORS headers for cross-origin requests
    36→
    37→### Path 2: Frontend Ingress (GKE Gateway API + IAP)
    38→
    39→```
    40→Internet → GCP External LB + Cloud Armor (WAF) + GKE Gateway API
    41→         → IAP (Identity-Aware Proxy) / IAM authentication
    42→         → {env}-web-apps (Nuxt 3 frontends)
    43→```
    44→
    45→| Component | Purpose |
    46→|-----------|---------|
    47→| **GKE Gateway API** | Native GKE ingress using `Gateway` and `HTTPRoute` resources |
    48→| **IAP** | Google-managed identity layer — authenticates users via Google/OIDC |
    49→| **Cloud Armor** | Same WAF policies as API path |
    50→
    51→#### IAP Configuration
    52→
    53→- Configured via `BackendConfig` with IAP enabled
    54→- Access controlled by IAM policies on the IAP resource
    55→- Only authorised users/groups can reach the frontend
    56→- No Kong involvement for frontend traffic
    57→
    58→### Internal: LiteLLM via Kong
    59→
    60→All LLM traffic routes through Kong to LiteLLM:
    61→
    62→```
    63→Any service pod → Kong (internal route)
    64→               → shared-litellm (LiteLLM proxy)
    65→               → Vertex AI / LLM providers
    66→```
    67→
    68→| Benefit | Description |
    69→|---------|-------------|
    70→| **Centralised access control** | Rate limiting, auth on LLM traffic |
    71→| **Usage metering** | Consistent billing attribution |
    72→| **Audit trail** | All LLM requests logged |
    73→| **No direct access** | NetworkPolicy blocks direct LiteLLM access |
    74→
    75→## Network Policies
    76→
    77→### Default Deny
    78→
    79→All application namespaces have **default deny ingress**:
    80→
    81→```yaml
    82→apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
    83→kind: NetworkPolicy
    84→metadata:
    85→  name: default-deny-ingress
    86→  namespace: dev-api-services
    87→spec:
    88→  podSelector: {}
    89→  policyTypes:
    90→    - Ingress
    91→```
    92→
    93→### GCP Health Check IPs
    94→
    95→**MANDATORY** for any service behind a load balancer:
    96→
    97→```yaml
    98→apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
    99→kind: NetworkPolicy
   100→metadata:
   101→  name: allow-gcp-health-checks
   102→spec:
   103→  podSelector: {}
   104→  ingress:
   105→    - from:
   106→        - ipBlock:
   107→            cidr: 35.191.0.0/16
   108→        - ipBlock:
   109→            cidr: 130.211.0.0/22
   110→      ports:
   111→        - protocol: TCP
   112→          port: 8080
   113→```
   114→
   115→:::warning
   116→70% of network policy issues stem from missing GCP health check IPs. Without these rules, backends are marked unhealthy and traffic doesn't flow.
   117→:::
   118→
   119→### Allow from Kong
   120→
   121→For API services:
   122→
   123→```yaml
   124→apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
   125→kind: NetworkPolicy
   126→metadata:
   127→  name: allow-from-kong
   128→spec:
   129→  podSelector:
   130→    matchLabels:
   131→      app: kix-mcp-gateway
   132→  ingress:
   133→    - from:
   134→        - namespaceSelector:
   135→            matchLabels:
   136→              name: shared-kong
   137→      ports:
   138→        - protocol: TCP
   139→          port: 8080
   140→```
   141→
   142→### Allow from Gateway API
   143→
   144→For frontend services:
   145→
   146→```yaml
   147→apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
   148→kind: NetworkPolicy
   149→metadata:
   150→  name: allow-from-gateway
   151→spec:
   152→  podSelector:
   153→    matchLabels:
   154→      app: kix-usecase-iq-portal
   155→  ingress:
   156→    - from:
   157→        - namespaceSelector:
   158→            matchLabels:
   159→              name: shared-gateway
   160→      ports:
   161→        - protocol: TCP
   162→          port: 3000
   163→```
   164→
   165→### LiteLLM Isolation
   166→
   167→LiteLLM only accepts traffic from Kong:
   168→
   169→```yaml
   170→apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
   171→kind: NetworkPolicy
   172→metadata:
   173→  name: litellm-kong-only
   174→  namespace: shared-litellm
   175→spec:
   176→  podSelector:
   177→    matchLabels:
   178→      app: litellm
   179→  ingress:
   180→    - from:
   181→        - namespaceSelector:
   182→            matchLabels:
   183→              name: shared-kong
   184→      ports:
   185→        - protocol: TCP
   186→          port: 8000
   187→```
   188→
   189→## TLS Configuration
   190→
   191→### Certificate Management
   192→
   193→- **cert-manager** in `shared-cert-manager` namespace
   194→- **Let's Encrypt** issuer for automatic certificates
   195→- Separate certificates per domain
   196→
   197→### DNS by Environment
   198→
   199→| Environment | API Domain | Frontend Domain |
   200→|-------------|------------|-----------------|
   201→| Dev | `dev.api.ix.konecta-digital.com` | `dev.app.ix.konecta-digital.com` |
   202→| QA | `qa.api.ix.konecta-digital.com` | `qa.app.ix.konecta-digital.com` |
   203→| Prod | `api.ix.konecta-digital.com` | `app.ix.konecta-digital.com` |
   204→
   205→### Service-Specific Domains
   206→
   207→Frontend services get dedicated subdomains:
   208→
   209→| Service | Dev | Prod |
   210→|---------|-----|------|
   211→| IQ Portal | `iq-portal.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com` | `iq-portal.app.ix.konecta-digital.com` |
   212→| HR Fraud | `hrfraud.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com` | `hrfraud.app.ix.konecta-digital.com` |
   213→
   214→## Ingress Resource Examples
   215→
   216→### Kong Ingress (API)
   217→
   218→```yaml
   219→apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
   220→kind: Ingress
   221→metadata:
   222→  name: kix-mcp-gateway
   223→  namespace: dev-mcp-servers
   224→  annotations:
   225→    kubernetes.io/ingress.class: kong
   226→    konghq.com/strip-path: "true"
   227→    konghq.com/protocols: "https"
   228→    konghq.com/plugins: rate-limiting-plugin
   229→spec:
   230→  rules:
   231→    - host: api.ix.konecta-digital.com
   232→      http:
   233→        paths:
   234→          - path: /mcp-gateway
   235→            pathType: Prefix
   236→            backend:
   237→              service:
   238→                name: kix-mcp-gateway
   239→                port:
   240→                  number: 8080
   241→  tls:
   242→    - hosts:
   243→        - api.ix.konecta-digital.com
   244→      secretName: api-tls-secret
   245→```
   246→
   247→### GKE Gateway API (Frontend)
   248→
   249→```yaml
   250→apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
   251→kind: HTTPRoute
   252→metadata:
   253→  name: kix-usecase-iq-portal
   254→  namespace: dev-api-services
   255→spec:
   256→  parentRefs:
   257→    - name: frontend-gateway
   258→      namespace: shared-gateway
   259→  hostnames:
   260→    - iq-portal.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com
   261→  rules:
   262→    - matches:
   263→        - path:
   264→            type: PathPrefix
   265→            value: /
   266→      backendRefs:
   267→        - name: kix-usecase-iq-portal
   268→          port: 3000
   269→```
   270→
   271→### BackendConfig for IAP
   272→
   273→```yaml
   274→apiVersion: cloud.google.com/v1
   275→kind: BackendConfig
   276→metadata:
   277→  name: kix-usecase-iq-portal-iap
   278→  namespace: dev-api-services
   279→spec:
   280→  iap:
   281→    enabled: true
   282→    oauthclientCredentials:
   283→      secretName: iap-oauth-credentials
   284→```
   285→
   286→## Internal Service Communication
   287→
   288→### ClusterIP Services
   289→
   290→Internal services use ClusterIP (no external access):
   291→
   292→```yaml
   293→apiVersion: v1
   294→kind: Service
   295→metadata:
   296→  name: kix-mcp-gateway
   297→  namespace: dev-mcp-servers
   298→spec:
   299→  type: ClusterIP
   300→  selector:
   301→    app: kix-mcp-gateway
   302→  ports:
   303→    - port: 8080
   304→      targetPort: 8080
   305→```
   306→
   307→### Service Discovery
   308→
   309→Services access each other via:
   310→
   311→```
   312→service.namespace.svc.cluster.local
   313→```
   314→
   315→Examples:
   316→- Kong: `kong.shared-kong.svc.cluster.local`
   317→- LiteLLM (via Kong): `kong.shared-kong.svc.cluster.local/llm`
   318→- MCP Gateway: `kix-mcp-gateway.dev-mcp-servers.svc.cluster.local`
   319→
   320→## Cloud Armor WAF Rules
   321→
   322→Both load balancers use Cloud Armor with OWASP top-10 protection:
   323→
   324→| Rule | Description |
   325→|------|-------------|
   326→| SQL injection | Block SQLi attempts |
   327→| XSS | Block cross-site scripting |
   328→| Remote file inclusion | Block RFI attacks |
   329→| Local file inclusion | Block LFI attempts |
   330→| Protocol attack | Block HTTP protocol violations |
   331→| Scanner detection | Block known scanner signatures |
   332→| DDoS protection | Rate limiting at edge |
   333→
   334→## Service Mesh Decision
   335→
   336→**Decision: No service mesh initially.**
   337→
   338→| Consideration | Rationale |
   339→|---------------|-----------|
   340→| **Kong handles ingress** | Traffic management, auth, rate limiting already covered |
   341→| **Migration complexity** | Adding Istio/Linkerd during migration adds risk |
   342→| **Resource overhead** | Sidecar proxies add CPU/memory overhead |
   343→| **Revisit post-migration** | Consider if mTLS or advanced traffic management needed |
   344→
   345→---
   346→
   347→**Next**: [Docker Security](docker-security) — Secure multi-stage builds and hardening.
   348→
```

     1→---
     2→title: IQ Portal Migration Guide
     3→sidebar_label: IQ Portal
     4→sidebar_position: 2
     5→description: Complete migration guide for IQ Portal from Cloud Run to kix-infrastructure
     6→---
     7→
     8→# IQ Portal Migration Guide
     9→
    10→**Service**: kon-iq-portal
    11→**Code Repo**: `konecta-ix-applications/kix-app-iqportal`
    12→**Workload Repo**: `konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-iqportal`
    13→**Phase**: P0 (Pilot)
    14→
    15→---
    16→
    17→## 1. Current State Assessment
    18→
    19→### Architecture
    20→
    21→IQ Portal is a **single-container monolith**: an Express.js (TypeScript) backend serves both the API (`/api/*`) and a pre-generated Nuxt 4 SPA (static files from `/dist`). Everything runs on port **8080** in production.
    22→
    23→```
    24→┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
    25→│  Cloud Run (kon-iq-portal)              │
    26→│                                         │
    27→│  Express.js :8080                       │
    28→│  ├── /api/*  → API routes               │
    29→│  ├── /docs   → Swagger UI               │
    30→│  └── /*      → Static Nuxt SPA          │
    31→│                                         │
    32→│  Cloud SQL (Unix socket)                │
    33→│  /cloudsql/project:region:instance      │
    34→└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
    35→```
    36→
    37→### Current Tech Stack
    38→
    39→| Component | Detail |
    40→|-----------|--------|
    41→| Runtime | Node.js 22 (Alpine) |
    42→| Frontend | Nuxt 4 (SPA, `ssr: false`, pre-generated static) |
    43→| Backend | Express 5 (TypeScript, via `tsx`) |
    44→| Database | PostgreSQL on Cloud SQL (`kd-lab-464110:europe-west1:konecta-iqplatform`) |
    45→| DB Connection | Unix socket via VPC connector (`DB_HOST=/cloudsql/...`) |
    46→| Migrations | Custom SQL/TS runner (33 migrations, runs on startup) |
    47→| Auth | Google OAuth → JWT in HttpOnly cookies |
    48→| Storage | GCS (3 buckets: images, videos, RAG docs) |
    49→| AI | Vertex AI (Gemini) + RAG corpus |
    50→| Async Jobs | Cloud Tasks → kon-rag-ingestion |
    51→| Email | ChannelHub (external Cognito-auth API) |
    52→| CI/CD | Cloud Build from Bitbucket |
    53→| Port | 8080 (production), 3002 (dev) |
    54→
    55→### Current GCP Service Dependencies
    56→
    57→| Service | Project | Used For |
    58→|---------|---------|----------|
    59→| Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL) | `kd-lab-464110` | Primary database |
    60→| Cloud Storage | `kd-corp-dgt-svc-apps-dev` | Image/video/RAG file storage |
    61→| Vertex AI | `kd-lab-464110` | Gemini LLM + RAG retrieval |
    62→| Cloud Tasks | `kd-lab-464110` | Async RAG document ingestion |
    63→| Secret Manager | `kd-lab-464110` | JWT secret, DB password, RAG token |
    64→
    65→---
    66→
    67→## 2. Target State
    68→
    69→```
    70→┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    71→│  kix-infrastructure GKE Cluster                                     │
    72→│                                                                     │
    73→│  Namespace: dev-api-services (then qa-api-services, prod-...)       │
    74→│                                                                     │
    75→│  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
    76→│  │  Pod: kix-apps-konectaiq                                   │  │
    77→│  │                                                               │  │
    78→│  │  ┌──────────────────────┐   ┌──────────────────────────────┐  │  │
    79→│  │  │  app (Express)       │   │  cloud-sql-proxy sidecar     │  │  │
    80→│  │  │  :8080               │──▶│  :5432 (TCP)                 │──────▶ Cloud SQL
    81→│  │  │  /api/* + SPA        │   │  --private-ip                │  │  │
    82→│  │  └──────────────────────┘   └──────────────────────────────┘  │  │
    83→│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
    84→│      │                                                              │
    85→│      ▼                                                              │
    86→│  Service: kix-apps-konectaiq :8080                               │
    87→│      │                         │                                    │
    88→│      ▼                         ▼                                    │
    89→│  Kong Ingress              GKE Gateway API                          │
    90→│  /api/iq-portal/*          iq.app.ix.konecta-digital.com            │
    91→│  (API consumers)           (browser users via IAP)                  │
    92→└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    93→```
    94→
    95→### Key Differences from Cloud Run
    96→
    97→| Aspect | Cloud Run | kix-infrastructure |
    98→|--------|-----------|-------------------|
    99→| DB connection | Unix socket via VPC connector | Cloud SQL Auth Proxy sidecar (TCP `localhost:5432`) |
   100→| Secrets | Secret Manager direct access | External Secrets Operator → K8s Secrets |
   101→| Scaling | 0-10 instances | HPA 1-5 replicas |
   102→| Ingress | Direct HTTPS | Dual: Kong (API) + Gateway API + IAP (frontend) |
   103→| CI/CD | Cloud Build + Bitbucket | GitHub Actions + ArgoCD |
   104→| Health checks | Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK | K8s liveness/readiness probes |
   105→
   106→---
   107→
   108→## 3. Pre-requisites
   109→
   110→Before starting, ensure:
   111→
   112→- [ ] Access to `konecta-ix-applications` GitHub org (write) — for code repo
   113→- [ ] Access to `konecta-ix-workloads` GitHub org (write) — for workload repo
   114→- [ ] Access to `konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-ci-workflows` (read)
   115→- [ ] `kix-platform-workload-template` available for scaffolding workload repos
   116→- [ ] Shared Kong gateway operational in `shared-kong` namespace
   117→- [ ] GKE Gateway API + IAP configured on frontend LB
   118→- [ ] GCP Workload Identity pool configured for GitHub Actions OIDC
   119→- [ ] Backstage operational in `shared-backstage` namespace
   120→- [ ] Cloud SQL instance accessible from GKE cluster (private IP, same VPC)
   121→- [ ] GCP service account for IQ Portal workload with IAM roles:
   122→  - `roles/cloudsql.client`
   123→  - `roles/storage.objectAdmin`
   124→  - `roles/aiplatform.user`
   125→  - `roles/cloudtasks.enqueuer`
   126→  - `roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor`
   127→
   128→---
   129→
   130→## Step 1: Create the Repositories
   131→
   132→IQ Portal follows the **two-repo pattern** — a code repo for source code and a workload repo for hosting data.
   133→
   134→### 1.1 Create the code repo
   135→
   136→```bash
   137→gh repo create konecta-ix-applications/kix-app-iqportal \
   138→  --template konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-service-template \
   139→  --private
   140→
   141→git clone git@github.com:konecta-ix-applications/kix-app-iqportal.git
   142→cd kix-app-iqportal
   143→```
   144→
   145→### 1.2 Create the workload repo
   146→
   147→```bash
   148→gh repo create konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-iqportal \
   149→  --template konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-workload-template \
   150→  --private
   151→```
   152→
   153→### 1.3 Copy application code into the code repo
   154→
   155→Copy the application source from the current `kon-iq-portal` repo into the code repo:
   156→
   157→```
   158→konecta-ix-applications/kix-app-iqportal/
   159→├── backend/              # Express.js API
   160→├── src/                  # Nuxt 4 frontend
   161→├── public/               # Static assets
   162→├── scripts/              # Deployment scripts
   163→├── nuxt.config.ts
   164→├── package.json
   165→├── package-lock.json
   166→├── tsconfig*.json
   167→├── version.txt
   168→├── Dockerfile            # Modified (see Step 3)
   169→├── docker-entrypoint.sh
   170→├── .dockerignore
   171→├── catalog-info.yaml     # Backstage descriptor
   172→├── docs/                 # TechDocs content
   173→│   └── index.md
   174→├── .github/workflows/    # CI pipeline
   175→│   └── ci.yaml
   176→├── CODEOWNERS
   177→└── .env.example
   178→```
   179→
   180→The workload repo structure is configured separately (see Step 4 and Step 7):
   181→
   182→```
   183→konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-iqportal/
   184→├── helm/                 # Helm chart
   185→│   ├── Chart.yaml
   186→│   ├── values.yaml
   187→│   ├── values-dev.yaml
   188→│   ├── values-qa.yaml
   189→│   └── values-prod.yaml
   190→├── argocd/
   191→│   └── application.yaml  # ArgoCD Application manifest
   192→├── terraform/            # Service infrastructure
   193→│   ├── main.tf
   194→│   ├── variables.tf
   195→│   └── backend.tf
   196→├── catalog-info.yaml     # Backstage service catalog descriptor
   197→├── .github/workflows/
   198→│   └── deploy.yaml       # Terraform workflow
   199→└── CODEOWNERS
   200→```
   201→
   202→### 1.4 Remove Cloud Build config
   203→
   204→```bash
   205→rm cloudbuild.yaml
   206→```
   207→
   208→### 1.5 Add CODEOWNERS
   209→
   210→```
   211→# Default owners
   212→* @konecta-ix-workloads/iq-portal-team
   213→```
   214→
   215→### 1.6 Add .dockerignore
   216→
   217→```
   218→node_modules
   219→.nuxt
   220→.output
   221→dist
   222→.git
   223→.github
   224→chart
   225→docs
   226→*.md
   227→.env*
   228→!.env.example
   229→```
   230→
   231→### 1.7 Add catalog-info.yaml
   232→
   233→```yaml
   234→apiVersion: backstage.io/v1alpha1
   235→kind: Component
   236→metadata:
   237→  name: kix-app-iqportal
   238→  description: Konecta IQ Portal — AI-powered knowledge platform
   239→  annotations:
   240→    github.com/project-slug: konecta-ix-applications/kix-app-iqportal
   241→    argocd/app-name: kix-app-iqportal
   242→    backstage.io/kubernetes-id: kix-app-iqportal
   243→    backstage.io/kubernetes-namespace: dev-api-services,qa-api-services,prod-api-services
   244→    backstage.io/techdocs-ref: dir:.
   245→    sonarqube.org/project-key: kix-app-iqportal
   246→  tags:
   247→    - nodejs
   248→    - express
   249→    - nuxt
   250→    - typescript
   251→    - cloud-sql
   252→spec:
   253→  type: service
   254→  lifecycle: production
   255→  owner: group:iq-portal-team
   256→  system: kix-platform
   257→  dependsOn:
   258→    - resource:cloud-sql-iqplatform
   259→    - component:kix-services-kong
   260→    - component:kix-mcp-gateway
   261→  links:

   263→      title: Workload Repo
   264→      icon: github

   266→
   267→## Step 2: Application Code Changes
   268→
   269→### 2.1 Database connection
   270→
   271→**No code changes required.** The existing `database.ts` supports both Unix socket (Cloud Run) and TCP (K8s):
   272→
   273→```typescript
   274→// backend/db/database.ts — already handles both
   275→const pool = process.env.DATABASE_URL
   276→    ? new Pool({ connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL })
   277→    : new Pool({
   278→        host: process.env.DB_HOST || 'localhost',
   279→        port: parseInt(process.env.DB_PORT || '5432'),
   280→        // ...
   281→    });
   282→```
   283→
   284→On kix, environment variables will be:
   285→```
   286→DB_HOST=localhost        # Cloud SQL Auth Proxy sidecar
   287→DB_PORT=5432
   288→```
   289→
   290→### 2.2 Add root-level health endpoint
   291→
   292→Add to `backend/routes/index.ts`:
   293→
   294→```typescript
   295→// K8S HEALTH PROBES
   296→// Lightweight endpoint for Kubernetes liveness probes
   297→app.get('/health', (req, res) => {
   298→    res.status(200).json({ status: 'ok' });
   299→});
   300→```
   301→
   302→Keep `/api/health` for detailed checks (DB + GCP connectivity).
   303→
   304→### 2.3 Environment variables
   305→
   306→All changes are via Helm values, no code changes:
   307→
   308→| Variable | kix Value |
   309→|----------|-----------|
   310→| `DB_HOST` | `localhost` (sidecar) |
   311→| `DB_PORT` | `5432` |
   312→| `MCP_GATEWAY_URL` | `http://kong.shared-kong.svc.cluster.local/mcp-gateway` |
   313→| `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | `https://iq-portal.app.ix.konecta-digital.com` |
   314→
   315→---
   316→
   317→## Step 3: Dockerfile Changes
   318→
   319→### 3.1 Pin base image digests
   320→
   321→Replace all `FROM node:22-alpine` with pinned digests:
   322→
   323→```dockerfile
   324→FROM node:22-alpine@sha256:<current-digest> AS dependencies
   325→```
   326→
   327→### 3.2 Remove HEALTHCHECK instruction
   328→
   329→Delete the `HEALTHCHECK` block (lines 142-157) — K8s probes replace it.

   442→
   443→## Step 5: GitHub Actions CI Workflow (Code Repo)
   444→
   445→Create `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` in the **code repo** (`konecta-ix-applications/kix-app-iqportal`):
   446→
   447→```yaml
   448→name: CI Pipeline
   449→
   450→on:
   451→  push:
   452→    branches: [develop, main]
   453→  pull_request:
   454→    branches: [main]
   455→
   456→permissions:
   457→  contents: read
   458→  id-token: write
   459→  security-events: write
   460→
   461→jobs:
   462→  pipeline:
   463→    uses: konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-ci-workflows/.github/workflows/standard-pipeline.yaml@v1
   464→    with:
   465→      service-name: kix-app-iqportal
   466→      dockerfile-path: ./Dockerfile
   467→      node-version: "22"
   468→      build-args: |
   469→        VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=${{ vars.VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID }}
   470→        NUXT_PUBLIC_ENVIRONMENT=${{ vars.ENVIRONMENT }}
   471→        COMMIT_SHA=${{ github.sha }}
   472→      skip-tests: true
   473→    secrets: inherit
   474→```
   475→
   476→:::note
   477→No `chart-path` — Helm charts live in the workload repo, not the code repo.
   478→:::
   479→
   480→---
   481→
   482→## Step 6: Secrets Migration (Workload Repo)
   483→
   484→Secrets are managed via **Terraform** in the workload repo (`kix-workload-iqportal/terraform/`).
   485→
   486→### 6.1 Auto-generated secrets (Terraform)
   487→
   488→Add to `terraform/main.tf`:
   489→
   490→```hcl
   491→# Auto-generated secrets
   492→resource "random_password" "db" {
   493→  length  = 32
   494→  special = true
   495→}
   496→
   497→resource "random_password" "jwt" {
   498→  length  = 64
   499→  special = true
   500→}
   501→
   502→resource "google_secret_manager_secret" "db_password" {
   503→  secret_id = "kix-iq-portal-db-password-${var.environment}"
   504→  replication { auto {} }
   505→}
   506→
   507→resource "google_secret_manager_secret_version" "db_password" {
   508→  secret=[REDACTED].db_password.id
   509→  secret_data = random_password.db.result
   510→}
   511→```
   512→
   513→### 6.2 Static secrets (GitHub Actions → Terraform)
   514→
   515→Add per-environment secrets to the **workload repo** GitHub settings:
   516→
   517→| GitHub Secret (per env) | Terraform Variable | Source |
   518→|-------------------------|-------------------|--------|
   519→| `TF_VARS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` | `var.google_client_id` | Google OAuth |
   520→| `TF_VARS_RAG_PIPELINE_TOKEN` | `var.rag_pipeline_token` | RAG service |
   521→| `TF_VARS_CHANNELHUB_CLIENT_ID` | `var.channelhub_client_id` | ChannelHub |
   522→| `TF_VARS_CHANNELHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` | `var.channelhub_client_secret` | ChannelHub |
   523→| `TF_VARS_CHANNELHUB_CONNECTION_ID` | `var.channelhub_connection_id` | ChannelHub |
   524→
   525→### 6.3 Create Kubernetes secret (Terraform)
   526→
   527→```hcl
   528→resource "kubernetes_secret" "app_secrets" {
   529→  metadata {
   530→    name      = "kix-app-iqportal-secrets"
   531→    namespace = var.namespace
   532→  }
   533→  data = {
   534→    DB_PASSWORD               = random_password.db.result
   535→    DB_USER                   = var.db_user
   536→    JWT_SECRET                = random_password.jwt.result
   537→    GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID          = var.google_client_id
   538→    RAG_PIPELINE_TOKEN        = var.rag_pipeline_token
   539→    CHANNELHUB_CLIENT_ID      = var.channelhub_client_id
   540→    CHANNELHUB_CLIENT_SECRET  = var.channelhub_client_secret
   541→    CHANNELHUB_CONNECTION_ID  = var.channelhub_connection_id
   542→    GCS_IMAGE_BUCKET          = var.gcs_image_bucket
   543→    GCS_VIDEO_BUCKET          = var.gcs_video_bucket
   544→    GCS_RAG_BUCKET            = var.gcs_rag_bucket
   545→  }
   546→}
   547→```
   548→
   549→### 6.4 Apply Terraform
   550→
   551→```bash
   552→# Run via GitHub Actions or manually
   553→cd kix-workload-iqportal/terraform
   554→terraform init
   555→terraform plan \
   556→  -var="environment=dev" \
   557→  -var="google_client_id=$TF_VARS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID" \
   558→  -var="rag_pipeline_token=$TF_VARS_RAG_PIPELINE_TOKEN" \
   559→  # ... other TF_VARS_
   560→terraform apply
   561→```
   562→
   563→---
   564→
   565→## Step 7: GitOps Configuration (Workload Repo)
   566→
   567→### 7.1 ArgoCD Application
   568→
   569→Create `argocd/application.yaml` in the workload repo:
   570→
   571→```yaml
   572→apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1

   583→    helm:

   611→      LOG_LEVEL: "debug"
   612→
   613→autoscaling:
   614→  minReplicas: 1

   616→
   617→services:

   620→      host: iq-portal.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com

   624→
   625→## Step 8: Database Migration
   626→
   627→### Strategy
   628→
   629→The app runs migrations automatically on startup. This is safe because:
   630→
   631→- The Cloud SQL instance already exists with the schema
   632→- Migrations are idempotent (tracked in `schema_migrations` table)
   633→- No schema changes are part of this migration
   634→
   635→### Connectivity test
   636→
   637→```bash
   638→# Deploy test pod with cloud-sql-proxy
   639→kubectl run sql-test --rm -it \
   640→  --image=gcr.io/cloud-sql-connectors/cloud-sql-proxy:2.14.3 \
   641→  --namespace=dev-api-services \
   642→  --serviceaccount=kix-apps-konectaiq \
   643→  -- --private-ip kd-lab-464110:europe-west1:konecta-iqplatform
   644→```
   645→
   646→---
   647→
   648→## Step 9: Verification & Smoke Tests
   649→
   650→### 9.1 Deployment checklist
   651→
   652→```bash
   653→NAMESPACE=dev-api-services
   654→
   655→# 1. Pod running (2/2 = app + cloud-sql-proxy)
   656→kubectl get pods -n $NAMESPACE -l app=kix-app-iqportal
   657→
   658→# 2. Both containers healthy
   659→kubectl describe pod -n $NAMESPACE -l app=kix-app-iqportal | grep -A5 "Conditions"
   660→
   661→# 3. Logs check
   662→kubectl logs -n $NAMESPACE -l app=kix-app-iqportal -c app | grep "running on"
   663→
   664→# 4. Cloud SQL proxy connected
   665→kubectl logs -n $NAMESPACE -l app=kix-app-iqportal -c cloud-sql-proxy | grep "ready"
   666→```
   667→
   668→### 9.2 Functional smoke tests
   669→
   670→```bash
   671→BASE_URL="https://iq-portal.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com"
   672→
   673→# Health check
   674→curl -s $BASE_URL/health | jq .
   675→# Expected: {"status":"ok"}
   676→
   677→# Full health check
   678→curl -s $BASE_URL/api/health | jq .
   679→# Expected: {"status":"ok","checks":{"database":"ok","gcp":"ok"}}
   680→

   690→# Expected: 401
   691→```

   695→## Step 10: DNS & Domain Cutover
   696→
   697→### New domains

     1→---
     2→title: Operations & Risks
     3→sidebar_label: Operations & Risks
     4→sidebar_position: 13
     5→description: Cost considerations, disaster recovery, and risk register
     6→---
     7→
     8→# Operations & Risks
     9→
    10→This document covers cost considerations, disaster recovery planning, and the risk register for the migration.
    11→
    12→## Cost Considerations
    13→
    14→### Cloud Run vs GKE Cost Model
    15→
    16→| Factor | Cloud Run | GKE (Target) |
    17→|--------|-----------|--------------|
    18→| **Billing model** | Per-request (scale to zero) | Reserved capacity (always-on) |
    19→| **Idle cost** | $0 | Node pool minimum |
    20→| **Burst cost** | High (cold starts + per-invocation) | Lower (pre-provisioned pods) |
    21→| **Predictability** | Variable | Predictable |
    22→
    23→### Cost Mitigation Strategies
    24→
    25→| Strategy | Implementation |
    26→|----------|----------------|
    27→| **GKE Autopilot** | Nodes scale down automatically based on pod demand |
    28→| **Low-traffic services** | `minReplicas: 1` for Tier 3 services |
    29→| **Scale-to-zero** | Consider KEDA for truly idle services (post-migration) |
    30→| **Right-sizing** | Tune resource requests based on actual usage |
    31→| **Spot/preemptible pods** | For dev/qa non-critical workloads |
    32→
    33→### Expected Cost Changes
    34→
    35→| Component | Before | After | Notes |
    36→|-----------|--------|-------|-------|
    37→| **Compute** | Cloud Run (pay-per-use) | GKE Autopilot (reserved) | More predictable, may be higher for low-traffic services |
    38→| **Networking** | Included in Cloud Run | Explicit LB costs | Two LBs (API + Frontend) |
    39→| **Observability** | Cloud Monitoring | Prometheus + Grafana | Reduced GCP monitoring costs |
    40→| **Secrets** | Secret Manager direct | ESO + Secret Manager | Same Secret Manager cost |
    41→
    42→## Operational Overhead
    43→
    44→### Reduced Overhead
    45→
    46→| Area | Improvement |
    47→|------|-------------|
    48→| **CI/CD** | Single pipeline for all services (vs. Cloud Build per-service) |
    49→| **Deployments** | ArgoCD GitOps eliminates manual deployment steps |
    50→| **Monitoring** | Unified dashboards across all services |
    51→| **Runbooks** | Standardised procedures (same platform, same patterns) |
    52→| **Troubleshooting** | Consistent logging and tracing across services |
    53→
    54→### New Overhead
    55→
    56→| Area | Mitigation |
    57→|------|------------|
    58→| **Helm chart maintenance** | Workload template scaffolding reduces per-service overhead |
    59→| **ArgoCD operations** | Self-healing reduces manual intervention |
    60→| **K8s complexity** | Platform team handles infrastructure; use-case teams focus on apps |
    61→
    62→## Disaster Recovery
    63→
    64→### Multi-Region Architecture
    65→
    66→| Component | Primary | Secondary |
    67→|-----------|---------|-----------|
    68→| **GKE Cluster** | eu-west1 | eu-west4 (pre-provisioned) |
    69→| **Cloud SQL** | eu-west1 (HA) | Cross-region replica in eu-west4 |
    70→| **GCS Buckets** | Multi-regional (EU) | N/A (inherently replicated) |
    71→| **Secret Manager** | Automatic replication | N/A |
    72→
    73→### Failover Strategy
    74→
    75→**DNS-based failover:**
    76→
    77→1. Primary cluster health check fails
    78→2. Cloud DNS updates to point to secondary cluster LB
    79→3. ArgoCD in secondary syncs from same GitOps repo
    80→4. Services running on secondary within 15 minutes
    81→
    82→### Recovery Objectives
    83→
    84→| Objective | Target | Description |
    85→|-----------|--------|-------------|
    86→| **RPO** | Near-zero | Managed services handle replication |
    87→| **RTO** | < 15 minutes | ArgoCD deploys from Git state |
    88→
    89→### Recovery Procedures
    90→
    91→#### Application Recovery
    92→
    93→```bash
    94→# ArgoCD can deploy entire platform from Git state
    95→argocd app sync --all
    96→
    97→# Verify services
    98→kubectl get pods -A | grep -v Running
    99→```
   100→
   101→#### Database Recovery
   102→
   103→```bash
   104→# Cloud SQL: promote replica to primary
   105→gcloud sql instances promote-replica <replica-name>
   106→
   107→# Update connection strings in secrets
   108→# (automated via ESO if using separate secret per region)
   109→```
   110→
   111→#### State Recovery
   112→
   113→All application state is in managed services:
   114→
   115→- **Cloud SQL**: HA with automatic failover, cross-region replicas
   116→- **GCS**: Multi-regional replication
   117→- **Firestore**: Regional or multi-regional
   118→- **Pub/Sub**: Multi-regional
   119→
   120→## Risk Register
   121→
   122→### Migration Risks
   123→
   124→| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
   125→|------|------------|--------|------------|
   126→| **Resource sizing incorrect** | Medium | Medium | Start generous, tune based on metrics post-migration |
   127→| **Secret exposure during migration** | Low | Critical | ESO, no secrets in Git, Workload Identity only |
   128→| **ArgoCD sync storms** | Low | Medium | Sync waves, rate limiting, progressive rollout |
   129→| **Team unfamiliarity with Helm/K8s** | Medium | Medium | Pilot phase training, runbook documentation |
   130→| **Kong ingress misconfiguration** | Low | High | Test routes per service before decommissioning Cloud Run |
   131→| **Shared workflow drift** | Low | Medium | Versioned `@v1` tag, Renovate bumps, changelog for breaking changes |
   132→| **LiteLLM routing via Kong** | Low | Medium | NetworkPolicy enforces Kong-only access; test early |
   133→
   134→### Operational Risks
   135→
   136→| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
   137→|------|------------|--------|------------|
   138→| **Cloud SQL connection exhaustion** | Low | High | Connection pooling, sidecar per-pod, monitoring |
   139→| **Certificate expiry** | Low | High | cert-manager auto-renewal, alerting at 14 days |
   140→| **Namespace resource exhaustion** | Medium | Medium | ResourceQuotas per namespace |
   141→| **Single point of failure (Kong)** | Low | High | HPA, PDB, multi-replica deployment |
   142→| **GitOps repo corruption** | Low | Critical | Git history, backups, branch protection |
   143→
   144→### Security Risks
   145→
   146→| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
   147→|------|------------|--------|------------|
   148→| **Unsigned image deployed** | Low | High | Kyverno admission control, Cosign verification |
   149→| **Secret leaked in logs** | Medium | High | Structured logging, log scrubbing, no secrets in env |
   150→| **Lateral movement between namespaces** | Low | High | NetworkPolicies, namespace isolation, least privilege |
   151→| **Compromised CI pipeline** | Low | Critical | OIDC auth, minimal permissions, no long-lived tokens |
   152→
   153→## Runbook Procedures
   154→
   155→### Common Operations
   156→
   157→#### Scale a Service
   158→
   159→```bash
   160→# Increase replicas
   161→kubectl scale deployment/kix-mcp-gateway -n dev-mcp-servers --replicas=5
   162→
   163→# Or update HPA
   164→kubectl patch hpa kix-mcp-gateway -n dev-mcp-servers -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":10}}'
   165→```
   166→
   167→#### Force Sync ArgoCD
   168→
   169→```bash
   170→# Sync a specific app
   171→argocd app sync kix-mcp-gateway-dev
   172→
   173→# Hard refresh (re-read Git)
   174→argocd app get kix-mcp-gateway-dev --hard-refresh
   175→```
   176→
   177→#### Restart All Pods
   178→
   179→```bash
   180→# Rolling restart
   181→kubectl rollout restart deployment/kix-mcp-gateway -n dev-mcp-servers
   182→```
   183→
   184→#### View Logs
   185→
   186→```bash
   187→# Current logs
   188→kubectl logs -n dev-mcp-servers -l app=kix-mcp-gateway -c app
   189→
   190→# Previous container (if crashed)
   191→kubectl logs -n dev-mcp-servers -l app=kix-mcp-gateway -c app --previous
   192→```
   193→
   194→#### Debug Network Issues
   195→
   196→```bash
   197→# Test connectivity from pod
   198→kubectl exec -it deploy/kix-mcp-gateway -n dev-mcp-servers -- \
   199→  wget -q -O- http://kong.shared-kong:80/health
   200→
   201→# Check network policies
   202→kubectl get networkpolicy -n dev-mcp-servers -o yaml
   203→```
   204→
   205→### Emergency Procedures
   206→
   207→#### Rollback Production Deployment
   208→
   209→```bash
   210→# Option 1: Revert Git commit
   211→cd kix-platform-infrastructure
   212→git revert HEAD
   213→git push
   214→# ArgoCD syncs automatically (if auto-sync) or manually trigger
   215→
   216→# Option 2: kubectl rollback (immediate, bypasses Git)
   217→kubectl rollout undo deployment/kix-mcp-gateway -n prod-mcp-servers
   218→```
   219→
   220→#### Disable a Service
   221→
   222→```bash
   223→# Scale to zero
   224→kubectl scale deployment/kix-mcp-gateway -n prod-mcp-servers --replicas=0
   225→
   226→# Or delete the ArgoCD app (keeps Git state)
   227→argocd app delete kix-mcp-gateway-prod --cascade=false
   228→```
   229→
   230→#### Emergency Secret Rotation
   231→
   232→```bash
   233→# Update secret in GCP Secret Manager
   234→echo -n "new-value" | gcloud secrets versions add my-secret --data-file=-
   235→
   236→# Force ESO to refresh
   237→kubectl annotate externalsecret my-secret -n dev-mcp-servers force-sync=$(date +%s)
   238→
   239→# Rolling restart to pick up new secret
   240→kubectl rollout restart deployment/kix-mcp-gateway -n dev-mcp-servers
   241→```
   242→
   243→## Monitoring and Health Checks
   244→
   245→### Daily Checks
   246→
   247→- [ ] ArgoCD sync status green for all environments
   248→- [ ] No pods in CrashLoopBackOff
   249→- [ ] Error rate within SLO budget
   250→- [ ] No critical alerts in PagerDuty
   251→
   252→### Weekly Checks
   253→
   254→- [ ] Review Grafana dashboards for anomalies
   255→- [ ] Check Renovate PRs for dependency updates
   256→- [ ] Review Cloud Armor logs for attack patterns
   257→- [ ] Verify backup procedures (test restore)
   258→
   259→### Monthly Checks
   260→
   261→- [ ] Review and update resource limits based on usage
   262→- [ ] Audit IAM permissions
   263→- [ ] Review and rotate long-lived credentials
   264→- [ ] Disaster recovery drill (failover test)
   265→
   266→---
   267→
   268→**Next**: [Appendix & Reference](appendix-reference) — Technology stack and mapping tables.
   269→
```

   295→
   296→## Key Design Decisions
   297→
   298→| Decision | Rationale |
   299→|----------|-----------|
   300→| **Code/hosting separation** | Clear ownership boundaries, independent release cycles, security isolation between source code and deployment config |
   301→| **Per-workload GitOps** | Each team owns their deployment, no bottleneck on a centralized repo, self-service infrastructure |
   302→| **Repo-per-service** | Team autonomy, clear ownership, independent release cycles |
   303→| **Terraform-managed secrets** | Secrets are version-controlled (encrypted), auditable, auto-generated where possible, no manual Secret Manager operations |
   304→| **TF_VARS\_ prefix convention** | Clear separation of Terraform variables from other GitHub secrets, per-environment via GitHub Environments |
   305→| **Workload repo template** | Consistency via scaffolding, teams own their charts |
   306→| **Cross-org workflow sharing** | DRY principle, single place to update pipeline logic |
   307→| **Dual ingress** | Different auth models for APIs vs. frontends |
   308→| **No service mesh (initially)** | Reduce complexity during migration; revisit post-migration |
   309→
   310→## Key Differences from Cloud Run
   311→
   312→| Aspect | Cloud Run | kix-infrastructure |
   313→|--------|-----------|-------------------|
   314→| **DB connection** | Unix socket via VPC connector | Cloud SQL Auth Proxy sidecar (TCP) |
   315→| **Secrets** | Secret Manager direct access | Terraform-managed K8s Secrets (auto-generated + TF_VARS_) |
   316→| **Scaling** | 0-10 instances (cold starts) | HPA 1-5+ replicas (always warm) |
   317→| **Ingress** | Direct HTTPS | Dual: Kong (API) + Gateway API + IAP (frontend) |
   318→| **CI/CD** | Cloud Build + Bitbucket | GitHub Actions + ArgoCD |
   319→| **Health checks** | Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK | K8s liveness/readiness probes |
   320→| **Observability** | Fragmented | Unified Prometheus/Grafana/Jaeger |
   321→| **Deployment config** | Terraform in same repo | Separate workload repo (Helm + ArgoCD + Terraform) |
   322→
   323→---
   324→
   325→**Next**: [Migration Phases](migration-phases) — Phased approach to migration.
   326→
