   251→## CI/CD Flow
   252→
   253→```
   254→CODE REPO (konecta-ix-applications or konecta-ix-mcp-servers)
   255→─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   256→Developer Push → Code Repo (any code org)
   257→  (e.g. konecta-ix-applications/kix-app-iqportal)
   258→       │
   259→       ▼  CI triggers on develop / main branches
   260→       Calls reusable workflows from:
   261→       {code-org}/.github-private (shared workflows)
   262→       ├── Lint + Unit Tests
   263→       ├── Secret Scan (Trivy)
   264→       ├── SCA (Dependency-Track)
   265→       ├── SAST (SonarQube)
   266→       ├── Docker Build (BuildKit, multi-stage)
   267→       ├── Container Scan + SBOM (Trivy + Syft)
   268→       ├── Push to Artifact Registry
   269→       └── Cosign Sign (OIDC keyless)
   270→
   271→WORKLOAD REPO (konecta-ix-workloads)
   272→─────────────────────────────────────
   273→  kix-workload-iqportal
   274→       │
   275→       ├── Terraform (via GitHub Actions deploy.yaml)
   276→       │   ├── Creates GCP service accounts + IAM
   277→       │   ├── Creates secrets (auto-generated + TF_VARS_)
   278→       │   └── Creates K8s secrets in target namespace
   279→       │
   280→       ├── ArgoCD watches this repo directly
   281→       │   ├── Detects changes to helm/ or argocd/
   282→       │   └── Syncs Helm release to target namespace
   283→       │
   284→       └── Image tag update (manual or automated)
   285→           ├── Update values-{env}.yaml with new image tag
   286→           ├── Dev: auto-sync on commit
   287→           ├── QA: manual sync (08:00-18:00 UTC)
   288→           └── Prod: manual sync (Tue-Thu 20:00-23:00 UTC)
   289→```

   185→
   186→### Kubernetes
   187→
   188→```bash
   189→# List all pods in a namespace
   190→kubectl get pods -n dev-api-services
   191→
   192→# Describe a deployment
   193→kubectl describe deployment kix-mcp-gateway -n dev-mcp-servers
   194→
   195→# View logs
   196→kubectl logs -n dev-mcp-servers -l app=kix-mcp-gateway -c app -f
   197→
   198→# Port forward for debugging
   199→kubectl port-forward -n dev-mcp-servers svc/kix-mcp-gateway 8080:8080
   200→
   201→# Exec into container
   202→kubectl exec -it deploy/kix-mcp-gateway -n dev-mcp-servers -c app -- /bin/sh
   203→```
   204→
   205→### ArgoCD
   206→
   207→```bash
   208→# Login
   209→argocd login argocd.ix.konecta-digital.com --sso
   210→
   211→# List applications
   212→argocd app list
   213→
   214→# Sync an application
   215→argocd app sync kix-mcp-gateway-dev
   216→
   217→# View app details
   218→argocd app get kix-mcp-gateway-dev
   219→
   220→# Force refresh
   221→argocd app get kix-mcp-gateway-dev --hard-refresh
   222→```
   223→
   224→### Helm
   225→
   226→```bash
   227→# Template locally (from workload repo)
   228→helm template kix-mcp-gateway ./helm -f helm/values.yaml -f helm/values-dev.yaml
   229→
   230→# Diff against deployed
   231→helm diff upgrade kix-mcp-gateway ./helm -n dev-mcp-servers
   232→
   233→# List releases
   234→helm list -n dev-mcp-servers
   235→```

All changes are complete and verified. Here's a summary of what was updated across **13 files**:

### Changes Made

**1. CI/CD Shared Pipeline (`.github-private` replaces `kix-platform-ci-workflows`)**
- Shared CI workflows now live in each code org's `.github-private` repo (e.g., `konecta-ix-applications/.github-private`)

- Removed `kix-platform-ci-workflows` from platform repo listings

**2. Artifact Registry (`kd-ix-eur-shr-artifacts/approved-images`)**
- All image repository paths now point to `europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev/kd-ix-eur-shr-artifacts/approved-images/`
- Updated in: values.yaml examples, Kyverno admission policies, multi-tier app examples, CI/CD flow diagrams

     1→---
     2→title: Deploy Your First Service
     3→sidebar_label: Deploy First Service
     4→sidebar_position: 3
     5→description: Step-by-step tutorial for deploying your first service on KIX Platform
     6→---
     7→
     8→# Deploy Your First Service
     9→
    10→## Overview
    11→
    12→This hands-on tutorial walks you through deploying a complete service on the KIX Platform, from code to production. You'll build a simple Python FastAPI service with health checks, secrets management, and proper observability.
    13→
    14→**What You'll Build:**
    15→- Python FastAPI REST API service
    16→- Terraform-managed GCP resources (secrets, IAM)
    17→- Helm chart for Kubernetes deployment
    18→- ArgoCD continuous deployment
    19→- Integration with Kong API Gateway
    20→
    21→**Time Required:** 2-3 hours
    22→
    23→**Prerequisites:**
    24→- Completed [Onboarding](/docs/getting-started/onboarding)
    25→- Access to `konecta-ix-workloads` GitHub organization
    26→- Local tools installed: `terraform`, `kubectl`, `helm`, `gh` CLI
    27→- GCP project access (provided during onboarding)
    28→
    29→---
    30→
    31→## Step 1: Create Repository
    32→
    33→### 1.1 Create from Template
    34→
    35→```bash
    36→# Clone the workload template
    37→gh repo create konecta-ix-workloads/kix-usecase-hello-world \
    38→  --template konecta-ix-workloads/kix-usecase-template \
    39→  --private \
    40→  --clone
    41→
    42→cd kix-usecase-hello-world
    43→```
    44→
    45→### 1.2 Initialize Git Flow
    46→
    47→```bash
    48→# Create develop branch
    49→git checkout -b develop
    50→git push -u origin develop
    51→
    52→# Set default branch to develop in GitHub
    53→gh repo edit --default-branch develop
    54→
    55→# Create your feature branch
    56→git checkout -b feature/initial-service
    57→```
    58→
    59→### 1.3 Update Repository Metadata
    60→
    61→Edit `README.md`:
    62→
    63→```markdown
    64→# Hello World Service
    65→
    66→Simple FastAPI service demonstrating KIX Platform deployment patterns.
    67→
    68→**Purpose:** Learning example for platform onboarding
    69→
    70→**Tech Stack:** Python 3.11, FastAPI, Uvicorn
    71→
    72→**Endpoints:**
    73→- `GET /health` - Health check
    74→- `GET /hello` - Returns greeting message
    75→```
    76→
    77→---
    78→
    79→## Step 2: Create Service Code
    80→
    81→### 2.1 Create Python Service
    82→
    83→Create `src/main.py`:
    84→
    85→```python
    86→"""Hello World FastAPI Service"""
    87→import os
    88→from datetime import datetime, timezone
    89→from fastapi import FastAPI
    90→from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
    91→import logging
    92→
    93→# Configure logging
    94→logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
    95→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    96→
    97→# Create FastAPI app
    98→app = FastAPI(
    99→    title="Hello World Service",
   100→    description="KIX Platform learning example",
   101→    version="1.0.0"
   102→)
   103→
   104→# Get configuration from environment
   105→API_KEY = os.getenv("API_KEY")
   106→ENVIRONMENT = os.getenv("ENVIRONMENT", "dev")
   107→
   108→@app.get("/health")
   109→async def health_check():
   110→    """Health check endpoint for load balancer"""
   111→    return JSONResponse(
   112→        status_code=200,
   113→        content={
   114→            "status": "healthy",
   115→            "timestamp": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
   116→            "environment": ENVIRONMENT
   117→        }
   118→    )
   119→
   120→@app.get("/hello")
   121→async def hello():
   122→    """Returns a greeting message"""
   123→    logger.info("Hello endpoint called")
   124→    return {
   125→        "message": "Hello from KIX Platform!",
   126→        "environment": ENVIRONMENT,
   127→        "timestamp": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
   128→    }
   129→
   130→@app.get("/")
   131→async def root():
   132→    """Root endpoint redirects to docs"""
   133→    return {
   134→        "message": "Hello World API",
   135→        "docs_url": "/docs",
   136→        "health_url": "/health"
   137→    }
   138→
   139→if __name__ == "__main__":
   140→    import uvicorn
   141→    uvicorn.run(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=8080)
   142→```
   143→
   144→### 2.2 Add Dependencies
   145→
   146→Create `requirements.txt`:
   147→
   148→```
   149→fastapi==0.109.0
   150→uvicorn[standard]==0.27.0
   151→pydantic==2.5.3
   152→```
   153→
   154→### 2.3 Create Dockerfile
   155→
   156→Create `Dockerfile`:
   157→
   158→```dockerfile
   159→# Multi-stage build for smaller image
   160→FROM python:3.11-slim as builder
   161→
   162→WORKDIR /app
   163→
   164→# Install dependencies
   165→COPY requirements.txt .
   166→RUN pip install --no-cache-dir --user -r requirements.txt
   167→
   168→# Runtime stage
   169→FROM python:3.11-slim
   170→
   171→# Create non-root user (matches pod securityContext runAsUser: 1000)
   172→RUN groupadd -g 1000 appuser && useradd -u 1000 -g appuser -m appuser
   173→
   174→WORKDIR /app
   175→
   176→# Copy dependencies from builder
   177→COPY --from=builder /root/.local /home/appuser/.local
   178→
   179→# Copy application code
   180→COPY src/ ./src/
   181→
   182→# Set ownership and PATH
   183→RUN chown -R appuser:appuser /app
   184→ENV PATH=/home/appuser/.local/bin:$PATH
   185→
   186→# Switch to non-root user
   187→USER 1000
   188→
   189→# Expose port
   190→EXPOSE 8080
   191→
   192→# Health check
   193→HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \
   194→  CMD python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8080/health')"
   195→
   196→# Run application
   197→CMD ["python", "-m", "uvicorn", "src.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8080"]
   198→```
   199→
   200→### 2.4 Test Locally
   201→
   202→```bash
   203→# Create virtual environment
   204→python3 -m venv venv
   205→source venv/bin/activate
   206→
   207→# Install dependencies
   208→pip install -r requirements.txt
   209→
   210→# Run service
   211→python src/main.py
   212→
   213→# Test in another terminal
   214→curl http://localhost:8080/health
   215→curl http://localhost:8080/hello
   216→```
   217→
   218→**Expected output:**
   219→```json
   220→{"status":"healthy","timestamp":"2026-02-09T12:00:00.000000","environment":"dev"}
   221→{"message":"Hello from KIX Platform!","environment":"dev","timestamp":"2026-02-09T12:00:00.000000"}
   222→```
   223→
   224→---
   225→
   226→## Step 3: Create Terraform Infrastructure
   227→
   228→### 3.1 Create Directory Structure
   229→
   230→```bash
   231→mkdir -p environments/dev/terraform
   232→cd environments/dev/terraform
   233→```
   234→
   235→### 3.2 Create Terraform Configuration
   236→
   237→Create `main.tf`:
   238→
   239→```hcl
   240→terraform {
   241→  required_version = ">= 1.5.0"
   242→
   243→  required_providers {
   244→    google = {
   245→      source  = "hashicorp/google"
   246→      version = "~> 5.0"
   247→    }
   248→    random = {
   249→      source  = "hashicorp/random"
   250→      version = "~> 3.6"
   251→    }
   252→  }
   253→
   254→  backend "gcs" {
   255→    bucket = "kd-ix-eur-dev-terraform-state"
   256→    prefix = "workloads/hello-world"
   257→  }
   258→}
   259→
   260→provider "google" {
   261→  project = var.gke_project_id
   262→  region  = var.region
   263→}
   264→
   265→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   266→# Random API Key (for demonstration)
   267→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   268→resource "random_password" "api_key" {
   269→  length  = 32
   270→  special = false
   271→}
   272→
   273→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   274→# GCP Secret Manager Secret
   275→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   276→resource "google_secret_manager_secret" "api_key" {
   277→  project   = var.security_project_id
   278→  secret_id = "hello-world-api-key"
   279→
   280→  replication {
   281→    user_managed {
   282→      replicas {
   283→        location = "europe-west1"
   284→      }
   285→      replicas {
   286→        location = "europe-west4"
   287→      }
   288→    }
   289→  }
   290→
   291→  labels = {
   292→    service     = "hello-world"
   293→    environment = var.environment
   294→    managed-by  = "terraform"
   295→  }
   296→}
   297→
   298→resource "google_secret_manager_secret_version" "api_key" {
   299→  secret=[REDACTED].api_key.id
   300→  secret_data = random_password.api_key.result
   301→}
   302→
   303→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   304→# Kubernetes Service Account (with Workload Identity)
   305→#------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   306→resource "google_service_account" "hello_world" {
   307→  account_id   = "hello-world-${var.environment}"
   308→  project      = var.gke_project_id
   309→  display_name = "Hello World Service (${var.environment})"
   310→  description  = "Service account for Hello World service"
   311→}
   312→
   313→# Grant Secret Manager access
   314→resource "google_secret_manager_secret_iam_member" "api_key_access" {
   315→  project   = var.security_project_id
   316→  secret_id = google_secret_manager_secret.api_key.secret_id
   317→  role      = "roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor"
   318→  member    = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.hello_world.email}"
   319→}
   320→
   321→# Workload Identity binding
   322→resource "google_service_account_iam_binding" "workload_identity" {
   323→  service_account_id = google_service_account.hello_world.name
   324→  role               = "roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser"
   325→  members = [
   326→    "serviceAccount:${var.gke_project_id}.svc.id.goog[hello-world/hello-world]"
   327→  ]
   328→}
   329→```
   330→
   331→Create `variables.tf`:
   332→
   333→```hcl
   334→variable "environment" {
   335→  description = "Environment name"
   336→  type        = string
   337→  default     = "dev"
   338→}
   339→
   340→variable "region" {
   341→  description = "GCP region"
   342→  type        = string
   343→  default     = "europe-west1"
   344→}
   345→
   346→variable "gke_project_id" {
   347→  description = "GKE project ID"
   348→  type        = string
   349→  default     = "kd-ix-eur-dev-gke"
   350→}
   351→
   352→variable "security_project_id" {
   353→  description = "Security project ID for Secret Manager"
   354→  type        = string
   355→  default     = "kd-ix-eur-dev-security"
   356→}
   357→```
   358→
   359→Create `outputs.tf`:
   360→
   361→```hcl
   362→output "service_account_email" {
   363→  description = "GCP Service Account email for Workload Identity"
   364→  value       = google_service_account.hello_world.email
   365→}
   366→
   367→output "api_key_secret_name" {
   368→  description = "GCP Secret Manager secret name for API key"
   369→  value       = google_secret_manager_secret.api_key.secret_id
   370→}
   371→```
   372→
   373→### 3.3 Deploy Terraform
   374→
   375→```bash
   376→# Initialize
   377→terraform init
   378→
   379→# Plan
   380→terraform plan
   381→
   382→# Apply
   383→terraform apply
   384→```
   385→
   386→**Verify:**
   387→```bash
   388→# Check secret exists
   389→gcloud secrets describe hello-world-api-key \
   390→  --project=kd-ix-eur-dev-security
   391→
   392→# Check service account
   393→gcloud iam service-accounts describe \
   394→  hello-world-dev@kd-ix-eur-dev-gke.iam.gserviceaccount.com
   395→```
   396→
   397→---
   398→
   399→## Step 4: Create Helm Chart
   400→
   401→### 4.1 Initialize Helm Chart
   402→
   403→```bash
   404→cd ../../..  # Back to repo root
   405→mkdir -p helm
   406→helm create helm/hello-world
   407→```
   408→
   409→### 4.2 Customize Values
   410→
   411→Edit `helm/hello-world/values.yaml`:
   412→
   413→```yaml
   414→replicaCount: 2
   415→
   416→image:
   417→  repository: europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev/kd-ix-eur-dev-gke/kix-workloads/hello-world
   418→  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
   419→  tag: "latest"
   420→
   421→serviceAccount:
   422→  create: true
   423→  annotations:
   424→    iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account: hello-world-dev@kd-ix-eur-dev-gke.iam.gserviceaccount.com
   425→  name: hello-world
   426→
   427→service:
   428→  type: ClusterIP
   429→  port: 8080
   430→  targetPort: 8080
   431→
   432→resources:
   433→  requests:
   434→    cpu: 100m
   435→    memory: 128Mi
   436→  limits:
   437→    cpu: 500m
   438→    memory: 512Mi
   439→
   440→autoscaling:
   441→  enabled: true
   442→  minReplicas: 2
   443→  maxReplicas: 10
   444→  targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 80
   445→
   446→livenessProbe:
   447→  httpGet:
   448→    path: /health
   449→    port: 8080
   450→  initialDelaySeconds: 10
   451→  periodSeconds: 30
   452→
   453→readinessProbe:
   454→  httpGet:
   455→    path: /health
   456→    port: 8080
   457→  initialDelaySeconds: 5
   458→  periodSeconds: 10
   459→
   460→# Environment-specific configuration
   461→environment: dev
   462→
   463→# External Secrets Operator integration
   464→externalSecrets:
   465→  enabled: true
   466→  secretStoreName: gcp-secret-manager
   467→  secrets:
   468→    - name: hello-world-secrets
   469→      keys:
   470→        - apiKey=[REDACTED]
   471→
   472→# Gateway configuration (Kong integration)
   473→gateway:
   474→  enabled: false  # Enable in Step 7
   475→  hostname: hello-world.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com
   476→```
   477→
   478→### 4.3 Update Deployment Template
   479→
   480→Edit `helm/hello-world/templates/deployment.yaml`:
   481→
   482→```yaml
   483→apiVersion: apps/v1
   484→kind: Deployment
   485→metadata:
   486→  name: {{ include "hello-world.fullname" . }}
   487→  labels:
   488→    {{- include "hello-world.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
   489→spec:
   490→  {{- if not .Values.autoscaling.enabled }}
   491→  replicas: {{ .Values.replicaCount }}
   492→  {{- end }}
   493→  selector:
   494→    matchLabels:
   495→      {{- include "hello-world.selectorLabels" . | nindent 6 }}
   496→  template:
   497→    metadata:
   498→      annotations:
   499→        prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
   500→        prometheus.io/port: "8080"
   501→        prometheus.io/path: "/metrics"
   502→      labels:
   503→        {{- include "hello-world.selectorLabels" . | nindent 8 }}
   504→    spec:
   505→      serviceAccountName: {{ include "hello-world.serviceAccountName" . }}
   506→      securityContext:
   507→        runAsNonRoot: true
   508→        runAsUser: 1000
   509→        fsGroup: 1000
   510→      containers:
   511→        - name: {{ .Chart.Name }}
   512→          image: "{{ .Values.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.image.tag | default .Chart.AppVersion }}"
   513→          imagePullPolicy: {{ .Values.image.pullPolicy }}
   514→          ports:
   515→            - name: http
   516→              containerPort: 8080
   517→              protocol: TCP
   518→          env:
   519→            - name: ENVIRONMENT
   520→              value: {{ .Values.environment }}
   521→            {{- if .Values.externalSecrets.enabled }}
   522→            - name: API_KEY
   523→              valueFrom:
   524→                secretKeyRef:
   525→                  name: hello-world-secrets
   526→                  key: apiKey
   527→            {{- end }}
   528→          livenessProbe:
   529→            {{- toYaml .Values.livenessProbe | nindent 12 }}
   530→          readinessProbe:
   531→            {{- toYaml .Values.readinessProbe | nindent 12 }}
   532→          resources:
   533→            {{- toYaml .Values.resources | nindent 12 }}
   534→          securityContext:
   535→            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
   536→            capabilities:
   537→              drop:
   538→                - ALL
   539→            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
   540→```
   541→
   542→### 4.4 Create ExternalSecret Template
   543→
   544→Create `helm/hello-world/templates/externalsecret.yaml`:
   545→
   546→```yaml
   547→{{- if .Values.externalSecrets.enabled }}
   548→apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
   549→kind: ExternalSecret
   550→metadata:
   551→  name: {{ include "hello-world.fullname" . }}-secrets
   552→  labels:
   553→    {{- include "hello-world.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
   554→spec:
   555→  refreshInterval: 1h
   556→  secretStoreRef:
   557→    kind: ClusterSecretStore
   558→    name: {{ .Values.externalSecrets.secretStoreName }}
   559→  target:
   560→    name: hello-world-secrets
   561→    creationPolicy: Owner
   562→  data:
   563→    {{- range .Values.externalSecrets.secrets }}
   564→    {{- range $key, $value := .keys }}
   565→    - secretKey: {{ $key }}
   566→      remoteRef:
   567→        key: {{ $value }}
   568→    {{- end }}
   569→    {{- end }}
   570→{{- end }}
   571→```
   572→
   573→### 4.5 Test Helm Chart
   574→
   575→```bash
   576→# Template to verify rendering
   577→helm template hello-world helm/hello-world \
   578→  --values helm/hello-world/values.yaml \
   579→  --namespace hello-world
   580→
   581→# Dry-run install
   582→helm install hello-world helm/hello-world \
   583→  --namespace hello-world \
   584→  --create-namespace \
   585→  --dry-run
   586→```

   609→
   610→# Test locally
   611→docker run -p 8080:8080 \
   612→  -e ENVIRONMENT=dev \
   613→  europe-west1-docker.pkg.dev/kd-ix-eur-dev-gke/kix-workloads/hello-world:v1.0.0

   618→
   619→### 5.3 Push Image
   620→
   621→```bash

   633→
   634→## Step 6: Deploy with ArgoCD
   635→
   636→### 6.1 Create ArgoCD Application
   637→
   638→Create `argocd/application-dev.yaml`:
   639→
   640→```yaml
   641→apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
   642→kind: Application
   643→metadata:
   644→  name: hello-world-dev
   645→  namespace: argocd
   646→  finalizers:
   647→    - resources-finalizer.argocd.argoproj.io
   648→spec:
   649→  project: default
   650→
   651→  source:
   652→    repoURL: https://github.com/konecta-ix-workloads/kix-usecase-hello-world.git
   653→    targetRevision: develop
   654→    path: helm/hello-world
   655→    helm:
   656→      valueFiles:
   657→        - values.yaml
   658→
   659→  destination:
   660→    # Use the dev cluster URL registered in ArgoCD (not kubernetes.default.svc,
   661→    # which would deploy to the shared cluster where ArgoCD itself runs).
   662→    # Find registered clusters: argocd cluster list
   663→    server: https://kd-ix-eur-dev-cluster.endpoint.kd-ix-eur-dev-gke.cloud.goog
   664→    namespace: hello-world
   665→
   666→  syncPolicy:
   667→    automated:
   668→      prune: true
   669→      selfHeal: true
   670→      allowEmpty: false
   671→    syncOptions:
   672→      - CreateNamespace=true
   673→      - ServerSideApply=false
   674→    retry:
   675→      limit: 5
   676→      backoff:
   677→        duration: 5s
   678→        factor: 2
   679→        maxDuration: 3m
   680→
   681→  ignoreDifferences:
   682→    - group: apps
   683→      kind: Deployment
   684→      jsonPointers:
   685→        - /spec/replicas
   686→```
   687→
   688→### 6.2 Deploy ArgoCD Application
   689→
   690→```bash
   691→# Apply to ArgoCD (runs on shared cluster)
   692→kubectl apply -f argocd/application-dev.yaml \
   693→  --context gke_kd-ix-eur-shr-gke_europe-west1_kd-ix-eur-shr-cluster
   694→
   695→# Verify ArgoCD app created
   696→argocd app get hello-world-dev
   697→
   698→# Watch sync progress
   699→argocd app sync hello-world-dev --watch
   700→```
   701→
   702→### 6.3 Verify Deployment
   703→
   704→```bash
   705→# Switch to dev cluster
   706→kubectl config use-context gke_kd-ix-eur-dev-gke_europe-west1_kd-ix-eur-dev-cluster
   707→
   708→# Check namespace
   709→kubectl get ns hello-world
   710→
   711→# Check pods
   712→kubectl get pods -n hello-world
   713→
   714→# Check ExternalSecret
   715→kubectl get externalsecret -n hello-world
   716→
   717→# Check secret created by ESO
   718→kubectl get secret -n hello-world hello-world-secrets
   719→
   720→# Check service account
   721→kubectl get sa -n hello-world hello-world -o yaml | grep iam.gke.io
   722→```
   723→
   724→**Expected output:**
   725→```
   726→NAME                              READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
   727→hello-world-6b8f5d9c7b-abc12      1/1     Running   0          2m
   728→hello-world-6b8f5d9c7b-def34      1/1     Running   0          2m
   729→```
   730→
   731→### 6.4 Test Service
   732→
   733→```bash
   734→# Port-forward to test
   735→kubectl port-forward -n hello-world svc/hello-world 8080:8080
   736→
   737→# Test in another terminal
   738→curl http://localhost:8080/health
   739→curl http://localhost:8080/hello
   740→```
   741→
   742→---
   743→
   744→## Step 7: Expose via Kong Gateway (Optional)
   745→
   746→### 7.1 Update Helm Values
   747→
   748→Edit `helm/hello-world/values.yaml`:
   749→
   750→```yaml
   751→# Enable gateway
   752→gateway:
   753→  enabled: true
   754→  hostname: hello-world.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com
   755→```
   756→
   757→### 7.2 Create HTTPRoute Template
   758→
   759→Create `helm/hello-world/templates/httproute.yaml`:
   760→
   761→```yaml
   762→{{- if .Values.gateway.enabled }}
   763→apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
   764→kind: HTTPRoute
   765→metadata:
   766→  name: {{ include "hello-world.fullname" . }}
   767→  labels:
   768→    {{- include "hello-world.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
   769→spec:
   770→  parentRefs:
   771→    - name: kong-gateway
   772→      namespace: kong
   773→      sectionName: https
   774→  hostnames:
   775→    - {{ .Values.gateway.hostname }}
   776→  rules:
   777→    - matches:
   778→        - path:
   779→            type: PathPrefix
   780→            value: /
   781→      backendRefs:
   782→        - name: {{ include "hello-world.fullname" . }}
   783→          port: 8080
   784→{{- end }}
   785→```
   786→
   787→### 7.3 Sync Changes
   788→
   789→```bash
   790→# Commit changes
   791→git add helm/hello-world/values.yaml helm/hello-world/templates/httproute.yaml
   792→git commit -m "feat: enable Kong gateway integration"
   793→git push
   794→
   795→# ArgoCD will auto-sync (or manually trigger)
   796→argocd app sync hello-world-dev
   797→
   798→# Verify HTTPRoute
   799→kubectl get httproute -n hello-world
   800→```
   801→
   802→### 7.4 Configure DNS
   803→
   804→Add DNS record in Cloud DNS:
   805→
   806→```bash
   807→# Get Kong Gateway IP
   808→kubectl get gateway -n kong kong-gateway -o jsonpath='{.status.addresses[0].value}'
   809→
   810→# Create DNS A record
   811→gcloud dns record-sets create hello-world.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com. \
   812→  --zone=kix-dev-zone \
   813→  --type=A \
   814→  --ttl=300 \
   815→  --rrdatas=<GATEWAY_IP>
   816→```
   817→
   818→### 7.5 Test External Access
   819→
   820→```bash
   821→# Test via Kong Gateway
   822→curl https://hello-world.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com/health
   823→curl https://hello-world.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com/hello
   824→```

   827→
   828→## Step 8: Production Deployment
   829→
   830→### 8.1 Create QA Environment
   831→
   832→```bash
   833→# Copy dev configuration to QA
   834→cp -r environments/dev environments/qa
   835→
   836→# Update QA variables
   837→# Edit environments/qa/terraform/terraform.tfvars or variables.tf defaults
   838→```
   839→
   840→Create `helm/hello-world/values-qa.yaml`:
   841→
   842→```yaml
   843→# Override values for QA environment
   844→environment: qa
   845→
   846→image:
   847→  tag: "v1.0.0"  # Pin to specific version in QA
   848→
   849→replicaCount: 3
   850→
   851→resources:
   852→  requests:
   853→    cpu: 200m
   854→    memory: 256Mi
   855→
   856→gateway:
   857→  hostname: hello-world.qa.ix.konecta-digital.com
   858→```
   859→
   860→### 8.2 Create QA ArgoCD Application
   861→
   862→Create `argocd/application-qa.yaml`:
   863→
   864→```yaml
   865→apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
   866→kind: Application
   867→metadata:
   868→  name: hello-world-qa
   869→  namespace: argocd
   870→spec:
   871→  project: default
   872→
   873→  source:
   874→    repoURL: https://github.com/konecta-ix-workloads/kix-usecase-hello-world.git
   875→    targetRevision: main  # QA deploys from main branch
   876→    path: helm/hello-world
   877→    helm:
   878→      valueFiles:
   879→        - values.yaml
   880→        - values-qa.yaml
   881→
   882→  destination:
   883→    # Use the QA cluster URL registered in ArgoCD
   884→    server: https://kd-ix-eur-qa-cluster.endpoint.kd-ix-eur-qa-gke.cloud.goog
   885→    namespace: hello-world
   886→
   887→  syncPolicy:
   888→    automated:
   889→      prune: true
   890→      selfHeal: true
   891→    syncOptions:
   892→      - CreateNamespace=true
   893→```
   894→
   895→### 8.3 Promotion Workflow
   896→
   897→```bash
   898→# Merge feature to develop
   899→git checkout develop
   900→git merge feature/initial-service
   901→git push origin develop
   902→# Dev environment auto-deploys
   903→
   904→# Test in dev, then promote to QA
   905→git checkout main
   906→git merge develop
   907→git push origin main
   908→# QA environment auto-deploys
   909→
   910→# Verify QA deployment
   911→argocd app get hello-world-qa
   912→kubectl get pods -n hello-world --context=<qa-cluster-context>
   913→```
   914→
   915→---
   916→
   917→## Troubleshooting
   918→
   919→### Pods Not Starting
   920→
   921→**Symptom:** Pods in `CrashLoopBackOff` or `ImagePullBackOff`
   922→
   923→**Debug:**
   924→```bash
   925→# Check pod status
   926→kubectl describe pod -n hello-world <pod-name>
   927→
   928→# Check logs
   929→kubectl logs -n hello-world <pod-name>
   930→
   931→# Check events
   932→kubectl get events -n hello-world --sort-by='.lastTimestamp'
   933→```
   934→
   935→**Common fixes:**
   936→- **ImagePullBackOff:** Verify image exists in Artifact Registry, check service account has `artifactregistry.reader` role
   937→- **CrashLoopBackOff:** Check application logs for startup errors, verify environment variables
   938→- **Pending:** Check resource requests fit available node capacity
   939→
   940→---
   941→
   942→### ExternalSecret Not Syncing
   943→
   944→**Symptom:** Secret not created by ESO
   945→
   946→**Debug:**
   947→```bash
   948→# Check ExternalSecret status
   949→kubectl describe externalsecret -n hello-world
   950→
   951→# Check ESO pod logs
   952→kubectl logs -n external-secrets-system -l app.kubernetes.io/name=external-secrets
   953→```
   954→
   955→**Common fixes:**
   956→- Secret doesn't exist in GCP Secret Manager → Create via Terraform
   957→- Workload Identity not configured → Verify service account annotation and IAM binding
   958→- Wrong secret name → Check `remoteRef.key` matches GCP secret name exactly
   959→
   960→---
   961→
   962→### HTTPRoute Not Working
   963→
   964→**Symptom:** 404 or 503 when accessing via Kong Gateway
   965→
   966→**Debug:**
   967→```bash
   968→# Check HTTPRoute status
   969→kubectl describe httproute -n hello-world
   970→
   971→# Check Kong gateway
   972→kubectl get gateway -n kong kong-gateway
   973→
   974→# Check service endpoints
   975→kubectl get endpoints -n hello-world
   976→```
   977→
   978→**Common fixes:**
   979→- HTTPRoute not accepted → Check `parentRefs` matches Kong gateway name
   980→- Service not found → Verify service name matches backend ref
   981→- DNS not resolving → Check DNS record created and propagated
   982→
   983→---
   984→
   985→## Next Steps
   986→
   987→**Congratulations!** You've deployed a complete service on the KIX Platform.
   988→
   989→**Learn More:**
   990→- [Secrets Management](/docs/developer-guide/secrets-management) - Advanced ESO patterns
   991→- [Kong Gateway Guide](/docs/services/kong-gateway) - Authentication, rate limiting, plugins
   992→
   993→**Platform Services:**
   994→- [LiteLLM Gateway](/docs/services/litellm-gateway) - AI model routing
   995→- [Cloud SQL](/docs/services/cloud-sql) - Managed PostgreSQL
   996→- [Memorystore Redis](/docs/services/redis) - Managed Redis cache
   997→
   998→**Get Help:**
   999→- Documentation: https://konecta-ix-platform.github.io/kix-platform-docs
  1000→
  1001→---
  1002→

  1004→**Last Updated:** 2026-02-09
  1005→**Maintained By:** Platform Engineering Team
  1006→

     1→---
     2→title: "Creating New Repositories"
     3→sidebar_label: "New Repository Guide"

     5→description: "Step-by-step guide for creating new KIX Platform repositories with appropriate CLAUDE.md documentation"
     6→---
     7→
     8→# Creating New Repositories - CLAUDE.md Guide
     9→
    10→**Purpose:** Step-by-step guide for creating new KIX Platform repositories with appropriate CLAUDE.md documentation
    11→
    12→**Last Updated:** 2026-02-03
    13→
    14→---
    15→
    16→## Overview
    17→
    18→Every KIX Platform repository MUST have a CLAUDE.md file. This guide helps you select the right template and configure it correctly.
    19→
    20→---
    21→
    22→## Step 1: Repository Classification
    23→
    24→Use this decision tree to determine which CLAUDE.md pattern to use:
    25→
    26→```
    27→What's the repository complexity?
    28→
    29→├─ HIGH (Multi-tier, complex workflows, 15+ config files, strict dependencies)
    30→│  └─ Pattern A: Extended CLAUDE.md (~2,500-3,000 tokens)
    31→│     Use template: CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_EXTENDED.md
    32→│
    33→├─ MEDIUM (Standard app/service, single tech stack, clear structure)
    34→│  └─ Pattern B: Standard CLAUDE.md (~1,500-2,000 tokens)
    35→│     Use template: CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_STANDARD.md
    36→│
    37→└─ LOW (Demo, utility, doc-only, experimental, <100 lines code)
    38→   └─ Pattern C: Minimal CLAUDE.md (~500-800 tokens)
    39→      Use template: CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_MINIMAL.md
    40→```
    41→
    42→### Pattern A - Extended (Complex)
    43→
    44→**Use when:**
    45→- Multi-environment operations (dev/qa/prod)
    46→- Complex apply order dependencies (3+ tiers)
    47→- Comprehensive testing requirements
    48→- Multiple technology layers
    49→- Critical production impact
    50→- 15+ configuration files
    51→- Complex state management
    52→
    53→**Examples:**
    54→- kix-platform-infrastructure (multi-tier Terraform)
    55→- kix-platform-modules (module development + Terratest)
    56→- kix-services-kong (complex service with network policies)
    57→
    58→**Token Budget:** ~2,500-3,000 tokens
    59→
    60→### Pattern B - Standard (Medium)
    61→
    62→**Use when:**
    63→- Single service or application
    64→- Clear technology stack
    65→- Standard development workflow
    66→- Moderate complexity
    67→- 3-15 configuration files
    68→- Single or dual environment
    69→
    70→**Examples:**
    71→- kix-services-litellm (service deployment)
    72→- kix-services-backstage (platform service)
    73→- kix-crews-library (crew development)
    74→- kix-usecase-* (use case applications)
    75→- kix-mcp-* (MCP servers)
    76→
    77→**Token Budget:** ~1,500-2,000 tokens
    78→
    79→### Pattern C - Minimal (Simple)
    80→
    81→**Use when:**
    82→- Demos and POCs
    83→- Single-purpose utilities
    84→- Documentation-only repos
    85→- Experimental/short-lived
    86→- Less than 100 lines of code
    87→- 1-2 configuration files
    88→
    89→**Examples:**
    90→- kix-demo-* (demonstrations)
    91→- Small utilities
    92→- Proof of concepts
    93→- Experimental projects
    94→
    95→**Token Budget:** ~500-800 tokens
    96→
    97→---
    98→
    99→## Step 2: Check for Organization-Level Guidance
   100→
   101→Determine if your organization has a CLAUDE_ORG.md file:
   102→
   103→### Organizations WITH Organization-Level Files
   104→
   105→**konecta-ix-platform:**
   106→- 📍 [.github/CLAUDE_ORG.md](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/.github/blob/main/CLAUDE_ORG.md)
   107→- Contains: Terraform workflow, module development, GCS state management
   108→
   109→**konecta-ix-services:**
   110→- 📍 [.github/CLAUDE_ORG.md](https://github.com/konecta-ix-services/.github/blob/main/CLAUDE_ORG.md)
   111→- Contains: Terraform → Helm migration, service deployment standards
   112→
   113→### Organizations WITHOUT Organization-Level Files
   114→
   115→- konecta-ix-crews
   116→- konecta-ix-workloads
   117→- konecta-ix-mcp-servers
   118→- konecta-ix-demos
   119→
   120→If your organization doesn't have a CLAUDE_ORG.md file, reference only Master CLAUDE.md.
   121→
   122→---
   123→
   124→## Step 3: Copy and Customize Template
   125→
   126→### 3.1 Copy Template File
   127→
   128→**Location:** `kix-platform-docs/templates/`
   129→
   130→**Copy command:**
   131→```bash
   132→# For Extended Pattern (A)
   133→cp templates/CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_EXTENDED.md ../[your-repo]/CLAUDE.md
   134→
   135→# For Standard Pattern (B)
   136→cp templates/CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_STANDARD.md ../[your-repo]/CLAUDE.md
   137→
   138→# For Minimal Pattern (C)
   139→cp templates/CLAUDE_TEMPLATE_MINIMAL.md ../[your-repo]/CLAUDE.md
   140→```
   141→
   142→### 3.2 Replace Placeholders
   143→
   144→Search and replace these placeholders in your CLAUDE.md:
   145→
   146→| Placeholder | Replace With | Example |
   147→|------------|--------------|---------|
   148→| `[REPOSITORY_NAME]` | Your repository name | kix-services-monitoring |
   149→| `[ORGANIZATION_NAME]` | Your organization | konecta-ix-services |
   150→| `[ORGANIZATION]` | Organization short name | konecta-ix-services |
   151→| `[DATE]` | Today's date | 2026-02-03 |
   152→| `[Team Name]` | Your team name | Platform Services Team |
   153→
   154→**Quick replace command:**
   155→```bash
   156→cd [your-repo]
   157→
   158→# macOS
   159→sed -i '' 's/\[REPOSITORY_NAME\]/kix-services-monitoring/g' CLAUDE.md
   160→sed -i '' 's/\[ORGANIZATION_NAME\]/konecta-ix-services/g' CLAUDE.md
   161→sed -i '' 's/\[ORGANIZATION\]/konecta-ix-services/g' CLAUDE.md
   162→sed -i '' 's/\[DATE\]/2026-02-03/g' CLAUDE.md
   163→sed -i '' 's/\[Team Name\]/Platform Services Team/g' CLAUDE.md
   164→
   165→# Linux
   166→sed -i 's/\[REPOSITORY_NAME\]/kix-services-monitoring/g' CLAUDE.md
   167→sed -i 's/\[ORGANIZATION_NAME\]/konecta-ix-services/g' CLAUDE.md
   168→sed -i 's/\[ORGANIZATION\]/konecta-ix-services/g' CLAUDE.md
   169→sed -i 's/\[DATE\]/2026-02-03/g' CLAUDE.md
   170→sed -i 's/\[Team Name\]/Platform Services Team/g' CLAUDE.md
   171→```
   172→
   173→### 3.3 Fill in Content
   174→
   175→Go through the template section by section and replace bracketed placeholders:
   176→
   177→**Pattern A (Extended):**
   178→- Repository Overview (purpose, tech stack, environments, dependencies)
   179→- Quick Start (prerequisites, setup commands)
   180→- Repository Structure (directory tree with descriptions)
   181→- Key Workflows (3+ major workflows with commands)
   182→- Environment Management (if multi-environment)
   183→- Apply Order & Dependencies (if applicable)
   184→- Testing Strategy (unit, integration, post-deployment)
   185→- Common Operations (frequent commands)
   186→- Troubleshooting (3+ common issues)
   187→
   188→**Pattern B (Standard):**
   189→- Repository Overview (purpose, tech stack)
   190→- Quick Start (prerequisites, setup, quick commands)
   191→- Repository Structure (directory tree)
   192→- Key Workflows (development, deployment)
   193→- Testing (unit, integration)
   194→- Deployment (steps and rollback)
   195→- Common Operations (frequent commands)
   196→- Troubleshooting (common issues)
   197→
   198→**Pattern C (Minimal):**
   199→- Overview (purpose, type, tech, status)
   200→- Quick Start (prerequisites, setup & run)
   201→- Structure (simple tree)
   202→- Key Commands (2-3 commands)
   203→- Notes (important context)
   204→- Experimental Status (if applicable)
   205→
   206→### 3.4 Update Reference Links
   207→
   208→**Ensure these links are correct:**
   209→
   210→1. **Master CLAUDE.md link:**
   211→   ```markdown
   212→   [Master CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-docs/blob/main/CLAUDE.md)
   213→   ```
   214→
   215→2. **Organization CLAUDE_ORG.md link** (if applicable):
   216→   ```markdown
   217→   [Organization CLAUDE_ORG.md](https://github.com/[YOUR-ORG]/.github/blob/main/CLAUDE_ORG.md)
   218→   ```
   219→
   220→3. **Navigation guide link:**
   221→   ```markdown
   222→   [CLAUDE_NAVIGATION.md](https://github.com/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-docs/blob/main/CLAUDE_NAVIGATION.md)
   223→   ```
   224→
   225→---
   226→
   227→## Step 4: Validation Checklist
   228→
   229→Before committing your CLAUDE.md, verify:
   230→
   231→### Content Completeness
   232→- [ ] All `[PLACEHOLDER]` text replaced
   233→- [ ] Repository overview filled in
   234→- [ ] Technology stack specified with versions
   235→- [ ] Quick start commands tested and work
   236→- [ ] Repository structure reflects actual structure
   237→- [ ] Key workflows documented with real commands
   238→- [ ] Common operations include copy-paste ready commands
   239→- [ ] Troubleshooting includes real issues (can add more over time)
   240→
   241→### References
   242→- [ ] Master CLAUDE.md link works
   243→- [ ] Organization CLAUDE_ORG.md link works (if applicable)
   244→- [ ] Navigation guide link works
   245→- [ ] All internal links (anchors) work
   246→- [ ] Cross-repository links use absolute GitHub URLs
   247→
   248→### Standards Compliance
   249→- [ ] Follows Master CLAUDE.md security requirements
   250→- [ ] Follows Master CLAUDE.md git workflow standards
   251→- [ ] References universal operational standards
   252→- [ ] No duplicate content from Master or Org files
   253→- [ ] Token budget target met (check with Claude Code)
   254→
   255→### Testing
   256→- [ ] Commands in Quick Start have been tested
   257→- [ ] Validation commands produce expected output
   258→- [ ] Troubleshooting solutions actually fix problems
   259→- [ ] All code blocks have syntax highlighting (language specified)
   260→
   261→---
   262→
   263→## Step 5: Token Budget Verification
   264→
   265→Ask Claude Code to estimate token count:
   266→
   267→**Pattern A (Extended):** Target ~2,500-3,000 tokens
   268→**Pattern B (Standard):** Target ~1,500-2,000 tokens
   269→**Pattern C (Minimal):** Target ~500-800 tokens
   270→
   271→**If over budget:**
   272→- Remove unnecessary details
   273→- Move repo-specific patterns to code comments instead
   274→- Link to external documentation for deep dives
   275→- Condense repetitive sections
   276→
   277→**If significantly under budget:**
   278→- Add missing workflows or operations
   279→- Expand troubleshooting section
   280→- Add validation commands and expected outputs
   281→- Include more examples
   282→
   283→---
   284→
   285→## Step 6: Commit and Register
   286→
   287→### 6.1 Commit CLAUDE.md
   288→
   289→```bash
   290→git add CLAUDE.md
   291→git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   292→docs: add CLAUDE.md with [Pattern A/B/C] guidance
   293→
   294→Initialize repository-specific guidance for Claude Code using [Extended/Standard/Minimal] pattern.
   295→
   296→References Master CLAUDE.md for universal standards.
   297→
   298→Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
   299→EOF
   300→)"
   301→git push origin main
   302→```
   303→
   304→### 6.2 Register in Navigation Guide
   305→
   306→Update `kix-platform-docs/CLAUDE_NAVIGATION.md`:
   307→
   308→1. Add your repository to the appropriate organization table
   309→2. Specify pattern (A/B/C)
   310→3. Include token budget
   311→4. Describe primary content
   312→
   313→**Example:**
   314→```markdown
   315→| [kix-services-monitoring/CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/konecta-ix-services/kix-services-monitoring/blob/main/CLAUDE.md) | Standard (B) | ~1,500 | Prometheus, Grafana, alerting |
   316→```
   317→
   318→### 6.3 Create PR for Navigation Update
   319→
   320→```bash
   321→cd kix-platform-docs
   322→git checkout -b docs/register-[repo-name]
   323→git add CLAUDE_NAVIGATION.md
   324→git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   325→docs: register [repo-name] in CLAUDE navigation
   326→
   327→Add [repo-name] to navigation guide with Pattern [A/B/C] classification.
   328→
   329→Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
   330→EOF
   331→)"
   332→git push -u origin docs/register-[repo-name]
   333→gh pr create --title "docs: register [repo-name] in CLAUDE navigation"
   334→```
   335→
   336→---
   337→
   338→## Step 7: Ongoing Maintenance
   339→
   340→### When to Update CLAUDE.md
   341→
   342→**Immediate updates needed when:**
   343→- Adding new major workflow or operation
   344→- Changing technology stack (versions, tools)
   345→- Discovering new common mistakes
   346→- Restructuring repository
   347→- Changing deployment process
   348→
   349→**Monthly reviews:**
   350→- Update token budget if significantly changed
   351→- Review and prune outdated sections
   352→- Add new troubleshooting entries
   353→- Update "Last Updated" date
   354→
   355→**Quarterly reviews:**
   356→- Evaluate if pattern classification still appropriate
   357→- Consider promoting repo-specific mistakes to org/master
   358→- Review and optimize token usage
   359→- Validate all links still work
   360→
   361→### Promoting Mistakes
   362→
   363→**When a mistake occurs 3+ times in your repo:**
   364→1. Document in your CLAUDE.md "Repository-Specific Mistakes"
   365→2. If pattern emerges, suggest promotion to Org file
   366→
   367→**When mistake affects 3+ repos in org:**
   368→1. Coordinate with team to promote to Org CLAUDE_ORG.md
   369→2. Remove from individual repo CLAUDE.md files
   370→3. Add reference to Org file
   371→
   372→**When mistake affects 3+ orgs:**
   373→1. Propose addition to Master CLAUDE.md
   374→2. Create PR to kix-platform-docs
   375→3. Remove from Org files after Master updated

   498→
   499→## Troubleshooting
   500→
   501→### Issue: Not sure which pattern to use
   502→
   503→**Solution:** Ask yourself:
   504→- How many configuration files? (15+ = Extended, 3-15 = Standard, 1-2 = Minimal)
   505→- Multi-environment? (Yes = Extended, No = Standard/Minimal)
   506→- Complex dependencies? (Yes = Extended, No = Standard)
   507→- Demo/experimental? (Yes = Minimal)
   508→
   509→When in doubt, start with Standard (B) and upgrade to Extended (A) if needed.
   510→
   511→### Issue: Token count too high
   512→
   513→**Solution:**
   514→- Remove duplicate content from Master/Org files
   515→- Link to external docs instead of embedding
   516→- Condense similar operations into patterns
   517→- Move detailed examples to separate docs
   518→
   519→### Issue: Don't know what workflows to document
   520→
   521→**Solution:**
   522→- Document the 3 most common operations
   523→- What does a new developer need to know?
   524→- What mistakes have you made?
   525→- What do you repeatedly look up?
   526→

   529→**Solution:**
   530→If 5+ repositories in your org share common patterns:
   531→1. Create issue in your organization's .github repository
   532→2. Propose creating CLAUDE_ORG.md
   533→3. Use CLAUDE_ORG_TEMPLATE.md as starting point
   534→4. Coordinate with team to extract shared patterns

    10→Welcome to the **Konecta KIX Platform** infrastructure repository. This guide takes you from zero to deploying infrastructure and contributing to the codebase.

    75→
    76→## Understanding the Repository Structure
    77→
    78→### Module Organization
    79→
    80→Modules are organized by provider type:
    81→
    82→**GCP Modules** (`modules/gcp/`):
    83→- `base-environment` - GCP folders and projects
    84→- `landing-zone` - VPC, networking, security baseline
    85→- `gke-cluster` - GKE cluster creation
    86→- `data-services/*` - Cloud SQL, Redis, GCS, Pub/Sub
    87→
    88→**Kubernetes Modules** (`modules/kubernetes/`):
    89→- `gke-config` - Namespaces, RBAC, network policies
    90→- `kong-gateway` - Kong API Gateway
    91→- `litellm` - LiteLLM proxy
    92→- `argocd` - ArgoCD GitOps continuous delivery (shared cluster)
    93→
    94→### Service Dependency Chain
    95→
    96→Services must be deployed in order:
    97→
    98→```
    99→+---------------------+
   100→|     bootstrap       |  Creates state buckets (run once)
   101→+---------+-----------+
   102→          |
   103→          v
   104→+---------------------+
   105→|    gcp/network      |  VPC, subnets, NAT, firewall
   106→+---------+-----------+
   107→          |
   108→          +----------------+
   109→          v                v
   110→+---------------+  +---------------+
   111→|   gcp/gke     |  |   gcp/data    |  (can run in parallel)
   112→+-------+-------+  +---------------+
   113→        |
   114→        v
   115→+---------------------+
   116→| kubernetes/platform |  gke-config, kong, litellm
   117→+---------------------+
   118→```
   119→
   120→### State Management
   121→
   122→Each service has its own state file:
   123→
   124→```
   125→gs://kd-tfstate-{env}/
   126→+-- gcp/network/
   127→+-- gcp/gke/
   128→+-- gcp/data/
   129→+-- kubernetes/platform/
   130→```
   131→
   132→---
   133→
   134→## Environment Configuration
   135→
   136→### config.json (Per Environment)
   137→
   138→Each environment has a `config.json` that drives all deployments:
   139→
   140→```json
   141→{
   142→  "global": {
   143→    "environment": "dev",
   144→    "region": "europe-west1",
   145→    "gke_project_id": "kd-ix-eur-dev-gke",
   146→    "data_project_id": "kd-ix-eur-dev-data"
   147→  },
   148→  "landing_zone": { ... },
   149→  "gke_cluster": { ... },
   150→  "gke_config": { ... },
   151→  "kong_gateway": { ... }
   152→}
   153→```
   154→
   155→**Usage in Terraform:**
   156→
   157→```hcl
   158→locals {
   159→  config = jsondecode(file("${path.module}/../config.json"))
   160→}
   161→
   162→module "landing_zone" {
   163→  source   = "../../../../modules/gcp/landing-zone"
   164→  vpc_name = local.config.landing_zone.vpc_name
   165→}
   166→```
   167→
   168→### Environment Differences
   169→
   170→| Setting | Dev | QA | Prod |
   171→|---------|-----|-----|------|
   172→| Flow logs | 50% sampling | 50% sampling | 100% sampling |
   173→| Node pool min nodes | 1 | 1 | 2 |
   174→| Deletion protection | false | false | true |
   175→| Kong replicas | 2 | 2 | 3 |
   176→| VPC Service Controls | false | false | true |

   255→
   256→---
   257→
   258→## Terraform Development Standards
   259→
   260→### Module Structure
   261→
   262→Every module MUST include:
   263→
   264→```
   265→module-name/
   266→+-- main.tf           # Resource definitions
   267→+-- variables.tf      # Input variables with descriptions
   268→+-- outputs.tf        # Output values with descriptions
   269→+-- versions.tf       # Provider version constraints
   270→+-- README.md         # Documentation
   271→+-- examples/         # Working examples
   272→```
   273→
   274→### Variable Naming Conventions
   275→
   276→| Pattern | Use Case | Example |
   277→|---------|----------|---------|
   278→| `enable_*` | Feature flags | `enable_versioning`, `enable_auth` |
   279→| `create_*` | Resource creation | `create_service_account` |
   280→| `*_config` | Configuration objects | `maintenance_config`, `logging_config` |
   281→| `*_policy` | Policy definitions | `retention_policy` |
   282→
   283→**Correct:**
   284→```hcl
   285→variable "enable_versioning" {
   286→  type        = bool
   287→  default     = true
   288→  description = "Enable object versioning for the bucket"
   289→}
   290→
   291→variable "maintenance_config" {
   292→  type = object({
   293→    day  = string
   294→    hour = number
   295→  })
   296→  description = "Maintenance window configuration"
   297→}
   298→```
   299→
   300→**Incorrect:**
   301→```hcl
   302→variable "auth_enabled" { ... }      # Use enable_* prefix
   303→variable "maintenance_policy" { ... } # Use *_config suffix
   304→```
   305→
   306→### Required Variables (All Modules)
   307→
   308→| Variable | Type | Description |
   309→|----------|------|-------------|
   310→| `project_id` | string | GCP project ID |
   311→| `environment` | string | Environment name (dev, qa, prod, lab) |
   312→| `cost_center` | string | Cost center for billing |
   313→
   314→### Variable Validation
   315→
   316→```hcl
   317→variable "environment" {
   318→  type        = string
   319→  description = "Environment name"
   320→
   321→  validation {
   322→    condition     = contains(["dev", "qa", "prod", "lab", "shared"], var.environment)
   323→    error_message = "Environment must be one of: dev, qa, prod, lab, shared"
   324→  }
   325→}
   326→```
   327→
   328→### README Standards
   329→
   330→All module READMEs MUST include:
   331→- Overview and architecture
   332→- Usage examples (basic and production)
   333→- **Security Requirements section** (mandatory)
   334→- Inputs/Outputs tables
   335→- Document metadata footer
   336→
   337→### Common Patterns
   338→
   339→**Use for_each:**
   340→```hcl
   341→resource "google_storage_bucket" "buckets" {
   342→  for_each = toset(["documents", "artifacts", "logs"])
   343→  name     = "${var.usecase_name}-${each.value}-${var.environment}"
   344→}
   345→```
   346→
   347→**Use locals for computed values:**
   348→```hcl
   349→locals {
   350→  project_id = "kix-${var.environment}-${var.function}"
   351→  common_labels = {
   352→    environment = var.environment
   353→    managed_by  = "terraform"
   354→  }
   355→}
   356→```
   357→
   358→### Pre-Commit Checklist
   359→
   360→```bash
   361→terraform fmt -recursive
   362→terraform validate
   363→terraform plan -out=tfplan
   364→terraform-docs markdown . > README.md
   365→```
   366→
   367→---
   368→
   369→## Running Tests
   370→
   371→### Run Individual Tests
   372→
   373→```bash
   374→cd terraform/test
   375→
   376→go test -v -timeout 30m -run TestBaseEnvironment
   377→go test -v -timeout 30m -run TestLandingZone
   378→go test -v -timeout 60m -run TestGKECluster
   379→go test -v -timeout 30m -run TestArgoCD
   380→```
   381→
   382→### Run All Tests
   383→
   384→```bash
   385→go test -v -timeout 120m ./...
   386→```
   387→
   388→### Debug Mode
   389→
   390→```bash
   391→export SKIP_TEARDOWN=true
   392→go test -v -timeout 30m -run TestGKECluster
   393→# Manually inspect, then destroy
   394→```
   395→
   396→---
   397→
   398→## Deploying Infrastructure Changes
   399→
   400→Changes to infrastructure follow a **controlled deployment process** with manual approvals for production.
   401→
   402→### Overview
   403→
   404→```
   405→Feature Branch --> PR Validation --> Merge to Main --> Manual Deploy
   406→    (fast)           (~10 min)       (validates)       (controlled)
   407→```
   408→
   409→### 1. Make Changes in Feature Branch
   410→
   411→```bash
   412→# Create feature branch
   413→git checkout -b feature/add-redis-instance
   414→
   415→# Make Terraform changes
   416→cd terraform/environments/dev/gcp/data
   417→# Edit *.tf files
   418→
   419→# Validate locally
   420→terraform fmt -recursive
   421→terraform validate
   422→terraform plan
   423→```
   424→
   425→### 2. Open Pull Request
   426→
   427→Submit PR to `main` branch. PR validation runs automatically (~10 minutes):
   428→
   429→**What happens:**
   430→- Terraform format check
   431→- Security scan (tfsec)
   432→- Terraform validate
   433→- Generate plans for changed directories
   434→- Run fast smoke tests (if modules changed)
   435→- Plan summary posted as PR comment
   436→
   437→**Review the plan output:**
   438→```
   439→Plan: 2 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy
   440→
   441→+ google_redis_instance.cache
   442→+ google_compute_firewall.redis_ingress
   443→~ google_service_account.redis (labels)
   444→```
   445→
   446→### 3. Merge to Main
   447→
   448→After PR approval, merge to `main`. **No automatic deployment occurs.**
   449→
   450→**What happens:**
   451→- Main validation runs (validates all changes)
   452→- Plans regenerated to prove deployability
   453→- Release tagged with semantic version (e.g., v1.2.3)
   454→- No infrastructure changes applied
   455→
   456→### 4. Deploy During Change Window
   457→
   458→Navigate to **Actions > Deploy Infrastructure** workflow and click **Run workflow**.
   459→
   460→**Configure deployment:**
   461→
   462→| Input | Description | Example |
   463→|-------|-------------|---------|
   464→| **environment** | Target environment | `dev`, `qa`, `prod`, `shared` |
   465→| **scope** | What to deploy | `network`, `gke`, `data`, `kong`, `all` |
   466→| **dry_run** | Plan only, no apply | `false` (deploy) or `true` (plan only) |
   467→| **auto_approve** | Skip approval (dev only) | `true` (dev) or `false` (qa/prod) |
   468→
   469→**Example: Deploy Redis to Dev**
   470→```yaml
   471→environment: dev
   472→scope: data
   473→dry_run: false
   474→auto_approve: true  # Dev allows auto-approve
   475→```
   476→
   477→**Example: Deploy GKE to Production**
   478→```yaml
   479→environment: prod
   480→scope: gke
   481→dry_run: false
   482→auto_approve: false  # Prod requires approval
   483→```
   484→
   485→**Deployment flow:**
   486→1. **Pre-flight checks** - Validates change window, permissions
   487→2. **Validate** - Format, security scan
   488→3. **Plan** - Generates fresh plan (catches drift)
   489→4. **Approval** - Manual review and approval (QA/Prod)
   490→5. **Apply** - Executes Terraform apply
   491→6. **Verify** - Runs smoke tests
   492→7. **Summary** - Posts deployment report
   493→
   494→### 5. Monitor Deployment
   495→
   496→Watch the workflow run:
   497→- Green checkmarks indicate success
   498→- Review plan output before approval
   499→- Monitor apply progress
   500→- Verify outputs after completion
   501→
   502→### Change Windows
   503→
   504→Infrastructure deployments are restricted by environment:
   505→
   506→| Environment | Change Window | Approval | Notes |
   507→|-------------|---------------|----------|-------|
   508→| **dev** | Anytime | Optional (auto-approve allowed) | Rapid iteration |
   509→| **qa** | Business hours (08:00-18:00 UTC) | Required | Avoid during testing |
   510→| **prod** | **Tue-Thu 20:00-23:00 UTC only** | Required + change ticket | Restricted window |
   511→| **shared** | Business hours (08:00-18:00 UTC) | Required | Impacts all environments |
   512→
   513→**Production restrictions:**
   514→- Deployments outside the window are **automatically blocked**
   515→- Emergency hotfixes require manual approval bypass (see [CI/CD Runbook](/docs/infrastructure-ops/cicd-runbook))
   516→- Change tickets must be referenced in deployment approval
   517→
   518→### Scope Mapping
   519→
   520→The `scope` input maps to Terraform directories:
   521→
   522→| Scope | Description | Directories |
   523→|-------|-------------|-------------|
   524→| `network` | VPC, subnets, firewall | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/network` |
   525→| `security` | Security baseline | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/security` |
   526→| `gke` | GKE cluster | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/gke` |
   527→| `platform` | Namespaces, RBAC | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/platform` |
   528→| `data` | Cloud SQL, Redis, GCS | `terraform/environments/{env}/gcp/data` |
   529→| `kong` | Kong API Gateway | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/kong` |
   530→| `gateway` | GKE Gateway | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/gateway` |
   531→| `litellm` | LiteLLM proxy | `terraform/environments/{env}/kubernetes/litellm` |
   532→| `argocd` | ArgoCD (shared only) | `terraform/environments/shared/kubernetes/argocd` |
   533→| `all` | All of the above | Sequential deployment (network > security > gke > platform > data) |
   534→
   535→### Deployment Best Practices
   536→
   537→**Before deploying:**
   538→- Verify plan output matches intent
   539→- Check for unexpected resource destruction
   540→- Ensure change window compliance (production)
   541→- Notify team in #kix-platform-engineering
   542→
   543→**During deployment:**
   544→- Monitor workflow progress
   545→- Watch for errors in real-time
   546→- Don't close browser until complete
   547→
   548→**After deployment:**
   549→- Verify services are healthy
   550→- Review Terraform outputs
   551→- Monitor metrics for anomalies
   552→- Update deployment log
   553→
   554→### Rollback Procedure
   555→
   556→If deployment causes issues:
   557→
   558→```bash
   559→# Option 1: Revert code and redeploy
   560→git revert <commit-hash>
   561→git push origin main
   562→# Then run deploy workflow with reverted code
   563→
   564→# Option 2: Manual Terraform rollback (emergency only)
   565→cd terraform/environments/{env}/{scope}
   566→terraform init
   567→terraform state pull > backup.tfstate
   568→# Manually fix state or apply reverted config
   569→```
   570→
   571→### Advanced: Drift Detection
   572→
   573→Nightly workflow checks for infrastructure drift:
   574→- Runs daily at 02:00 UTC
   575→- Checks all environments and scopes
   576→- Creates GitHub issues if drift detected
   577→
   578→**Manually trigger drift detection:**
   579→```
   580→Actions > Nightly Quality Checks > Run workflow
   581→```
   582→
   583→### Troubleshooting Deployments
   584→
   585→See [CI/CD Runbook](/docs/infrastructure-ops/cicd-runbook) for detailed troubleshooting:
   586→- Plan shows unexpected changes
   587→- Apply fails with "resource already exists"
   588→- Workflow stuck on approval
   589→- Change window blocked production deployment
   590→
   591→---
   592→
   593→## Contributing
   594→
   595→### Before Contributing
   596→
   597→1. Read `CLAUDE.md` section "Approval Requirements"
   598→2. Create feature branch: `git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name`
   599→3. Follow pre-commit checklist
   600→4. Submit PR for review
   601→
   602→### Good First Contributions
   603→
   604→- Fix documentation typos
   605→- Add examples to module READMEs
   606→- Improve variable descriptions
   607→- Add validation rules
   608→
   609→### Approval Requirements
   610→
   611→| Environment | Approvers |
   612→|-------------|-----------|
   613→| Dev | Infrastructure Lead |
   614→| QA | Infrastructure Lead + DevSecOps Lead |
   615→| Prod | Chief Engineer + Infrastructure Lead + CISO |

   618→
   619→## Troubleshooting
   620→
   621→### Error: "The caller does not have permission"
   622→
   623→```bash
   624→gcloud auth list
   625→gcloud config get-value account
   626→# If wrong account:
   627→gcloud auth login your.email@konecta-group.com
   628→gcloud auth application-default login
   629→```
   630→
   631→### Error: "Failed to save state: AccessDenied"
   632→
   633→```bash
   634→gsutil ls gs://kd-tfstate-dev
   635→terraform init -reconfigure
   636→```
   637→
   638→### Error: "Quota exceeded"
   639→
   640→```bash
   641→gcloud compute project-info describe \
   642→  --project=kd-ix-eur-dev-gke \
   643→  --format="table(quotas.metric,quotas.limit,quotas.usage)"
   644→# Request quota increase in GCP Console
   645→```
   646→
   647→### Error: "Timeout waiting for cluster"
   648→
   649→GKE clusters take 15-20 minutes. Check status:
   650→```bash
   651→gcloud container clusters describe kix-dev-cluster \
   652→  --region=europe-west1 \
   653→  --project=kd-ix-eur-dev-gke
   654→```
   655→
   656→### State Lock Error
   657→
   658→```bash
   659→# Only if certain no other process is running:
   660→terraform force-unlock LOCK_ID
   661→```
   662→
   663→### Debug Logging
   664→
   665→```bash
   666→export TF_LOG=DEBUG
   667→export TF_LOG_PATH=./terraform-debug.log
   668→terraform plan
   669→# Review logs
   670→cat terraform-debug.log
   671→unset TF_LOG TF_LOG_PATH
   672→```
   673→
   674→### Getting Help
   675→
   676→**Include when asking for help:**
   677→1. Full error message
   678→2. Terraform version: `terraform version`
   679→3. Module/environment
   680→4. Steps to reproduce

     1→---
     2→title: Namespaces
     3→sidebar_label: Namespaces
     4→sidebar_position: 6
     5→description: Kubernetes namespace design, RBAC, resource quotas, and network policies
     6→---
     7→
     8→# Namespaces
     9→
    10→Each workload on the KIX Platform runs in a dedicated Kubernetes namespace. Namespaces provide the primary isolation boundary — each one gets its own RBAC roles, resource quotas, network policies, and GCP service account.
    11→
    12→## Namespace Taxonomy
    13→
    14→```
    15→GKE Cluster
    16→├── Platform Namespaces (managed by platform team)
    17→│   ├── kong                      # Kong API Gateway (external APIs only)
    18→│   ├── litellm                   # LiteLLM unified LLM proxy
    19→│   ├── monitoring                # Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Tempo
    20→│   ├── cert-manager              # TLS certificate management
    21→│   └── external-secrets          # Secret Manager sync
    22→│
    23→├── Shared Platform Cluster (kd-ix-eur-shr-platform)
    24→│   └── argocd                    # ArgoCD server, controller, repo-server
    25→│       ├── ApplicationSet controller (auto-generate apps)
    26→│       ├── Image Updater (watch Artifact Registry)
    27→│       ├── Notifications (Google Chat)
    28→│       └── Manages all environment clusters via GitOps
    29→│
    30→└── Use Case Namespaces (defined in config.json)
    31→    ├── autopilot-scheduling-{env}
    32→    │   ├── Use case application (FastAPI/Flask)
    33→    │   ├── CrewAI agent deployment
    34→    │   ├── Per-use-case Cloud SQL instance
    35→    │   ├── Per-use-case GCS buckets
    36→    │   └── Per-use-case Pub/Sub topics
    37→    │
    38→    ├── autopilot-outbound-{env}
    39→    ├── autopilot-inbound-{env}
    40→    └── customer-zero-{env}
    41→```
    42→
    43→## Namespace Naming Conventions
    44→
    45→| Namespace Type | Pattern | Example |
    46→|----------------|---------|---------|
    47→| **Platform services** | `{service-name}` | `kong`, `litellm`, `monitoring` |
    48→| **Use case (dev)** | `{use-case}-dev` | `autopilot-scheduling-dev` |
    49→| **Use case (qa)** | `{use-case}-qa` | `autopilot-scheduling-qa` |
    50→| **Use case (prod)** | `{use-case}-prod` | `autopilot-scheduling-prod` |
    51→
    52→All use case namespaces are defined in the environment's `config.json` file and provisioned automatically by Terraform.
    53→
    54→## RBAC Roles
    55→
    56→Each namespace has role bindings that control who and what can access resources within it.
    57→
    58→### Platform Namespace RBAC
    59→
    60→| Role | Binding | Scope | Who |
    61→|------|---------|-------|-----|
    62→| `cluster-admin` | ClusterRoleBinding | Cluster-wide | Platform engineering team |
    63→| `namespace-admin` | RoleBinding | Platform namespace | Platform service owners |
    64→| `view` | RoleBinding | Platform namespace | All authenticated users |
    65→
    66→### Use Case Namespace RBAC
    67→
    68→| Role | Binding | Scope | Who |
    69→|------|---------|-------|-----|
    70→| `namespace-admin` | RoleBinding | Use case namespace | Use case development team |
    71→| `edit` | RoleBinding | Use case namespace | CI/CD service account (ArgoCD) |
    72→| `view` | RoleBinding | Use case namespace | Platform engineering team |
    73→
    74→The Kubernetes service account in each use case namespace is bound to a GCP service account via Workload Identity, giving it scoped access to only its own GCP resources (secrets, databases, storage).
    75→
    76→## Resource Quotas
    77→
    78→Each use case namespace has resource quotas to prevent any single workload from consuming excessive cluster resources.
    79→
    80→### Default Resource Quotas
    81→
    82→| Resource | Dev | QA | Prod |
    83→|----------|-----|-----|------|
    84→| **CPU requests** | 4 cores | 8 cores | 16 cores |
    85→| **CPU limits** | 8 cores | 16 cores | 32 cores |
    86→| **Memory requests** | 8Gi | 16Gi | 32Gi |
    87→| **Memory limits** | 16Gi | 32Gi | 64Gi |
    88→| **Pods** | 20 | 40 | 80 |
    89→| **Services** | 10 | 10 | 20 |
    90→| **PVCs** | 5 | 5 | 10 |
    91→
    92→Resource quotas are configured per use case in `config.json` and can be adjusted based on workload requirements.
    93→
    94→### Limit Ranges
    95→
    96→In addition to quotas, each namespace has LimitRange defaults to ensure pods always specify resource requests:
    97→
    98→| Setting | Default Request | Default Limit |
    99→|---------|----------------|---------------|
   100→| **CPU** | 100m | 500m |
   101→| **Memory** | 128Mi | 512Mi |
   102→
   103→## Network Policies
   104→
   105→Network policies provide pod-level network isolation within the cluster. Use case namespaces with `network_isolation.enabled = true` have a default-deny-ingress policy, with explicit allow rules for required communication paths.
   106→
   107→### Default Network Policy (Use Case Namespace)
   108→
   109→```yaml
   110→apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
   111→kind: NetworkPolicy
   112→metadata:
   113→  name: use-case-default
   114→  namespace: autopilot-scheduling-dev
   115→spec:
   116→  podSelector: {}
   117→  policyTypes:
   118→    - Ingress
   119→    - Egress
   120→
   121→  ingress:
   122→    # Allow from Kong ingress controller
   123→    - from:
   124→        - namespaceSelector:
   125→            matchLabels:
   126→              app.kubernetes.io/component: api-gateway
   127→      ports:
   128→        - protocol: TCP
   129→          port: 8080
   130→
   131→  egress:
   132→    # Allow to LiteLLM
   133→    - to:
   134→        - namespaceSelector:
   135→            matchLabels:
   136→              app.kubernetes.io/component: llm-proxy
   137→      ports:
   138→        - protocol: TCP
   139→          port: 80
   140→
   141→    # Allow to Kong for external API calls
   142→    - to:
   143→        - namespaceSelector:
   144→            matchLabels:
   145→              app.kubernetes.io/component: api-gateway
   146→      ports:
   147→        - protocol: TCP
   148→          port: 80
   149→
   150→    # Allow to Cloud SQL (private IP range)
   151→    - to:
   152→        - ipBlock:
   153→            cidr: 10.1.0.0/24
   154→      ports:
   155→        - protocol: TCP
   156→          port: 5432
   157→
   158→    # Allow to GCP APIs via Private Google Access
   159→    - to:
   160→        - ipBlock:
   161→            cidr: 199.36.153.4/30
   162→      ports:
   163→        - protocol: TCP
   164→          port: 443
   165→
   166→    # Allow DNS resolution
   167→    - to:
   168→        - namespaceSelector: {}
   169→          podSelector:
   170→            matchLabels:
   171→              k8s-app: kube-dns
   172→      ports:
   173→        - protocol: UDP
   174→          port: 53
   175→```
   176→
   177→### GCP Health Check IPs (Mandatory)
   178→
   179→When `network_isolation.enabled = true`, you **must** allow GCP health check IPs in the ingress rules. Without these, the load balancer marks backends as unhealthy and traffic does not flow.
   180→
   181→```json
   182→{
   183→  "allowed_ingress": [
   184→    {"cidr_block": "35.191.0.0/16", "ports": [{"port": 8080, "protocol": "TCP"}]},
   185→    {"cidr_block": "130.211.0.0/22", "ports": [{"port": 8080, "protocol": "TCP"}]}
   186→  ]
   187→}
   188→```
   189→
   190→**Why this matters:** 70% of network policy issues stem from missing GCP health check IP ranges. These IP ranges are where Google Cloud load balancer health checks originate. If they are blocked, backends are marked unhealthy and no traffic is served.
   191→
   192→### Network Policy Summary by Source
   193→
   194→| Source | Allowed Target | Port | Purpose |
   195→|--------|---------------|------|---------|
   196→| GCP health checks (`35.191.0.0/16`, `130.211.0.0/22`) | Use case pods | TCP 8080 | Load balancer health checks |
   197→| Kong namespace | Use case pods | TCP 8080 | Ingress routing |
   198→| Use case pods | LiteLLM namespace | TCP 80 | LLM API access |
   199→| Use case pods | Kong namespace | TCP 80 | External API access |
   200→| Use case pods | Cloud SQL CIDR | TCP 5432 | Database access |
   201→| Use case pods | Private Google Access | TCP 443 | GCP APIs (GCS, Pub/Sub, etc.) |
   202→| Use case pods | kube-dns | UDP 53 | DNS resolution |
   203→
   204→## Use Case Isolation Model
   205→
   206→Each use case is isolated at multiple levels:
   207→
   208→| Isolation Layer | Mechanism | What It Provides |
   209→|----------------|-----------|-----------------|
   210→| **Namespace** | Kubernetes namespace | Logical boundary for all resources |
   211→| **RBAC** | RoleBindings per namespace | Access control for team members |
   212→| **Network** | NetworkPolicy per namespace | Pod-level traffic control |
   213→| **Identity** | Workload Identity per namespace | Scoped GCP access |
   214→| **Resources** | ResourceQuota per namespace | Fair share of cluster resources |
   215→| **Data** | Per-use-case Cloud SQL, GCS, Pub/Sub | Data isolation |
   216→| **Secrets** | Per-use-case Secret Manager secrets | Credential isolation |
   217→
   218→## Environment Differentiation
   219→
   220→Settings vary by environment via `config.json`:
   221→
   222→| Setting | Dev | QA | Prod |
   223→|---------|-----|-----|------|
   224→| `cloud_sql.availability_type` | ZONAL | ZONAL | REGIONAL |
   225→| `cloud_sql.deletion_protection` | false | false | true |
   226→| `cloud_sql.point_in_time_recovery` | false | false | true |
   227→| `gcs.force_destroy` | true | true | false |
   228→| `namespace.network_isolation.allow_egress_internet` | true | true | false |
   229→| `litellm.replicas` | 1 | 2 | 3 |
   230→| `kong_gateway.enable_admin_api` | true | true | false |
   231→
```

     5→description: "Guide for use case developers building AI agents and services on the KIX Platform"
     6→---
     7→
     8→# Developer Guide
     9→
    10→This guide explains how to build services on the KIX Platform. It covers what the platform provides, how to build use cases, service patterns, and technology specifications.
    11→
    12→**Audience:** Use case developers building on KIX
    13→
    14→## Architecture Layers
    15→
    16→| Layer | Purpose | Components |
    17→|-------|---------|------------|
    18→| **Northbound** | Service exposure to consumers | Kong API Gateway, LiteLLM MCP Gateway, Admin UI |
    19→| **Capability** | Business logic and orchestration | Control Plane, Agents, Voice, Messaging, Knowledge |
    20→| **Southbound** | Infrastructure (abstracted) | GCP services, databases, storage, events |
    21→
    22→## Service Consumption Model
    23→
    24→Consumers access platform capabilities through three methods:
    25→
    26→| Method | Consumer Type | Authentication |
    27→|--------|---------------|----------------|
    28→| REST API (Kong) | External systems, applications | API Key or JWT |
    29→| MCP Tools (LiteLLM) | AI agents | Service account |
    30→| Admin UI | Internal users | OIDC |
    31→
    32→All requests are authenticated, routed through the appropriate gateway, and executed by the capability layer. Infrastructure is never exposed directly to consumers.
    33→
    34→## Sections
    35→
    36→- **[Platform Overview](./platform-overview)** — What the platform provides and what developers build
    37→- **[Building Use Cases](./building-use-cases)** — Service patterns, development flow, and deployment
    38→- **[Technology Specs](./technology-specs)** — Detailed specifications for each platform component
    39→- **[Use Case Examples](./use-case-examples)** — Real-world use case implementations
    40→- **[Testing](./testing)** — Writing and running tests
    41→
    42→## Related Documentation
    43→
    44→- [Platform Architecture](/docs/architecture) — Technical infrastructure details
    45→- [Onboarding](/docs/getting-started/onboarding) — Getting started with the repository
    46→- [Strategy](/docs/strategy) — Platform vision and business goals
    47→
