     1→---
     2→title: "Platform Overview"
     3→sidebar_label: "Platform Overview"
     4→sidebar_position: 2
     5→description: "What the KIX Platform provides to use case developers and what developers are responsible for building"
     6→---
     7→
     8→# Platform Overview
     9→
    10→## What the Platform Provides
    11→
    12→When a use case is onboarded, the platform automatically provisions:
    13→
    14→| Resource | Description |
    15→|----------|-------------|
    16→| **Kubernetes Namespace** | Isolated environment for workloads |
    17→| **PostgreSQL Database** | Dedicated database with credentials |
    18→| **Redis Key Prefix** | Shared cache with isolated keyspace |
    19→| **GCS Bucket** | Object storage for documents and artifacts |
    20→| **Pub/Sub Topic** | Event bus for async messaging |
    21→| **Kong Routes** | API endpoints at `/api/v1/{use-case}/*` |
    22→| **Secrets Folder** | Secret Manager path for credentials |
    23→| **Service Account** | GCP identity with least-privilege permissions |
    24→| **Observability** | Pre-configured dashboard, logs, and traces |
    25→| **Identity** | Identity services abstracting credential handling |
    26→| **Security** | Security monitoring, WAF, and firewall services |
    27→| **Service Catalogue** | Backstage portal for discovering available services |
    28→
    29→### Service Discovery via Backstage
    30→
    31→Use case developers discover available platform services through **Backstage**, the internal service catalogue:
    32→
    33→| What You Can Discover | Examples |
    34→|----------------------|----------|
    35→| **Platform Services** | LiteLLM endpoints, Kong routes, MCP tools |
    36→| **Data Services** | Available databases, Redis instances, GCS buckets |
    37→| **CrewAI Agents** | Existing agents you can call or integrate with |
    38→| **Pub/Sub Topics** | Event bus topics for async messaging |
    39→| **API Schemas** | OpenAPI specs for all platform APIs |
    40→| **Documentation** | Tech docs aggregated from all services |
    41→
    42→Access Backstage at: `https://backstage.kix.konecta.com` (internal only)
    43→
    44→### What Developers CAN Access
    45→
    46→- Kubernetes namespace (isolated)
    47→- Database connection (their database only)
    48→- Cache client (their key prefix only)
    49→- Storage bucket (their bucket only)
    50→- Pub/Sub topic (their topic only)
    51→
    52→### What Developers CANNOT Access
    53→
    54→- GCP console directly
    55→- Other use case resources
    56→- Organization-level settings
    57→- Service account keys
    58→
    59→## What Developers Build
    60→
    61→| Component | Responsibility |
    62→|-----------|----------------|
    63→| **Agent Logic** | Business logic using CrewAI framework |
    64→| **API Endpoints** | Request handlers behind Kong routes |
    65→| **Data Schema** | Database tables and vector collections |
    66→| **Prompts** | LLM prompts and configurations |
    67→| **Workflows** | Multi-step orchestration (if needed) |
    68→
    69→## BAOE Readiness Framework
    70→
    71→A use case is **AVAILABLE** when it meets all four readiness dimensions:
    72→
    73→| Dimension | Code | Description |
    74→|-----------|------|-------------|
    75→| **Built** | B | Autopilot flow completed in ElevenLabs/CrewAI |
    76→| **API-fied** | A | Standard Agent API contracts, lifecycle APIs |
    77→| **Observable** | O | Telemetry, decision logging, audit trails |
    78→| **Platform-Enabled** | E | Configuration-driven deployment, tenant isolation |
    79→
    80→**Progression Example:**
    81→```
    82→Month 1: B . A . O      -> Flow built, APIs ready, observable
    83→Month 2: B . A . O . E  -> Fully platform-enabled
    84→Month 3: AVAILABLE      -> Production-ready
    85→```
    86→
    87→## Autonomy Tiers
    88→
    89→Each use case operates at a specific autonomy tier:
    90→
    91→| Tier | Description | Human Involvement | Example |
    92→|------|-------------|-------------------|---------|
    93→| **Supervised** | Human monitors all actions | High — approval required | FAQ, Password Reset |
    94→| **Conditional** | Autonomous within bounds, escalates on triggers | Medium — exception handling | Scheduling, Collections |
    95→| **Assistive** | AI assists human decision-making | Medium — human leads | Copilot Sales |
    96→| **Full** | Fully autonomous, rare and restricted | Low — audit only | Simple bookings |
    97→
    98→### Escalation Triggers
    99→
   100→| Trigger | Action | Target |
   101→|---------|--------|--------|
   102→| Customer says "supervisor" | Immediate transfer | Human Expert |
   103→| Sentiment drops below threshold | Flag + optional transfer | Copilot Assisted |
   104→| Compliance violation detected | Immediate transfer | Human Expert |
   105→| Agent confidence below 70% | Request human review | Copilot Assisted |
   106→| 3+ failed resolution attempts | Escalate | Human Expert |
   107→

{
  "file_path": "/home/nathan_booth/code/konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-docs/docs/developer-guide/branching-strategy.md",
  "content": "---\ntitle: \"Branching Strategy\"\nsidebar_label: \"Branching Strategy\"\nsidebar_position: 4\ndescription: \"Gitflow branching model and branch-to-environment mapping for KIX Platform repositories\"\n---\n\n# Branching Strategy\n\nAll KIX Platform code and workload repositories follow a **Gitflow** branching model. Each long-lived branch maps to a deployment environment — merging to a branch automatically triggers deployment to the corresponding environment via CI/CD.\n\n## Branch-to-Environment Mapping\n\n| Branch | Environment | Deployment | Notes |\n|--------|-------------|------------|-------|\n| `develop` | **Dev** | Automatic on push | Integration branch — all feature work merges here first |\n| `main` | **QA** | Automatic on push | Promoted code under test — merge `develop` → `main` when ready for QA |\n| `v*` tags | **Prod** | Automatic on tag | Tagged releases only — create a tag from `main` after QA sign-off |\n\n```\nfeature/* ──PR──▶ develop ──merge──▶ main ──tag v1.2.0──▶ Production\n                     │                  │                       │\n                     ▼                  ▼                       ▼\n                   Dev env           QA env                 Prod env\n```\n\n## Branch Lifecycle\n\n### Feature Branches\n\nAll development happens on short-lived feature branches created from `develop`:\n\n```bash\n# Create feature branch\ngit checkout develop\ngit pull origin develop\ngit checkout -b feature/add-auth-endpoint\n\n# Work, commit, push\ngit add src/auth.py\ngit commit -m \"feat: add OAuth2 token endpoint\"\ngit push -u origin feature/add-auth-endpoint\n\n# Open PR to develop\ngh pr create --base develop --title \"feat: add OAuth2 token endpoint\"\n```\n\nFeature branches are deleted after merging.\n\n### Promotion Flow\n\n#### Dev → QA\n\nWhen features are ready for QA testing, merge `develop` into `main`:\n\n```bash\ngit checkout main\ngit pull origin main\ngit merge develop\ngit push origin main\n# QA environment deploys automatically\n```\n\n#### QA → Prod\n\nAfter QA sign-off, create a versioned tag from `main`:\n\n```bash\ngit checkout main\ngit pull origin main\ngit tag v1.2.0\ngit push origin v1.2.0\n# Production environment deploys automatically\n```\n\n### Hotfix Branches\n\nFor urgent production fixes, create a hotfix branch from `main`:\n\n```bash\ngit checkout main\ngit checkout -b hotfix/fix-auth-crash\n\n# Fix, commit, push\ngit commit -m \"fix: handle null token in auth middleware\"\ngit push -u origin hotfix/fix-auth-crash\n\n# PR to main (deploys to QA for verification)\ngh pr create --base main --title \"fix: handle null token in auth middleware\"\n\n# After QA verification, tag for prod\ngit checkout main\ngit pull origin main\ngit tag v1.2.1\ngit push origin v1.2.1\n\n# Back-merge to develop\ngit checkout develop\ngit merge main\ngit push origin develop\n```\n\n## Repository-Specific Notes\n\n### Code Repos (konecta-ix-applications, konecta-ix-mcp-servers)\n\nCode repositories contain application source code and Dockerfiles. The CI pipeline (defined in `.github-private` per org) builds and pushes container images to Artifact Registry on every push to `develop` or `main`.\n\n| Event | CI Action |\n|-------|-----------|\n| Push to `develop` | Build image, push with `dev-<sha>` tag |\n| Push to `main` | Build image, push with `qa-<sha>` tag |\n| Tag `v*` | Build image, push with version tag (e.g., `v1.2.0`) |\n\n### Workload Repos (konecta-ix-workloads)\n\nWorkload repositories contain Helm charts, ArgoCD manifests, and Terraform. ArgoCD watches these repos and syncs changes automatically:\n\n| Branch/Tag | ArgoCD `targetRevision` | Destination |\n|------------|------------------------|-------------|\n| `develop` | `develop` | `dev-{workload}` namespace |\n| `main` | `main` | `qa-{workload}` namespace |\n| `v*` tag | `v1.2.0` | `prod-{workload}` namespace |\n\n### Infrastructure Repos (konecta-ix-platform)\n\nInfrastructure repositories follow a different model — changes are validated via PR, merged to `main`, and then deployed manually via GitHub Actions workflow dispatch. See [Onboarding — Deploying Infrastructure Changes](/docs/getting-started/onboarding#deploying-infrastructure-changes) for details.\n\n## Branch Protection Rules\n\nAll repositories enforce branch protection on `develop` and `main`:\n\n| Rule | `develop` | `main` |\n|------|-----------|--------|\n| Require PR | Yes | Yes |\n| Required reviewers | 1 | 1 |\n| Require status checks | CI pass | CI pass |\n| Require linear history | No | No |\n| Allow force push | No | No |\n| Allow deletions | No | No |\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n```bash\n# Start feature work\ngit checkout develop && git pull\ngit checkout -b feature/my-feature\n\n# Promote to QA\ngit checkout main && git merge develop && git push\n\n# Release to Prod\ngit tag v1.2.0 && git push origin v1.2.0\n\n# Hotfix\ngit checkout main && git checkout -b hotfix/fix-issue\n# After merge to main:\ngit tag v1.2.1 && git push origin v1.2.1\ngit checkout develop && git merge main && git push\n```\n"
}
```

    1→---\n     2→title: Kong API Gateway\n     3→sidebar_label: Kong Gateway\n     4→sidebar_position: 1\n     5→description: Using Kong Gateway for API management, authentication, and traffic routing\n     6→---\n     7→\n     8→# Kong API Gateway\n     9→\n    10→## Overview\n    11→\n    12→Kong Gateway provides enterprise API management capabilities for the KIX Platform, including traffic routing, authentication, rate limiting, and 3rd party API abstraction.\n    13→\n    14→**Use Kong Gateway when you need:**\n    15→- External API access (public internet → your services)\n    16→- Centralized authentication (API keys, OAuth, JWT)\n    17→- Rate limiting and throttling\n    18→- Request/response transformation\n    19→- API analytics and monitoring\n    20→- 3rd party API abstraction (Salesforce, Google Calendar, telephony)\n    21→\n    22→**Available In:** dev, qa, prod environments\n    23→\n    24→**Access:** `https://api.{env}.ix.konecta-digital.com`\n    25→\n    26→---\n    27→\n    28→## Quick Start\n    29→\n    30→### Prerequisites\n    31→\n    32→- Service deployed on KIX Platform (see [Deploy First Service](/docs/developer-guide/deploy-first-service))\n    33→- Service has Kubernetes Service resource\n    34→- (Optional) API key for authentication\n    35→\n    36→### Step 1: Create HTTPRoute\n    37→\n    38→Create `httproute.yaml` in your Helm chart:\n    39→\n    40→```yaml\n    41→apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1\n    42→kind: HTTPRoute\n    43→metadata:\n    44→  name: my-service\n    45→  namespace: my-service\n    46→spec:\n    47→  parentRefs:\n    48→    - name: kong-gateway\n    49→      namespace: kong\n    50→      sectionName: https\n    51→  hostnames:\n    52→    - api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com\n    53→  rules:\n    54→    - matches:\n    55→        - path:\n    56→            type: PathPrefix\n    57→            value: /my-service\n    58→      backendRefs:\n    59→        - name: my-service\n    60→          port: 8080\n    61→```\n    62→\n    63→### Step 2: Apply HTTPRoute\n    64→\n    65→```bash\n    66→kubectl apply -f httproute.yaml\n    67→\n    68→# Verify route accepted\n    69→kubectl get httproute -n my-service my-service\n    70→```\n    71→\n    72→### Step 3: Test Route\n    73→\n    74→```bash\n    75→# Test via Kong Gateway\n    76→curl https://api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com/my-service/health\n    77→```\n    78→\n    79→**That's it!** Your service is now accessible via Kong Gateway.\n    80→"}]},"uuid":"096b33c7-14a1-4a2b-8bad-36486955998b","timestamp":"2026-02-16T17:43:09.540Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"13cfc991-83fa-4b1b-8d6e-fe6c14bba0e8"}

    1→---\n     2→title: LiteLLM Gateway\n     3→sidebar_label: LiteLLM Gateway\n     4→sidebar_position: 2\n     5→description: Using LiteLLM for AI model routing, load balancing, and cost tracking\n     6→---\n     7→\n     8→# LiteLLM Gateway\n     9→\n    10→## Overview\n    11→\n    12→LiteLLM Gateway provides unified access to multiple AI/LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Azure, etc.) with intelligent routing, load balancing, cost tracking, and fallback capabilities.\n    13→\n    14→**Use LiteLLM Gateway when you need:**\n    15→- Call multiple LLM providers with a single API\n    16→- Load balancing across models and regions\n    17→- Automatic fallback when models are unavailable\n    18→- Cost tracking and budgeting\n    19→- Caching to reduce costs\n    20→- Rate limiting per model/user\n    21→- Centralized API key management\n    22→\n    23→**Supported Providers:**\n    24→- OpenAI (GPT-4, GPT-3.5)\n    25→- Anthropic (Claude Sonnet, Opus, Haiku)\n    26→- Google (Gemini Pro, Gemini Ultra)\n    27→- Azure OpenAI\n    28→- AWS Bedrock\n    29→- Cohere, Together AI, Replicate, and 100+ more\n    30→\n    31→**Available In:** dev, qa, prod environments\n    32→\n    33→**Access:** `https://litellm.{env}.ix.konecta-digital.com` (via IAP + Kong)\n    34→\n    35→---\n    36→\n    37→## Quick Start\n    38→\n    39→### Prerequisites\n    40→\n    41→- Kong API key (for authentication)\n    42→- LiteLLM base URL: `https://api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com/llm`\n    43→- (Optional) Admin UI access via IAP\n    44→\n    45→### Step 1: Get Your API Key\n    46→\n    47→Request Kong API key from Platform Engineering team (or generate via Kong Admin API if authorized).\n    48→\n    49→```bash\n    50→# Test authentication\n    51→curl -H \"apikey=[REDACTED]\" \\\n    52→  https://api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com/llm/health\n    53→```\n    54→\n    55→### Step 2: Make Your First Request\n    56→\n    57→:::warning Authentication Header\n    58→Kong's `key-auth` plugin expects the API key in an `apikey` header by default, but the OpenAI SDK sends credentials via `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. The Kong plugin for LiteLLM is configured to accept keys from the `apikey` header. When using the OpenAI SDK, pass the key via `default_headers` instead of `api_key`:\n    59→:::\n    60→\n    61→**OpenAI-compatible API:**\n    62→\n    63→```python\n    64→import openai\n    65→\n    66→client = openai.OpenAI(\n    67→    base_url=\"https://api.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com/llm\",\n    68→    api_key=\"not-used\",  # Required by SDK but not used for auth\n    69→    default_headers={\"apikey\": \"your-kong-api-key\"}\n    70→)\n    71→\n    72→response = client.chat.completions.create(\n    73→    model=\"gpt-4\",\n    74→    messages=[\n    75→        {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"Hello, how are you?\"}\n    76→    ]\n    77→)\n    78→\n    79→print(response.choices[0].message.content)\n    80→```"}]},"uuid":"19db631c-e91e-4f03-ab62-7c3c05da20d6","timestamp":"2026-02-16T17:43:09.541Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"6f8a305c-bb49-4fdd-9907-06842208e675"}

   181→        - namespaceSelector:
   182→            matchLabels:
   183→              name: shared-kong
   184→      ports:
   185→        - protocol: TCP
   186→          port: 8000
   187→```
   188→
   189→## TLS Configuration
   190→
   191→### Certificate Management
   192→
   193→- **cert-manager** in `shared-cert-manager` namespace
   194→- **Let's Encrypt** issuer for automatic certificates
   195→- Separate certificates per domain
   196→
   197→### DNS by Environment
   198→
   199→| Environment | API Domain | Frontend Domain |
   200→|-------------|------------|-----------------|
   201→| Dev | `dev.api.ix.konecta-digital.com` | `dev.app.ix.konecta-digital.com` |
   202→| QA | `qa.api.ix.konecta-digital.com` | `qa.app.ix.konecta-digital.com` |
   203→| Prod | `api.ix.konecta-digital.com` | `app.ix.konecta-digital.com` |
   204→
   205→### Service-Specific Domains
   206→
   207→Frontend services get dedicated subdomains:
   208→
   209→| Service | Dev | Prod |
   210→|---------|-----|------|
   211→| IQ Portal | `iq-portal.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com` | `iq-portal.app.ix.konecta-digital.com` |
   212→| HR Fraud | `hrfraud.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com` | `hrfraud.app.ix.konecta-digital.com` |
   213→
   214→## Ingress Resource Examples
   215→
   216→### Kong Ingress (API)
   217→
   218→```yaml
   219→apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
   220→kind: Ingress
   221→metadata:
   222→  name: kix-mcp-gateway
   223→  namespace: dev-mcp-gateway
   224→  annotations:
   225→    kubernetes.io/ingress.class: kong
   226→    konghq.com/strip-path: "true"
   227→    konghq.com/protocols: "https"
   228→    konghq.com/plugins: rate-limiting-plugin
   229→spec:
   230→  rules:
   231→    - host: api.ix.konecta-digital.com
   232→      http:
   233→        paths:
   234→          - path: /mcp-gateway
   235→            pathType: Prefix
   236→            backend:
   237→              service:
   238→                name: kix-mcp-gateway
   239→                port:
   240→                  number: 8080
   241→  tls:
   242→    - hosts:
   243→        - api.ix.konecta-digital.com
   244→      secretName: api-tls-secret
   245→```
   246→
   247→### GKE Gateway API (Frontend)
   248→
   249→```yaml
   250→apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
   251→kind: HTTPRoute
   252→metadata:
   253→  name: kix-usecase-iq-portal
   254→  namespace: dev-iqportal
   255→spec:
   256→  parentRefs:
   257→    - name: frontend-gateway
   258→      namespace: shared-gateway
   259→  hostnames:
   260→    - iq-portal.dev.ix.konecta-digital.com
   261→  rules:
   262→    - matches:
   263→        - path:
   264→            type: PathPrefix
   265→            value: /
   266→      backendRefs:
   267→        - name: kix-usecase-iq-portal
   268→          port: 3000
   269→```
   270→
   271→### BackendConfig for IAP
   272→
   273→```yaml
   274→apiVersion: cloud.google.com/v1
   275→kind: BackendConfig
   276→metadata:
   277→  name: kix-usecase-iq-portal-iap
   278→  namespace: dev-iqportal
   279→spec:
   280→  iap:
   281→    enabled: true
   282→    oauthclientCredentials:
   283→      secretName: iap-oauth-credentials
   284→```

     1→---
     2→title: Migration Phases
     3→sidebar_label: Migration Phases
     4→sidebar_position: 4
     5→description: Phased migration strategy with priorities and timeline
     6→---
     7→
     8→# Migration Phases
     9→
    10→This document describes the phased approach to migrating services from Cloud Run to kix-infrastructure.
    11→
    12→## Migration Context
    13→
    14→**No services are currently in production.** Services will migrate directly to new domains on kix-infrastructure — no dual-stack, no DNS cutover, no downtime concerns.
    15→
    16→All application services are **stateless** — state lives in Cloud SQL, Firestore, and GCS. Container images contain no data; configuration is provided via ConfigMaps and Secrets.
    17→
    18→## Migration Priority
    19→
    20→| Priority | Services | Rationale |
    21→|----------|----------|-----------|
    22→| **P0 — Pilot** | kix-usecase-iq-portal (backend + frontend) | Validates entire platform: both ingress paths, Cloud SQL sidecar, standard pipeline, cross-org dispatch |
    23→| **P1 — Platform Core** | Kong, LiteLLM (behind Kong), MCP Gateway | Must be running before other services can function |
    24→| **P2 — MCP Servers** | Remaining 13 MCP servers | Foundation for AI/business workflows |
    25→| **P3 — Business Apps** | kix-app-hrfraud, kix-app-hrportal, kix-usecase-testiq | Remaining user-facing applications |
    26→| **P4 — Data & Demos** | RAG pipelines, bot, prototypes | Lower priority, migrate last |
    27→
    28→## Phase 1: Platform Foundation + Pilot
    29→
    30→**Focus**: Establish platform infrastructure and validate with the pilot service.
    31→
    32→### Platform Infrastructure Tasks
    33→
    34→| Task | Repository | Description |
    35→|------|------------|-------------|
    36→| Create shared CI workflows | `.github-private` per code org | Standard pipeline with reusable workflows |
    37→| Create workload template | `kix-platform-workload-template` | Helm chart templates, ArgoCD manifests, Terraform scaffolding |
    38→| Configure ArgoCD | `kix-platform-infrastructure` | ApplicationSets with git directory generator |
    39→| Create service template | `kix-platform-service-template` | Template repo for bootstrapping |
    40→| Install GitHub App | Cross-org | Enable cross-org dispatch for GitOps updates |
    41→| Configure OIDC | Per org | GitHub OIDC → GCP Workload Identity Pool |
    42→| Deploy Kong + LiteLLM | `shared-kong`, `shared-litellm` | API gateway and LLM proxy |
    43→| Deploy Backstage | `shared-backstage` | Developer portal with GitHub org discovery |
    44→
    45→### Pilot: IQ Portal
    46→
    47→Deploy `kix-usecase-iq-portal` as the first service through the full pipeline:
    48→
    49→| Validation Point | Description |
    50→|------------------|-------------|
    51→| **Backend deployment** | Kong API ingress, Cloud SQL Auth Proxy sidecar, External Secrets |
    52→| **Frontend deployment** | GKE Gateway API + IAP ingress path, separate LB |
    53→| **Helm chart profiles** | Both API Service and Frontend profiles |
    54→| **Cross-org dispatch** | konecta-ix-workloads → konecta-ix-platform GitOps |
    55→| **Full CI pipeline** | Build, scan, sign, push, deploy |
    56→
    57→**Outcome**: Fix any issues in Helm charts, CI workflows, or ArgoCD config before scaling out.
    58→
    59→**Detailed guide**: [IQ Portal Migration Guide](service-guides/iq-portal)
    60→
```

### Key Facts

- **Service name**: `kon-iq-portal` (current) -> `kix-app-iqportal` (target)
- **Code repo**: `konecta-ix-applications/kix-app-iqportal`
- **Workload repo**: `konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-iqportal`
- **Phase**: P0 (Pilot) -- this is the FIRST service migrated and validates the entire platform
- **Architecture**: Single-container monolith (Express.js + Nuxt 4 SPA), port 8080
- **Current hosting**: Cloud Run with Cloud Build from Bitbucket

---

## PHASE 0: PREREQUISITES (Platform Infrastructure)

These must be completed BEFORE IQ Portal migration can begin. Owned by the **Platform Engineering team** in `konecta-ix-platform`.

### P0-1: Create shared CI workflows
- **Repo**: `konecta-ix-applications/.github-private`
- **Task**: Create the shared reusable workflow `standard-pipeline.yaml` and all sub-workflows (`_lint-and-test.yaml`, `_secret-scan.yaml`, `_sca.yaml`, `_sast.yaml`, `_build-image.yaml`, `_container-scan-sign.yaml`, `_push-registry.yaml`, `_promote.yaml`, `_dast.yaml`)
- **Dependencies**: None
- **Validation**: A test repo can call the shared workflow and complete all 7 stages successfully

### P0-2: Create workload template repository
- **Repo**: `konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-workload-template`
- **Task**: Create template repo containing scaffolded `helm/`, `argocd/`, `terraform/`, `.github/workflows/deploy.yaml`, `catalog-info.yaml`, `CODEOWNERS`
- **Dependencies**: None
- **Validation**: `gh repo create --template` produces a valid workload repo skeleton

### P0-3: Create service template repository
- **Repo**: `konecta-ix-platform/kix-platform-service-template`
- **Task**: Create template repo for code repositories containing standard `Dockerfile`, `.github/workflows/ci.yaml`, `catalog-info.yaml`, `docs/index.md`, `.dockerignore`, `CODEOWNERS`, `.env.example`
- **Dependencies**: P0-1 (shared workflows must exist for ci.yaml to reference)
- **Validation**: `gh repo create --template` produces a valid code repo skeleton

### P0-4: Configure ArgoCD for workload repos
- **Repo**: `kix-platform-infrastructure`
- **Task**: Configure ArgoCD to watch `konecta-ix-workloads` org repos. Set up ArgoCD Projects (`dev-project`, `qa-project`, `prod-project`) with RBAC isolation per environment. Configure sync policies (dev=auto, qa=manual, prod=manual)
- **Dependencies**: None
- **Validation**: ArgoCD recognizes Application manifests from workload repos

### P0-5: Install GitHub App for cross-org dispatch
- **Repo**: Cross-org configuration
- **Task**: Install GitHub App to enable cross-org dispatch for GitOps updates between code orgs and workload org

## PHASE 3: DOCKERFILE CHANGES

### P3-1: Pin base image digests
- **Repo**: `konecta-ix-applications/kix-app-iqportal`
- **Task**: Replace all `FROM node:22-alpine` with `FROM node:22-alpine@sha256:<current-digest>` in every stage. Get current digest via `docker inspect --format='{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' node:22-alpine`
- **Dependencies**: P1-3
- **Validation**: `docker build` succeeds with pinned digests; no mutable tags in Dockerfile

### P3-2: Remove HEALTHCHECK instruction
- **Repo**: `konecta-ix-applications/kix-app-iqportal`
- **Task**: Delete the `HEALTHCHECK` block (lines 142-157 in current Dockerfile). K8s probes replace it
- **Dependencies**: P1-3
- **Validation**: No `HEALTHCHECK` instruction in Dockerfile

### P3-3: Ensure non-root user (UID 65532)
- **Repo**: `konecta-ix-applications/kix-app-iqportal`
- **Task**: Verify Dockerfile uses `USER 65532` or `USER appuser` (UID 65532) before `ENTRYPOINT`. If not present, add it. Required by pod security policy (`runAsNonRoot: true`)
- **Dependencies**: P1-3
- **Validation**: `docker inspect` shows user is not root

### P3-4: Add OCI labels
- **Repo**: `konecta-ix-applications/kix-app-iqportal`
- **Task**: Add OCI labels to final stage: `org.opencontainers.image.created`, `org.opencontainers.image.revision`, `org.opencontainers.image.version`, `org.opencontainers.image.source`, `org.opencontainers.image.title`, `org.opencontainers.image.vendor`
- **Dependencies**: P1-3
- **Validation**: `docker inspect` shows OCI labels populated

### P3-5: Ensure no secrets baked into image
- **Repo**: `konecta-ix-applications/kix-app-iqportal`
- **Task**: Verify no `.env` files, secrets, or credentials are copied into the image. All config via K8s ConfigMaps/Secrets. Build secrets (if any) must use `docker build --secret`
- **Dependencies**: P1-3
- **Validation**: Trivy filesystem secret scan passes; no `.env` files in image layers

### P3-6: Ensure multi-stage build has production-only deps
- **Repo**: `konecta-ix-applications/kix-app-iqportal`
- **Task**: Verify the final runtime stage has only production dependencies (`npm prune --omit=dev`). No build tools in final image
- **Dependencies**: P1-3
- **Validation**: Image size within target (< 80MB for Node.js/Nuxt); no devDependencies present

  - `deployment.yaml` -- Pod spec with app container + cloud-sql-proxy sidecar
  - `service.yaml` -- K8s Service on port 8080
  - `ingress.yaml` -- Kong Ingress for `/api/iq-portal` + GKE Gateway API HTTPRoute for frontend
  - `hpa.yaml` -- HorizontalPodAutoscaler (1-5 replicas, 70% CPU target)

  - `networkpolicy.yaml` -- Default deny ingress + allow GCP health checks + allow from Kong + allow from Gateway
  - `serviceaccount.yaml` -- With Workload Identity annotation

  - Cloud SQL Proxy: enabled, instance connection name, port 5432
  - Service account with Workload Identity annotation
  - Probes: liveness (`/health`), readiness (`/api/health`), startup (`/health` with failureThreshold=12)
  - HPA: min=1, max=5, target CPU=70%
  - Services: API (Kong, path `/api/iq-portal`, stripPath=true) + Frontend (Gateway API, host `iq.<env>.ix.konecta-digital.com`)

## PHASE 5: CI/CD PIPELINE (Code Repo)

### P5-1: Create CI workflow
- **Repo**: `konecta-ix-applications/kix-app-iqportal`
- **Task**: Create `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` calling the shared pipeline:
  ```yaml
  uses: konecta-ix-applications/.github-private/.github/workflows/standard-pipeline.yaml@main
  with:
    service-name: kix-app-iqportal
    dockerfile-path: ./Dockerfile
    node-version: "22"
    build-args: |
      VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=${{ vars.VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID }}
      NUXT_PUBLIC_ENVIRONMENT=${{ vars.ENVIRONMENT }}
      COMMIT_SHA=${{ github.sha }}
    skip-tests: true
  ```
  Triggers: push to `develop`/`main`, PR to `main`

## PHASE 12: ENVIRONMENT PROMOTION

### P12-1: Promote to QA
- **Repo**: `konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-iqportal`
- **Task**:
  1. Verify service healthy in dev (Phase 11 passed)
  2. Create `qa-iqportal` namespace (same process as P7-2)
  3. Run Terraform for QA environment (secrets, IAM)
  4. Update `helm/values-qa.yaml` with image tag from dev
  5. Create ArgoCD Application for QA (or update targetRevision)
  6. Manual sync in ArgoCD during change window (08:00-18:00 UTC Mon-Fri)
- **Dependencies**: All Phase 11 tasks pass
- **Validation**: Service running and healthy in `qa-iqportal` namespace

### P12-2: Run DAST scan against QA
- **Task**: Run OWASP ZAP baseline scan against QA endpoint before prod promotion
- **Dependencies**: P12-1 (service running in QA)
- **Validation**: ZAP scan passes with no critical/high findings

### P12-3: Promote to Production
- **Repo**: `konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-iqportal`
- **Task**:
  1. Verify ZAP scan passed (P12-2)
  2. Create `prod-iqportal` namespace
  3. Run Terraform for prod environment
  4. Update `helm/values-prod.yaml` with image tag
  5. Create PR with approval requirement
  6. After merge, manual sync during change window (Tue-Thu 20:00-23:00 UTC)
- **Dependencies**: P12-2
- **Validation**: Service running and healthy in `prod-iqportal` namespace

## ROLLBACK PLAN (Available at any point)

Three rollback options documented in the migration guide:

1. **Git revert** (recommended): `git revert HEAD && git push` in workload repo; ArgoCD auto-syncs
2. **kubectl rollback** (emergency): `kubectl rollout undo deployment/kix-app-iqportal -n dev-iqportal`
3. **Fall back to Cloud Run**: `gcloud run services update kon-iq-portal --max-instances=10`

Auth Proxy or private IP\n\n### Phase 9: Ingress and Networking (5 issues)\n\n58. **Configure Kong route for IQ Portal** — Kong Ingress Controller route: `iqportal.app.ix.konecta-digital.com` → IQ Portal service\n59. **Configure TLS certificate (Google-managed or cert-manager)** — Ensure HTTPS termination with valid certificate\n60. **Configure CORS and security headers** — Kong plugins for by Cloud Logging\n64. **Create Cloud Monitoring dashboards** — GKE pod metrics, request latency, error rates, resource utilization\n65. **Configure alerting policies** — Alerts for: pod restarts > threshold, error rate > 5%, latency P99 > SLO\n66. **Add Prometheus metrics endpoint** — `/metrics` endpoint for custom application metrics\n67. **Configure distributed tracing (Cloud Trace)** — OpenTelemetry instrumentation for request tracing\n68. **Create SLO definitions** — Define availability and latency SLOs for IQ Portal\n\n### Phase 11: Verification and Smoke Tests (13 issues)\n\n69. **Verify pod starts and passes health checks** — Pod Running, liveness/readiness probes passing\n70. **Verify Workload Identity authentication** — Pod can authenticate to GCP services without service account keys\n71. **Verify secrets are mounted correctly** — ExternalSecret sync status healthy, secrets available as env vars\n72. **Verify database connectivity** — Application can query the down\n75. **Verify PDB prevents full outage during rollout** — Rolling update respects PDB, zero-downtime deployment\n76. **Verify logging pipeline** — Application logs appear in Cloud Logging with correct labels\n77. **Verify monitoring dashboards populate** — Metrics visible in Cloud Monitoring dashboards\n78. **Verify alerting fires correctly** — Trigger test alert, verify notification environment** — Deploy to QA, run smoke tests, verify functionality matches dev\n83. **Promote to prod environment** — Deploy to prod with manual approval, run production smoke tests\n84. **Verify production traffic routing** — Confirm production DNS and traffic flow correctly\n\n### Phase 13: DNS and Domain Cutover (3 issues)\n\n85. **Plan DNS cutover from Cloud Run to GKE** — Document cutover ## Approved Plan:
# Plan: Create IQ Portal Migration Backlog as GitHub Issues

## Context

The KIX platform documentation defines a comprehensive migration path for moving services from Cloud Run to GKE. The IQ Portal is the first service to migrate. This plan creates a full backlog of GitHub Issues covering the end-to-end migration, to be added to the GitHub Project at `https://github.com/orgs/konecta-ix-workloads/projects/1/views/1`.

The task breakdown is derived from the app-migration documentation (14 docs covering target architecture, Helm charts, CI/CD, GitOps, networking, security, observability, and operations).

## Approach

1. **Check project access** — Verify `gh` CLI can access the `konecta-ix-workloads` org and project
2. **Determine target repo** — Create issues in an appropriate repo (likely `konecta-ix-workloads/kix-workload-iqportal` or a planning repo)
3. **Create labels** — Phase labels (`phase:0-prerequisites` through `phase:14-decommission`) plus `migration` and `iq-portal`
4. **Create 92 issues** — Using `gh issue create` with title, body (acceptance criteria, dependencies), and labels
5. **Add to project** — Use `gh project item-add` to add each issue to project board

## Architecture

Two layers, two toolchains:

| Layer | Tool | Repo | What it provisions |
|-------|------|------|--------------------|
| **Infrastructure** | Terraform | `kix-workload-iqportal/terraform/` | GCP resources: service accounts, IAM, secrets, DNS, Cloud SQL access, Workload Identity, network policies |
| **Application** | Helm + ArgoCD | `kix-workload-iqportal/helm/` + `argocd/` | K8s resources: Deployment, Service, HPA, PDB, ExternalSecrets, ServiceAccount, Ingress |

Terraform runs first to provision all GCP infrastructure. Then Helm deploys the application into the namespaces and service accounts that Terraform created.

Each issue will include:
- **Description**: What needs to be done and which tool (Terraform or Helm)
- **Acceptance Criteria**: Checklist of deliverables
- **Dependencies**: Which issues must be completed first (by phase)
- **Reference**: Link to relevant app-migration documentation page

## Notes

- **Phase 0** = Terraform provisions all GCP infrastructure (namespaces, IAM, secrets, networking, DNS)
- **Phase 1** = Repository setup including Helm chart scaffolding
- **Phases 2-4** = Application code, Docker image, and Helm chart configuration
- **Phase 5+** = CI/CD, GitOps, verification, promotion, cutover, decommission
- Labels `terraform` and `helm` indicate which toolchain owns each issue
- Dependencies between phases are sequential (Phase N depends on Phase N-1)

```
